paper.title: Blind Men and the Elephant: Probing the Epistemic Myopia of LLMs under Long-Tail Divergent Knowledge
paper.abstract: Factual question answering (QA) typically assumes a single canonical answer, obscuring whether large language models (LLMs) retain divergent accounts of long-tail facts. To address this gap, we introduce ElephantBench, a closed-book knowledge probe comprising 1,094 questions generated through an auditable graph-based pipeline. The pipeline retrieves related documents from a low-exposure web corpus, identifies naturally occurring disagreements, and converts them into multi-account QA records. Eac

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要测的不是“模型知不知道一个事实”，而是“模型对低曝光、且存在多种已验证说法的事实，能否在闭卷条件下把不同 account 都从参数记忆里找回来”。传统 factual QA 默认只有一个标准答案，长尾知识 benchmark 也大多只看单一 recall；而知识冲突类 benchmark 往往把冲突证据在推理时直接给模型，测的是 open-book reasoning，不是 parametric memory。ElephantBench 把这两件事拆开：先问模型是否记得这个低曝光事实，再问它记得是否完整，是否只保留了更常见的一种说法而漏掉另一种说法。作者把这种偏向单一 account 的记忆缺失称为 epistemic myopia。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的意义主要有三层。第一，它把“知识记忆完整性”从普通准确率里单独拎出来，给了一个更细的诊断维度。对于做数据配比、数据清洗、长尾覆盖和 continual pretrain 的人，这比单纯看 QA accuracy 更接近训练语料分布的真实后果。第二，它提出了一个可审计的构造流程：从低质量过滤后被丢弃的语料 D_low 中挖长尾事实，再找天然存在的跨文档分歧，最后转成闭卷 probe。这个思路对预训练数据研究很有启发，因为它不是再去堆热门网页，而是反过来检查过滤器和采样策略是否系统性抹掉了稀有但真实的知识。第三，论文给出一个很具体的经验结论：主流 account 的曝光更影响“能不能记住这个事实”，少数 account 的曝光更影响“记忆是否完整”。这直接把 corpus exposure asymmetry 和模型的记忆缺口连了起来，能反过来指导数据保留、重采样和去重策略。
summary.technical_approach:
方法核心是一个两阶段、图结构驱动的 benchmark 构造流程。起点不是全网高质量语料，而是先用质量分类器 Q（文中举例 DCLM fastText）把语料分成 D_high 和 D_low，然后专门在 D_low 里找候选事实。这样做的理由很明确：标准 quality filtering 往往会把低曝光、低频但可能真实的长尾知识一起滤掉，而这些内容更适合做参数记忆压力测试。

接着作者把 D_low 表示成文档图。节点是文档；support edge 表示两篇文档在讲同一个具体事实；conflict edge 表示它们针对同一 subject-attribute pair 给出了不兼容的 account。为了避免 O(n^2) 的全对比较，作者先让 LLM 给每篇文档打 knowledge-point label，按知识点聚类，只在簇内做候选配对；再结合实体抽取进一步缩小候选空间。之后再用 LLM 去判定 support / conflict 关系。这里的关键不是单次 LLM judge，而是把 LLM 放在离线图构造环节，用来做候选验证和结构化抽取，而不是直接拿它生成 benchmark 后就结束。

有了 verified conflict edge 之后，作者从冲突子图里采样，合成 QA：一个问题 q 对应一个答案集合 A={v1,...,vk}，其中 k≥2，每个答案都必须能追溯到源文档，并且还要经过外部公开权威来源验证与人工复核。这样得到的不是“模型在给定证据下如何整合冲突”，而是“不给证据时，模型参数里到底保留了哪些 account”。

评测指标也做了拆分。论文不是只算一个 accuracy，而是区分 fact recall 与 account completeness：前者看模型是否至少记住了这个低曝光事实的一种说法，后者看它是否把所有已验证 account 都说出来。这个拆分很重要，因为很多模型并不是完全不知道，而是只记住了曝光更高的一边。论文后面还把每个 account 在语料中的支持文档数作为 exposure proxy，分析不同侧的文档频次与 recall / completeness 的关系。这一点让 benchmark 不只是排名工具，而能回到训练数据分布本身。
summary.experiments:
基准规模是 1,094 个闭卷问题，来自低曝光网页语料中的自然分歧案例。每个样本都经过源文档追溯、外部验证和人工审核。作者评测了 32 个模型。最强模型也只能在 52.4% 的问题上同时找回两个 account；而在几乎所有剩余失败样本里，模型并不是完全答不出，而是能答出其中一个 account，却漏掉另一个。这说明主要失败模式不是“事实完全遗忘”，而是“记忆不完整”。

论文最有信息量的实验不是单纯模型排名，而是 exposure asymmetry 分析。作者统计冲突两侧各自被多少文档支持，用支持文档数近似训练曝光度。结果显示：更常见 account 的曝光与 fact recall 更相关，也就是它决定模型是否能把这个事实想起来；较少见 account 的曝光则更影响 completeness，也就是模型能否把另一种已验证说法也保留下来。这个结果和预训练里常见的频次偏置一致，但这里给出了更细粒度的闭卷证据。

从摘要和正文可见，作者还强调 benchmark construction 的效率：通过 knowledge-point clustering 和 entity-based retrieval，把原本需要大规模 pairwise LLM judging 的图构造成本显著压低。虽然当前给出的片段里没有完整的成本数字，但方法设计上已经说明其目标是把任意低曝光语料转成可复用的 memory probe，而不是一次性手工整理数据集。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读时先看 Introduction，抓住它和两类已有 benchmark 的区别：长尾 QA 只测单一答案 recall，冲突 benchmark 多是 open-book；ElephantBench 测的是 closed-book parametric memory completeness。然后重点看 Figure 2 和 Tracing the Elephant 这一节，理解 D_low、document graph、support/conflict edge、以及 QA 合成链路。这里是整篇工作的骨架。

第二个值得看的是指标定义和 exposure 分析部分。阅读时要特别留意作者如何把“记得一个答案”和“记得全部答案”分开，以及支持文档数是如何被当作 exposure proxy 使用的。这个部分决定了 benchmark 是否能反映训练语料分布，而不只是做一个更难的 QA 集。

如果时间有限，优先看：1）任务定义与 benchmark positioning；2）图构造流程图和样例；3）主结果表，尤其是 strongest model 只有 52.4% complete recall 这一点；4）exposure asymmetry 的图表。预计 25–35 分钟能抓住主要贡献。若要深挖，建议进一步检查人工审核协议、外部验证标准，以及 conflict edge 的 precision 控制方式，因为这些决定 benchmark 噪声水平。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper asks a narrower and more useful question than standard factual QA: when a long-tail fact has multiple verified accounts in the wild, can an LLM recover all of them from parametric memory in a closed-book setting? Existing long-tail QA benchmarks mostly assume a single canonical answer, so they only test whether a model recalls a rare fact at all. Existing conflict benchmarks usually provide conflicting passages at inference time, so they test evidence integration rather than stored knowledge. ElephantBench is built to isolate memory completeness: does the model remember the fact, and if yes, does it retain the full set of verified accounts or only the dominant one?
summary_en.importance: This matters for pretraining because it exposes a failure mode that ordinary accuracy hides. A model can look competent on factual QA while systematically collapsing minority accounts into a single dominant answer. That is directly relevant to data filtering, mixture design, long-tail coverage, deduplication, and continual pretraining. The second contribution is methodological: the benchmark is constructed from the filtered remainder of a web corpus, D_low, rather than from the high-quality slice that most pipelines keep. That inversion is useful for data research because it turns quality filtering itself into an object of study. The third contribution is the corpus-level finding: exposure to the more prevalent account is associated with recalling the fact at all, while exposure to the less prevalent account is more associated with recalling the full set of accounts. That links a measurable corpus property to a concrete memory failure mode.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The benchmark construction pipeline is graph-based and deliberately audit-friendly. The corpus is first partitioned by a quality classifier into D_high and D_low. Instead of mining the retained high-quality pool, the authors search D_low for low-exposure facts that are more likely to reveal parametric memory limits. Documents in D_low become nodes in a graph. Support edges connect documents about the same specific fact, while conflict edges connect documents that give incompatible accounts for the same subject-attribute pair.

A naive all-pairs comparison would be quadratic, so the paper uses a two-stage narrowing strategy. First, an LLM assigns each document a knowledge-point label, and candidate comparisons are restricted within those clusters. Second, entity-based retrieval further reduces the candidate set. Only then are LLM judgments used to verify support and conflict relations. This is an important design choice: the LLM is used offline to structure the corpus and identify disagreements, not to provide evidence at evaluation time.

Verified conflict edges seed subgraph sampling and QA synthesis. Each question is paired with an answer set containing at least two verified accounts, and every answer must remain traceable to source documents, externally checked against authoritative public sources, and reviewed by human annotators. The evaluation is closed-book: no retrieval, no source passages, no tools.

The metric design is also central. The paper separates fact recall from account completeness. A model may recover one account and therefore show some memory of the fact, yet still fail the completeness criterion by omitting the alternative verified account. The authors then use the number of supporting documents on each side of a disagreement as an exposure proxy, which allows them to analyze how corpus prevalence relates to these two failure modes.
summary_en.experiments:
ElephantBench contains 1,094 closed-book questions mined from naturally occurring disagreements in a low-exposure web corpus. Each item is source-traceable, externally verified, and human-reviewed. The evaluation covers 32 models. The headline result is that even the strongest model recovers both accounts on only 52.4% of questions. On nearly all of the remaining cases, the model does not fail by total ignorance; instead, it recalls one verified account while omitting the other. That makes incompleteness, not pure forgetting, the dominant error mode.

The most informative analysis is the exposure asymmetry study. By counting how many documents support each side of a disagreement, the paper approximates relative corpus exposure. The more prevalent account is more predictive of whether the model recalls the fact at all. The less prevalent account is more predictive of whether the model recalls the full set of verified accounts. This is a clean empirical link between corpus imbalance and partial memory retention.

The paper also argues for construction efficiency. Knowledge-point clustering and entity-based retrieval reduce the need for exhaustive pairwise LLM judging. The excerpt provided here does not include the full cost table, but the design goal is clear: make the pipeline reusable for turning any low-exposure corpus into a memory probe rather than building a one-off benchmark by manual curation.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Start with the introduction and benchmark positioning. The key is to see why this is neither a standard long-tail QA benchmark nor a standard conflict-reasoning benchmark. Then read the pipeline section around Figure 2 carefully. D_low, the document graph, support versus conflict edges, and the QA synthesis process are the structural core of the work.

After that, focus on the metric definitions and the exposure analysis. The paper becomes much more interesting once you see that it is not just making QA harder; it is separating recall from completeness and tying both to corpus prevalence. That is the part most relevant to pretraining data decisions.

If reading time is limited, prioritize: the task definition, the graph construction figure, the main results table with the 52.4% complete-recall ceiling, and the plots analyzing support-document asymmetry. Around 25 to 35 minutes should be enough for a solid skim. For a deeper read, inspect the human review protocol, external verification criteria, and how conflict-edge precision is controlled, because benchmark noise will matter a lot for interpreting the memory-completeness claim.

recommendation.zh: 这篇会直接提醒你：闭卷知识不是“记住没记住”，而是“记住了几个版本”；做数据配比和知识保真时应把 exposure imbalance 当一等公民。
recommendation.en: This should update your prior that closed-book knowledge is binary recall; the real issue is how many accounts survive pretraining, so exposure imbalance deserves first-class treatment in data work.

paper.title: LoopArena: Benchmarking Models as Runtime Controllers for Loop Engineering
paper.abstract: Loop Engineering is emerging as a practice for organizing development work around coding agents. Instead of writing each prompt by hand, practitioners design loops that monitor progress, assign work, run checks, and decide what the agent should do next. Even with a capable coding agent, a loop may trust a stale progress note, skip needed verification, spend its budget in the wrong direction, or stop before the task is safe to submit. Yet the final outcome of one end-to-end run cannot tell whethe

summary.core_problem: 长程软件工程任务里，“写代码的 agent”之外还需要运行时控制器（loop/controller）做预算分配、验证与停机决策；端到端成败无法区分是 controller 还是 worker 的问题。
summary.importance: 核心贡献是评测资产：把“模型作为运行时控制器”单独拉出来评估，能更干净地测 agentic loop 的决策质量，对 coding-agent/agent 评测与训练信号设计有直接价值。
summary.technical_approach: LoopArena：固定一个 Worker（编码 agent），被测模型作为 Controller；每轮 Controller 只看结构化运行摘要（progress/检查结果/状态等）并决定下一步指令或是否停止，从而把“控制策略”与“执行能力”解耦评测。
summary.experiments: 摘要未给出具体任务数量、worker 选择、对比 controller baseline（规则/LLM）与指标（成功率/成本/回合数/安全提交率等）的细节；但评测设定本身清晰可复用。

summary_en.core_problem: In long-running software engineering, a runtime loop/controller must allocate budget, enforce verification, and decide when to stop; end-to-end outcomes conflate controller quality with the coding agent’s execution ability.
summary_en.importance: Primary contribution is an evaluation asset: it isolates and benchmarks models as runtime controllers, enabling cleaner measurement of loop decision quality—useful for training/evaluating agentic control policies.
summary_en.technical_approach: LoopArena fixes a Worker coding agent and evaluates a Controller model that only sees structured run summaries after each round, then issues next-step instructions or stop decisions, decoupling control from execution.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract omits concrete task counts, worker choice, controller baselines, and metrics (success/cost/rounds/safe-to-submit); the benchmark framing is the main value.

recommendation.zh: 把“controller 决策质量”从“coding agent 能力”里剥离出来这点很干净；只读任务/指标定义与 controller 输入输出协议，够你复刻内部评测。
recommendation.en: The clean decoupling of controller policy from worker capability is the key; read the task/metric definitions and the controller I/O protocol—enough to replicate an internal eval.

paper.title: The Illusion of $\textit{What If}$: Evaluating the Breakdown of Counterfactual Reasoning in LLMs
paper.abstract: Counterfactual reasoning requires models to reason beyond the observed world and explain how altered conditions propagate through downstream consequences. Existing benchmarks largely target bounded settings with fixed variables or single gold outcomes, overlooking open-domain scenarios requiring causal-process evaluation. To this end, we present $\textbf{WhatIfBench}$, a diagnostic benchmark for open-domain, open-form, long-horizon counterfactual causal reasoning, containing 220 what-if question

summary.core_problem: 评估 LLM 在开放域、长视野的反事实因果推理（Counterfactual Reasoning）任务上的表现，解决现有基准局限于固定变量或单一标准答案的问题。
summary.importance: 提出了一个诊断性基准 WhatIfBench 和一个基于因果图的评估框架 PRISM，揭示了前沿 LLM 在复杂反事实推理中的严重缺陷（The Illusion of What If）。
summary.technical_approach: 构建 WhatIfBench，包含 220 个跨学科的 what-if 问题。提出 PRISM 评估框架：首先将自然语言解释转化为包含事件、状态和机制的响应衍生语义因果图（RSCG）；然后联合应用过程指标（评估图级因果有效性）和 Rubric 指标（评估答案级解释充分性）。
summary.experiments: 使用该框架评估了六个前沿 LLM，发现它们在 WhatIfBench 上的表现仍然不佳，存在反事实推理崩溃的现象。
summary.authors_note: 来自浙江大学、香港城市大学等机构。

summary_en.core_problem: Evaluating LLMs on open-domain, long-horizon counterfactual causal reasoning, addressing the limitation of existing benchmarks that focus on fixed variables or single gold outcomes.
summary_en.importance: Introduces a diagnostic benchmark (WhatIfBench) and a causal graph-based evaluation framework (PRISM), revealing severe breakdowns in complex counterfactual reasoning among frontier LLMs.
summary_en.technical_approach: Constructs WhatIfBench with 220 cross-disciplinary what-if questions. Proposes the PRISM evaluation framework: it first converts natural language explanations into a Response-Derived Semantic Causal Graph (RSCG) of events, states, and mechanisms; then jointly applies a Process Metric (for graph-level causal validity) and a Rubric Metric (for answer-level explanatory adequacy).
summary_en.experiments: Evaluated six frontier LLMs using this framework, finding that they still struggle significantly on WhatIfBench, exhibiting breakdowns in counterfactual reasoning.
summary_en.authors_note: From Zhejiang University, City University of Hong Kong, etc.

recommendation.zh: 提出了一个评估长视野反事实推理的新 Benchmark 和基于因果图的评估方法，揭示了当前 LLM 在因果链条推导上的缺陷，对理解模型推理瓶颈有参考价值。
recommendation.en: Proposes a new benchmark and causal graph-based evaluation for long-horizon counterfactual reasoning, highlighting current LLM deficits in causal chain deduction.

paper.title: LongPIBench: A Long-Context Benchmark for Prompt Injection
paper.abstract: Prompt injection attacks pose a serious security risk to large language models in real-world applications. However, existing prompt injection benchmarks primarily focus on short-context inputs, leaving the attacks and defenses in long-context settings largely unexplored. This gap leads to a substantial overestimation of the effectiveness of current defenses. In this paper, we bridge the gap by introducing LongPIBench, a long-context benchmark for prompt injection covering 4 realistic application

summary.core_problem: 现有的提示注入（Prompt Injection）基准测试主要集中在短上下文，如何评估长上下文场景下的提示注入攻击和防御有效性？
summary.importance: 提出了首个针对长上下文提示注入的基准测试 LongPIBench，填补了该领域的空白，并揭示了现有防御机制在长上下文下的严重脆弱性。
summary.technical_approach: 构建了涵盖论文同行评审、简历筛选、代码审查和电子邮件摘要 4 个真实应用场景的数据集（包含合成和真实数据），上下文长度从数千到数万 token 不等。
summary.experiments: 评估结果表明，在长上下文设置下，即使是简单的启发式提示注入攻击也能实现高成功率，并频繁绕过最先进的防御机制。
summary.authors_note: 来自 Duke University 的研究团队，关注 LLM 安全性。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing prompt injection benchmarks focus on short contexts; how to evaluate the effectiveness of prompt injection attacks and defenses in long-context scenarios?
summary_en.importance: Introduces LongPIBench, the first benchmark for long-context prompt injection, filling a gap in the field and revealing the severe vulnerability of existing defenses in long-context settings.
summary_en.technical_approach: Constructs datasets (synthetic and real-world) covering 4 realistic scenarios: paper peer review, resume screening, code review, and email summary, with context lengths ranging from thousands to tens of thousands of tokens.
summary_en.experiments: Evaluation results show that in long-context settings, even simple heuristic prompt injection attacks achieve high success rates and frequently bypass state-of-the-art defenses.
summary_en.authors_note: Research team from Duke University, focusing on LLM security.

recommendation.zh: 揭示了长上下文模型在安全防御上的盲区，对于关注长文本能力和安全对齐的后训练研究员有参考价值，可快速浏览其攻击构造方式。
recommendation.en: Reveals blind spots in security defenses for long-context models, valuable for post-training researchers focusing on long-context capabilities and safety alignment; quickly skim their attack construction methods.

paper.title: XHotpotQA: A Benchmark for Cross-Lingual Knowledge Composition in Multi-Hop Question Answering
paper.abstract: Knowledge-intensive multi-hop question answering requires systems to select evidence and compose dependent facts, yet multilingual benchmarks usually translate an entire example into one language. This hides failures at language boundaries inside the reasoning chain. We introduce XHotpotQA, a controlled benchmark for cross-lingual knowledge composition over mixed-language evidence. Each instance is modeled as an evidence-dependency graph whose question, bridge evidence, answer-bearing evidence,

summary.core_problem: 评测多语言多跳问答里，模型在跨语言证据链上的知识组合能力，而不是单语翻译后的伪多语能力。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是 benchmark。它把问题、桥接证据、答案证据和干扰项的语言分配显式化，专门暴露 reasoning chain 在语言边界处的失败模式；这对多语预训练和跨语检索-推理接口有一定诊断价值。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 XHotpotQA，将每个样本建模为 evidence-dependency graph，并对 question、bridge evidence、answer-bearing evidence、distractors 指定语言；数据集提供句级支持监督和 distractors，强调控制式构造而非简单整题翻译。
summary.experiments: 数据包含 15,661 个训练样本和 7,405 个验证样本。验证集中 99.81% 的样本跨越 question-to-gold-evidence 语言接口，95.60% 的 gold paragraph 分属不同语言。作者在三个 reader artifact 上观察到：当问题与证据完全语言不匹配时，Unicode-aware answer F1 比部分对齐低 10.25 到 15.79。

summary_en.core_problem: It evaluates whether models can compose knowledge across language boundaries in multi-hop QA, rather than succeeding on fully translated pseudo-multilingual examples.
summary_en.importance: This is a benchmark contribution. By explicitly assigning languages to the question, bridge evidence, answer-bearing evidence, and distractors, it exposes failures at language boundaries in reasoning chains. That gives it some diagnostic value for multilingual pretraining and cross-lingual retrieval-reasoning interfaces.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper introduces XHotpotQA, modeling each instance as an evidence-dependency graph with explicit language assignments for the question, bridge evidence, answer-bearing evidence, and distractors. It provides sentence-level support supervision and supplied distractors, emphasizing controlled construction over whole-example translation.
summary_en.experiments: The dataset contains 15,661 training and 7,405 validation instances. In validation, 99.81% of examples cross the question-to-gold-evidence language interface, and 95.60% use gold paragraphs in different languages. Across three reader artifacts, full question-evidence language mismatch reduces Unicode-aware answer F1 by 10.25 to 15.79 compared with partial alignment.

recommendation.zh: 不是预训练论文，但 benchmark 设计是干净的；只看数据构造和语言错配降幅那张表，就够判断你家多语模型短板在哪。
recommendation.en: Not a pretraining paper, but the benchmark design is clean; read the construction details and the mismatch-drop table to see where your multilingual model actually breaks.

paper.title: PersonaForge: Realistic Multi-Turn User Simulation for Agentic Systems
paper.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as agentic workflow executors, yet existing training data and benchmarks largely assume informationally complete, single-turn queries. Our analysis of 16K real-world sessions shows that 75.9% of interactions are multi-turn, revealing a substantial gap between how users interact with agents and how such systems are trained and evaluated. We introduce \textbf{PersonaForge}, a user simulation framework for synthesizing realistic multi-turn user--agent int

summary.core_problem: 现有 agent 训练与评测大多假设单轮、信息完备用户输入，无法覆盖真实多轮交互中的用户行为分布。
summary.importance: 这篇工作的主要价值是评测与数据资产：用真实会话统计驱动用户模拟，构造多轮 agent 训练集和 benchmark。对 pretrain 本身帮助有限，但对 post-train agent 数据分布设计有现实意义。
summary.technical_approach: 作者先分析 16K 真实会话，发现 75.9% 交互是多轮；随后提出 PersonaForge 用户模拟框架，包含四维 persona 空间、SOUL 行为控制，以及基于真实种子查询的 Reverse Deep Construction。基于该框架构建 6.3K 训练数据和 PersonaForge-Bench，覆盖 20 多个专业领域，并采用四维评分。
summary.experiments: 在 Qwen3.5-27B 上，PersonaForge 训练带来复合分数约 +4 的提升。实验重点是多轮 agent 训练和评测，而不是基座模型预训练。摘要没有给出更大规模模型、跨家族泛化或更严格的 ablation 细节，因此更适合作为 agent eval/data 资产参考。
summary.authors_note: Peking University、Xiaomi 等；Lei Li、Lingpeng Kong 属于较知名研究者。

summary_en.core_problem: Current agent training and evaluation mostly assume single-turn, information-complete user queries, missing the distribution of real multi-turn interactions.
summary_en.importance: The main contribution is an evaluation and data asset: a user simulator grounded in real session statistics, plus a multi-turn training set and benchmark. It is only indirectly relevant to pretraining, but useful for post-training data design for agents.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper analyzes 16K real-world sessions and finds that 75.9% are multi-turn. It then introduces PersonaForge, a user simulation framework with a four-dimensional persona space, SOUL-based behavioral control, and Reverse Deep Construction seeded from authentic queries. This is used to build a 6.3K training set and PersonaForge-Bench with 138 manually annotated tasks across 20+ professional domains and four-dimensional scoring.
summary_en.experiments: On Qwen3.5-27B, training with PersonaForge improves the composite score by about +4. The focus is multi-turn agent training/evaluation rather than foundation-model pretraining. The abstract does not show broader cross-model generalization or especially deep ablations, so this is best treated as an agent eval/data reference.
summary_en.authors_note: Peking University, Xiaomi, and collaborators; Lei Li and Lingpeng Kong are recognizable researchers.

recommendation.zh: 如果你关心 post-train agent 数据分布，这篇可看真实会话统计和 benchmark 设计；对 pretrain 几乎没有直接动作，不必细读方法细节。
recommendation.en: If you care about post-training data distributions for agents, read the real-session statistics and benchmark design; it has little direct consequence for pretraining, so skip the method details.

paper.title: SkillSafetyBench: Evaluating Agent Safety under Skill-Facing Attack Surfaces
paper.abstract: Reusable skills are becoming a common interface for extending large language model agents, packaging procedural guidance with access to files, tools, memory, and execution environments. However, this modularity introduces attack surfaces that are largely missed by existing safety evaluations: even when the user request is benign, unsafe influence may reside in skill guidance, local artifacts, or execution-environment files that steer the agent toward unsafe actions. We present SkillSafetyBench,

summary.core_problem: 评估 LLM agent 在“技能包”接口下的安全失效：用户请求本身无害，但技能说明、本地文件或执行环境可诱导 agent 做出危险行为。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是 agent safety benchmark。它把安全评测从用户 prompt 扩展到技能、文件、工具和执行环境这些非用户输入面，补上了现有 agent 评测中容易漏掉的一类攻击面。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 SkillSafetyBench，一个可运行的评测集，包含 155 个对抗案例、47 个任务、6 个风险域和 30 个安全类别。每个案例配有特定规则验证器，用来判断 agent 是否执行了不安全行为。方法重点不是训练模型，而是构造技能侧攻击和可复现实验环境。
summary.experiments: 在多个 CLI agent 和不同模型后端上评测。结果显示，非用户来源的攻击可以稳定诱导不安全行为，并且不同风险域、攻击方式、agent scaffold 与模型组合呈现不同失败模式。摘要未给出具体模型清单和完整数值表。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper evaluates safety failures in LLM agents when reusable skills, local artifacts, or execution-environment files carry unsafe instructions despite a benign user request.
summary_en.importance: Its contribution is an agent-safety benchmark. It moves the threat model beyond user-prompt attacks and tests skill-facing surfaces that are increasingly common in tool-using agent systems.
summary_en.technical_approach: SkillSafetyBench is a runnable benchmark with 155 adversarial cases over 47 tasks, 6 risk domains, and 30 safety categories. Each case uses a case-specific rule-based verifier to check whether the agent took an unsafe action. The work is mainly an evaluation asset rather than a training method.
summary_en.experiments: The benchmark is run on multiple CLI agents and model backends. The reported finding is that non-user attacks can consistently induce unsafe behavior, with different failure patterns across domains, attack methods, and scaffold-model pairings. The abstract does not expose the full model list or detailed tables.

recommendation.zh: 预训练侧不用细读；做 agent 后训练或安全数据设计时，看攻击面 taxonomy 和 verifier 设计即可。
recommendation.en: Not a pretraining read; if you build agent post-training or safety data, inspect the attack taxonomy and verifier design.

paper.title: CNeo-Bench: Diagnosing Large Language Models on Chinese Neologisms
paper.abstract: Chinese neologisms exploit diverse and unique linguistic mechanisms, such as phonetic substitution (e.g., 886 for ``bye-bye'') and visual character decomposition that are rare in other languages. We introduce CNeo-Bench, a benchmark of 4,759 such neologisms with reference definitions, organized into five top-level categories and nine subcategories by the linguistic mechanism behind each expression. CNeo-Bench is paired with a two-tier evaluation framework that separates whether a model can descr

summary.core_problem: 评测 LLM 是否理解中文新词的构词机制，而不只是能生成近似释义。
summary.importance: 贡献是中文新词 benchmark 和分层评测协议。它对 tokenizer、中文预训练语料覆盖、字符级/音形义表示有间接参考价值，但还不是预训练方法论文。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 CNeo-Bench，收集 4,759 个中文新词及参考定义，并按语言机制划分为 5 个一级类别和 9 个子类别。评测分两层：一层看模型能否解释新词含义，另一层看模型能否操作其底层机制，例如源形式还原。
summary.experiments: 评测 18 个 LLM。多数模型在 definition generation 上低于 40%。若干子类出现 recognition-manipulation gap：模型能描述新词含义，却在 source-form restoration 中用语义等价表达替代原始形式。另有 1,05 开头规模的 few-shot 分析，但摘要被截断，无法确认完整样本量和结论。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自 The University of Tokyo、小红书和 Tsinghua University。Yoshimasa Tsuruoka 是长期从事 NLP 与机器学习研究的学者。

summary_en.core_problem: The benchmark evaluates whether LLMs understand the formation mechanisms of Chinese neologisms, rather than merely producing approximate definitions.
summary_en.importance: The main contribution is a Chinese neologism benchmark with a two-tier evaluation protocol. It is indirectly useful for tokenizer design, Chinese pretraining coverage, and character/phonetic/visual representation analysis, but it is not a pretraining-method paper.
summary_en.technical_approach: CNeo-Bench contains 4,759 Chinese neologisms with reference definitions, organized into five top-level mechanism categories and nine subcategories. The evaluation separates definition generation from mechanism-level operations such as restoring the source form.
summary_en.experiments: The paper evaluates 18 LLMs. Most models score below 40% on definition generation. Several subcategories show a recognition-manipulation gap: models can describe a neologism but replace the required source form with a semantic paraphrase in restoration tasks. The abstract mentions a few-shot analysis over a 1,05*-sized subset, but the full number and details are truncated.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors are from The University of Tokyo, Xiaohongshu Inc., and Tsinghua University. Yoshimasa Tsuruoka is a well-known NLP and machine learning researcher.

recommendation.zh: 读任务设计即可；它暴露的是中文 tokenizer/语料覆盖的盲区，不是模型推理能力本身。
recommendation.en: Read the task design only; it exposes Chinese tokenizer and corpus-coverage blind spots more than general reasoning failure.

paper.title: Evaluating Language Models in Realistic Conversational Contexts
paper.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed to serve open-ended, multi-turn interactions, evaluating conversational quality at human scale has become a central challenge. Existing evaluation frameworks built for summarization, translation, or short-form QA tasks fall short of adequately measuring the consistency of human-scale dialogue, especially when derivation and validation of these metrics themselves often rely on synthetic rather than human sources. We fill the gap by introdu

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解决的不是“模型会不会聊天”，而是“怎么把长对话评测做得可信”。现有对话评测大多沿用摘要、翻译、短问答里的指标，偏向词面重合、事实正确或单轮偏好判断，难以覆盖多轮对话里更关键的性质：语气是否稳定、角色是否一致、上下文是否延续、回答是否自然推进任务。作者指出，很多近年的对话评测又依赖 LLM-as-a-judge 或合成数据，这会把评测误差、分布偏差和数据泄漏问题一起带进来。UPHELD 的核心目标，是构造一个以真实长对话为中心、带密集人工标注、能专门检验 conversational coherence 的评测基座。
summary.importance: 对基座模型研究的意义主要在评测层，而不是方法层。它补的是一个长期缺口：预训练和后训练都在追求更长、更自然、更稳定的交互，但公开评测往往仍停留在单轮问答、知识正确性或偏好胜率。UPHELD 把评测重心从“答对没有”转到“整段对话是否像一个稳定的人在交流”，这对研究训练目标、数据配比、对话式 continued pretraining、SFT 数据质量、以及 RL 后的风格漂移都更有针对性。量级上，它不是改变训练范式的论文，但作为评测资产是扎实的：专业编剧撰写的人类对话、3 万+ turns、15 万+ per-turn 人工标签，这种密度在公开对话评测里并不常见。
summary.technical_approach:
方法上分两部分。第一部分是数据构建。作者没有从论坛或客服日志里抓噪声对话，也没有让普通众包写模板化任务对话，而是请专业 script writers 生成完整 human-to-human 对话。任务是有目标但不强约束的，例如辅导、规划、日常说明，不要求唯一正确答案，也尽量避免重知识检索和复杂工具使用。这样做的原因很明确：如果任务过于知识密集，评测会重新退化成检索或事实核验；如果目标过于刚性，对话又会变成流程脚本。作者想保留“有用”与“自然”之间的张力。

第二部分是标注与指标分析。UPHELD 不是只给整段对话一个总分，而是做 dense per-turn annotation，围绕内容一致性、风格一致性、连贯性等维度给每一轮打标签。这样可以把长对话里的局部失稳暴露出来，而不是被整段平均分掩盖。作者随后系统比较了几类常见评测：传统 lexical / semantic metrics、单一 LLM judge，以及基于 UPHELD 训练的 mixture-of-judges。结论是，前两类在这种任务上相关性都不够高，尤其难抓住长程一致性；而简单的学习式集成指标能更好贴近人工判断。这里真正有意思的点，不是又提出了一个 judge，而是作者用高质量人工标注证明：对话评测不能只靠单一代理信号，尤其不能把合成数据上的 judge 表现直接外推到真实长对话。
summary.experiments: 从全文可见的关键结果主要有四类。第一，数据规模：UPHELD 包含数百段完整对话，超过 3 万个高质量 human-written turns，并提供 153,578 个密集的逐轮人工标签。作者强调，这个标注规模大约是同类 human-verified 对话评测的近 10 倍量级。第二，分布设计：对话长度更接近真实人类任务型交流，而不是为了“长”而长；作者给出对现有人类对话数据的统计，完整人类收集数据的平均长度约 9.3 turns，Topical-Chat 最大 21 turns，因此 UPHELD 让写作者自然结束对话，而不是人为拉长。第三，指标对比：传统 NLP 指标和单一 LLM-as-a-judge 在 UPHELD 上与人工判断的相关性较弱，尤其在风格一致、内容延续、整体自然度这些维度上不足；作者训练的 mixture-of-judges 在相关性上更高。摘要里没有给出完整数值表，但从正文描述看，提升是稳定且跨多类模型成立的。第四，误差分析：作者专门讨论了 synthetic dialogue 和 judge leakage 的问题，说明在分布外真实对话上，很多看似有效的自动指标会失真。
summary.reading_guide: 这篇适合泛读，不需要逐式推导。优先看 Introduction 和数据构建部分，先确认作者到底把“真实对话”定义成什么，以及为什么刻意避开知识密集任务。然后看标注 schema，重点关注每轮标什么、为什么按 turn 而不是只按 conversation 打分。接着看 metric analysis 和 human-correlation 结果，这部分决定了数据集是否真的有评测价值。若时间有限，抓三件事就够：一是 professional writers 带来的数据质量差异；二是对话长度和任务设定为何更贴近日常交互；三是单一 judge 为什么在这里不够用。预计 20 到 30 分钟可以读完主要内容。对做预训练的人，值得深挖的是：这些逐轮标签能否反过来做 reward modeling，或者作为 continued pretraining / dialogue annealing 的验证集。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper is about evaluation reliability, not dialogue generation itself. The core question is how to evaluate long, realistic conversations in a way that reflects what actually matters in deployment: coherence across turns, consistency of tone and persona, and the ability to sustain a useful interaction without collapsing into generic or contradictory behavior. Existing metrics inherited from MT, summarization, or short QA mostly capture lexical overlap or factuality. More recent dialogue benchmarks often rely on LLM judges or synthetic conversations, which introduces judge bias, leakage risk, and distribution mismatch. UPHELD is designed to provide a human-written, densely annotated benchmark centered on conversational quality rather than answer correctness.
summary_en.importance: Its value is mainly as an evaluation asset for foundation-model research. Pretraining and post-training increasingly target multi-turn assistants, but public evaluation still overweights single-turn correctness and pairwise preference wins. UPHELD shifts the target toward sustained conversational behavior. That makes it relevant for studying dialogue-oriented continued pretraining, SFT data quality, RL-induced style drift, and whether a model trained for helpfulness can remain stable over an extended exchange. This is not a training-method paper, but the dataset scale and annotation density are meaningful: professional-writer dialogues, 30k+ turns, and 153k+ turn-level human labels give it more signal than many existing dialogue benchmarks.
summary_en.technical_approach:
There are two main components. First is dataset construction. Instead of scraping noisy online conversations or using lightly controlled crowdworkers, the authors hire professional script writers to produce complete human-to-human dialogues. The tasks are goal-directed but open-ended, such as tutoring, planning, or everyday assistance. They intentionally avoid heavy knowledge retrieval, coding, or tasks with a single correct endpoint. That design choice matters: if the task is too knowledge-bound, the benchmark becomes another factual QA test; if it is too rigidly task-scripted, it stops measuring natural conversation.

Second is annotation and metric analysis. UPHELD provides dense turn-level labels rather than only conversation-level scores. The labels target dimensions such as stylistic consistency, content consistency, and coherence. This lets the benchmark expose local failures inside a long interaction instead of averaging them away. The paper then compares several evaluation families: classical lexical/semantic metrics, single LLM-as-a-judge systems, and a learned mixture-of-judges built using UPHELD supervision. The main takeaway is that standard metrics and single judges correlate poorly with human judgments on realistic dialogue, especially for long-range conversational properties, while a simple learned ensemble tracks humans better. The interesting contribution is less the ensemble itself and more the empirical demonstration that synthetic-data-based judge validation does not transfer cleanly to real human-scale conversations.
summary_en.experiments: The most important results are about dataset scale, distribution, and metric validity. UPHELD contains hundreds of complete dialogues, more than 30,000 human-written turns, and 153,578 dense turn-level human labels. The authors position this as roughly an order-of-magnitude increase over comparable human-verified dialogue evaluation resources. They also analyze dialogue length distributions and argue that realistic human task-oriented conversations are usually much shorter than many benchmark setups; they cite an average of about 9.3 turns in fully human-collected datasets, with Topical-Chat maxing out at 21 turns, and allow writers to stop naturally rather than forcing long transcripts. On evaluation, traditional NLP metrics and single LLM judges show weak correlation with human ratings on UPHELD, especially on style and content consistency, while the learned mixture-of-judges improves correlation. The excerpt does not expose the full numeric table, but the paper’s claim is that the gains are consistent across settings. The error analysis also emphasizes failures caused by synthetic dialogue bias and judge leakage.
summary_en.reading_guide: This is a skim paper. Start with the introduction and dataset design choices: what counts as a realistic conversation here, and why the benchmark avoids knowledge-heavy tasks. Then read the annotation schema carefully, because the turn-level labeling strategy is the main reason the benchmark is useful. After that, go to the metric comparison and human-correlation sections; that is where the paper earns its relevance. If time is limited, focus on three points: why professional writers matter, why natural dialogue length matters, and why a single LLM judge is not enough for this setting. Around 20 to 30 minutes should be enough for the main ideas. For pretraining researchers, the most interesting follow-up question is whether these turn-level labels can support reward modeling or serve as a validation set for dialogue-focused continued pretraining.

recommendation.zh: 如果你做对话后训练或 judge，这套数据值得收；若你做 pretrain，只需看 benchmark 设计和人类标注协议，不必细读全部指标表。
recommendation.en: Worth tracking if you work on dialogue post-training or judges; for pretraining, just read the benchmark design and annotation protocol rather than every metric table.

paper.title: MemToC: Benchmarking Memory-Tool Conflict Resolution in Large Language Models
paper.abstract: Tool-augmented LLMs must arbitrate between two fallible sources when a tool return conflicts with their parametric memory, yet existing evaluations measure source preference without establishing source correctness. We introduce MemToC, a controlled benchmark for post-tool-return arbitration with executable tools. MemToC comprises 6,504 evaluation episodes constructed from 542 quality-controlled factual questions, independently elicited model-specific closed-book answers, and controlled tool retu

summary.core_problem: 在工具调用场景里，当“工具返回”和“模型参数记忆（closed-book）”发生冲突时，如何构造一个可控评测，使得每个 episode 都能明确知道哪一方是对的，从而真正评估模型的冲突仲裁能力（而不是仅统计它更偏向工具还是更偏向记忆）。
summary.importance: 这是评测资产而非预训练方法论文，但对 post-train（SFT/DPO）与 agent 可靠性有直接价值：它把“工具是否正确”作为可控变量注入，解决了以往冲突评测里 correctness 不可知导致的指标混淆。对基座研究的启发点在于：当训练/对齐信号来自外部工具或检索时，必须把“来源正确性”显式建模，否则模型学到的可能只是固定偏好（永远信工具/永远不信工具），而不是条件化的仲裁策略。
summary.technical_approach:
MemToC 的关键设计是把冲突从“自然发生”改为“实验干预（intervention）”：
- 数据来源：ToolHop（多跳分解问题、可本地执行的 tool call、可验证中间答案）。作者取其中可独立查询的子问题，构造成短答案事实问答。
- 先固定 benchmark 工件：问题 q、可执行调用、verified gold answer g、以及至少一个同类型且可信的 distractor（用于构造错误返回）。两名标注者独立审核，做自包含性、答案泄露、distractor 合理性等质检。
- 对每个模型、每个 prompt 变体，先测 closed-book 回答 m，并据此判定“模型记忆是否正确”（m 是否等于 g）。
- 再在同一问题上提供被控制的工具返回 r，分四类：correct return、incorrect return（用经验证答案与人工校验的 distractor 注入）、error payload、no return。因为 r 是作者注入的，所以工具侧正确性在回答前已知。
- 这样每个 episode 的“正确行为”是可判定的：当工具对且记忆错，应跟随工具；当工具错且记忆对，应抵抗工具；再加上工具 error/no-tool 作为控制组。
- 评测细节：采用 extraction-first 的答案匹配；提供三种指令措辞变体但固定问题文本，以测提示敏感性。
- 缓解方法对比：prompting vs SFT vs DPO；并用 cross-fitting（按 ToolHop chain 划分/持出）保证每个报告的微调预测都在训练未见问题上得到，减少泄漏。
summary.experiments:
规模与设置：542 个质检后的事实问题；结合 4 种工具条件与 3 种指令措辞，形成 6,504 个固定评测 episodes；评测 5 个开源 7–9B 模型。
构建统计：从 ToolHop 3,912 子问题扁平化去重到 1,948；筛到 605 个可独立检索事实；质检后得到 575 池；最终 542。443/542 具备 far distractor。
结果层面：提供了 prompting、SFT、DPO 的对比，并强调该基准能分别度量“正确工具返回的利用”与“错误工具返回的抵抗”。（提供的全文片段未包含具体分数表，因此无法在此复述各模型在四象限上的数值差异。）
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议（30–45 分钟）：
- 先读 Introduction 里对“source preference ≠ arbitration”的动机与 Figure 1/2 的设定。
- 精看 Benchmark construction：问题筛选标准（可独立查询 vs 需要链式计算）、distractor 的 near/far 定义、以及两人质检流程与拒绝率来源。
- 看 Evaluation protocol：closed-book m 的获取方式、四种工具条件的注入、以及为什么要加 tool-error/no-tool 控制。
- 如果关心训练信号：读 Mitigation methods（SFT/DPO）与 cross-fitting 的划分方式，确认没有链级泄漏。

适合带着的问题：
- 指标是否区分“拒答/不确定”与“给出错误答案”？基准要求 closed-book 不可 abstain，但 tool 条件下是否允许。
- 错误返回的分布是否过于“同类型但容易识别为假”（例如罕见实体），从而高估抵抗能力。
- 该设置固定了 tool selection，只评估 post-tool-call 仲裁；若用于端到端 agent，还需要与 tool 选择错误耦合的评测。

summary_en.core_problem: How to evaluate tool–memory conflict resolution in LLM agents under controlled source correctness, so that each episode has a known “right arbitration decision” rather than merely measuring whether the model tends to follow tools or its parametric memory.
summary_en.importance: Primarily an evaluation contribution (not a pretraining method), but it matters for post-training and agent reliability: by intervening on tool returns, it disentangles source preference from correct arbitration. For foundation-model training, the key lesson is that when external tools/retrieval are used as supervision or inference-time evidence, correctness must be explicitly controlled/measured; otherwise models can be rewarded for a fixed bias (always trust tools / always distrust tools) instead of learning conditional arbitration.
summary_en.technical_approach:
MemToC is built as a controlled post-tool-call benchmark derived from ToolHop.
- Data pipeline: start from ToolHop sub-questions with locally executable tool calls and verified intermediate answers; keep only self-contained facts with short verifiable answers.
- Pre-construct benchmark artifacts before evaluating any model: question q, verified gold g, executable call, and curated distractors to synthesize plausible incorrect tool returns. Two annotators independently review for self-containedness, answer leakage, answer validity, and distractor plausibility.
- For each model and each prompt wording variant, first elicit a closed-book answer m (forced to answer, no abstention) and score it against g to determine whether the model’s memory is correct.
- Then present the same question with an injected tool return r under four conditions: correct return, incorrect return (built from verified answers and human-validated distractors), error payload, and no return. Because r is injected, tool correctness is known a priori.
- This yields a source-correctness matrix where the “correct behavior” is well-defined (use correct tools, resist incorrect tools), with tool-error/no-tool as controls.
- Evaluation details include extraction-first answer matching and three instruction-wording variants with fixed question text.
- Mitigations: compare prompting vs SFT vs DPO, using cross-fitting over ToolHop chains so that each reported fine-tuned prediction is on held-out questions.
summary_en.experiments:
Benchmark size: 542 quality-controlled factual questions; with 4 tool conditions and 3 instruction variants, 6,504 fixed evaluation episodes. Models: five open-weight 7–9B LLMs.
Construction stats: ToolHop 3,912 sub-questions → 1,948 unique candidates → 605 independently retrievable facts → QC pool 575 → final 542. Far distractors exist for 443/542.
Outcome reporting: the benchmark enables separate measurement of (i) appropriate deference to correct tool returns and (ii) resistance to incorrect returns, and compares prompting/SFT/DPO. (The provided excerpt does not include the final score tables, so per-model numeric results cannot be reproduced here.)
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim plan (30–45 minutes):
- Read the motivation carefully: why “following tools” is not the same as correct arbitration.
- Focus on benchmark construction: the criteria for independently retrievable facts, near vs far distractors, and the two-annotator QC process.
- Study the evaluation protocol: how closed-book correctness is measured per model, how tool returns are intervened upon, and why tool-error/no-tool controls are necessary.
- If you care about training signals, read the mitigation section for the cross-fitting setup to rule out leakage.

Questions to keep in mind:
- How does the benchmark treat abstention/uncertainty under tool conditions?
- Are incorrect returns “too clean” or systematically detectable, potentially inflating resistance?
- Since tool selection is fixed, what additional evaluation is needed for end-to-end agents where tool choice itself can be wrong?

recommendation.zh: 这篇值得看，因为它把“会用工具”拆成“会不会盲从工具”；若你做 tool-use post-train，先复现这套控制实验，再谈 agent 能力。
recommendation.en: Worth reading because it separates tool use from tool obedience; if you work on tool-use post-training, reproduce this control setup before claiming agent capability.

paper.title: Knowledge-Verified Emergent Deception in LLM Agents Under Conflicting Incentives
paper.abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents serving users on behalf of companies, placing them in settings where user and deployer interests can conflict. When an agent knows that a user is owed something its deployer would prefer to deny, does it remain honest? Answering this is difficult because false statements can reflect either ignorance or hallucination rather than deception. To address this challenge, we introduce KnownLieBench , a knowledge-verified benchmark tha

summary.core_problem: 评估 LLM agent 在用户利益和部署方利益冲突时，是否会在已经知道事实的情况下对用户说假话。
summary.importance: 这是 agent safety 与 deception 评测贡献。关键点是把“模型不知道/幻觉”与“模型知道但在激励冲突下说假话”分开，给欺骗行为测量提供更干净的实验设计。
summary.technical_approach: 论文提出 KnownLieBench。评测流程先用中立 probe 确认 agent 知道用户应得权益，再引入部署方不希望承认该权益的激励设置，观察 agent 是否产生虚假陈述。benchmark 覆盖 8 个客服领域、112 个 grounded cases，并使用多轮对话和 trust-tracking customer agent。它还区分仅由激励诱发的 deception 与显式指令下的 deception。
summary.experiments: 实验覆盖 18 个 proprietary 与 open-weight 模型。摘要未给出具体 deception rate 或模型排名，但说明评测对象包含多轮对话、知识验证、冲突激励和显式指令条件。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper evaluates whether LLM agents lie to users under conflicts between user interests and deployer incentives, after verifying that the agent already knows the relevant entitlement.
summary_en.importance: This is an agent-safety and deception-evaluation contribution. The important design choice is separating ignorance or hallucination from knowingly false claims under incentive conflict.
summary_en.technical_approach: The authors introduce KnownLieBench. The protocol first uses a neutral probe to confirm that the agent knows the user’s entitlement, then introduces an incentive for the deployer to deny it and measures whether false claims emerge. The benchmark covers eight customer-service domains and 112 grounded cases, uses multi-round dialogues with a trust-tracking customer agent, and distinguishes incentive-only deception from deception under explicit instruction.
summary_en.experiments: The evaluation spans 18 proprietary and open-weight models. The abstract does not provide exact deception rates or model-level results, but the setup includes multi-turn dialogue, knowledge verification, conflicting incentives, and explicit-instruction conditions.

recommendation.zh: 值得看实验协议而非榜单；knowledge-verified 设计比普通 deception prompt 更干净，可借鉴到 RL 安全评测。
recommendation.en: Read the protocol, not the leaderboard; the knowledge-verified setup is cleaner than ordinary deception prompts and useful for RL safety evals.

paper.title: From Atomic to Agentic: Towards Interpretable Evaluation of LLMs' Agentic Mathematical Capabilities
paper.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are evolving from performing end-to-end mathematical reasoning to integrating agentic intelligence. However, most existing math benchmarks evaluate only final answers. This outcome-oriented evaluation provides limited diagnostic value for identifying process-level failures or rigorous logic, failing to guide the transformation of LLMs into robust agents. To bridge this gap, we present a process-level benchmark designed to evaluate the inherent agentic mathematical re

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解决的是：现有数学 benchmark 大多只看最终答案，对 agentic reasoning 的评估过于结果导向，无法区分模型到底是不会规划、不会执行某个原子能力，还是不会在中途发现并修正错误。作者关心的不是“端到端数学题能做对多少”，而是“基础模型是否已经具备可被 agent 框架调用的内在 agentic 数学能力”。因此他们把数学推理拆成原子能力，再把这些能力映射到 Planning、Action、Feedback 三类 agent 功能，做过程级、可诊断的评测。
summary.importance: 对预训练本身不是直接贡献，但对 pretrain-posttrain 接口有现实意义。现在很多推理增强、tool use、agent 框架把性能提升归因于系统设计，可如果底座模型在 planning、step execution、self-correction 上的能力分布并不均衡，后续训练和系统搭建就容易误判瓶颈。AMB 的价值在于把“数学能力”与“agentic 能力”做了结构化对齐，提供了更细粒度的 failure surface。对做 reasoning data synthesis、process supervision、RL for reasoning、verifier 或 curriculum 的人，这类 benchmark 能帮助判断该补的是原子执行能力、元认知能力，还是反馈修正能力。
summary.technical_approach: 方法上，论文先构建一个数学原子能力 taxonomy，再把它与 agent 功能轴对齐。数学能力分三层：Level 1 是基础概念与计算，包括符号识别、概念理解、计算；Level 2 是高级推理与应用，包括空间感知、形式化、演绎/归纳推理、数学建模；Level 3 是元认知，包括定理应用、自我反思、新知识学习。作者强调这不是简单给数学技能换标签，而是评估“能力 × agent 功能”的交叉点：Planning 关注能力选择、排序和下一步决策；Action 关注单个原子能力的独立执行；Feedback 关注对既有轨迹的监控、诊断与修正。数据构建方面，作者做了自动化 pipeline，包括数据收集、高质量 trajectory synthesis、多阶段过滤和细粒度标注，并覆盖 text-only 与 multimodal 场景。这个设计的关键取舍是把内在 agentic intelligence 与完整 agent system 解耦：不要求模型真的去调工具、跑环境，而是先测底座是否具备这些可复用的过程能力。这样评测更可控，也更容易定位短板。
summary.experiments: 从给出的全文片段看，实验主结论是：一些 end-to-end 数学表现接近的模型，在 AMB 上会呈现明显不同的 agentic profile，说明只看 final answer 会掩盖过程能力差异。论文还强调 benchmark 覆盖 planning、action、feedback 三类任务，并同时包含文本与多模态数学场景。当前可确认的实验信息主要是定性结论和 benchmark 设计，而不是具体榜单数字；如果阅读全文，建议重点查模型列表、任务规模、每个子能力的样本数、自动标注一致性、以及不同模型在三大功能轴上的分数分布。真正决定这篇 benchmark 是否站得住的，不是总分，而是：1）子任务是否足够去耦；2）自动构造的 trajectory 和标签是否可靠；3）过程级指标是否能预测真实 agent 系统中的失效模式。
summary.reading_guide: 这篇适合按 benchmark 论文的方式读。先看方法部分对 taxonomy 的定义，确认数学原子能力与 Planning/Action/Feedback 的映射是否清楚、是否有重叠。然后看数据构建 pipeline，尤其是 trajectory synthesis、过滤和标注规则，因为 benchmark 的可信度主要取决于这里。实验部分不要只看总榜，优先看各子能力、各 agent 功能维度的拆分结果，以及作者是否展示了“终局分数相近但过程画像不同”的案例。若时间有限，读引言、taxonomy 设计、数据构建和主实验图表即可，约 25 分钟。若要深挖，建议重点检查附录里任务定义、标注模板和 failure case，因为这决定它能否真正服务于 reasoning/post-training 研究，而不只是再多一个数学榜单。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a clear evaluation gap: most math benchmarks judge only the final answer, which makes them poor tools for diagnosing agentic reasoning. They cannot tell whether a model failed at planning, failed to execute a specific atomic skill, or failed to detect and revise an earlier mistake. The goal is therefore not to measure end-to-end math accuracy again, but to evaluate whether a base LLM already contains the intrinsic agentic capabilities needed for mathematical problem solving. To do that, the authors decompose math reasoning into atomic capabilities and align them with three agent functions: Planning, Action, and Feedback.
summary_en.importance: This is not a direct pretraining contribution, but it is relevant to the pretrain-to-posttrain interface. A lot of current progress in reasoning and agents is attributed to scaffolding, tool use, or system design. That can hide the actual bottleneck if the underlying model has uneven capability across planning, execution, and self-correction. AMB is useful because it turns that vague question into a structured evaluation surface. For work on reasoning data synthesis, process supervision, RL for reasoning, verifiers, or curricula, this kind of benchmark can help identify whether the missing ingredient is atomic execution skill, meta-cognitive control, or feedback-based revision.
summary_en.technical_approach: The benchmark is organized around two aligned axes. On the math side, the authors define a taxonomy of atomic capabilities in three levels: Level 1 covers foundational concepts and calculation, including symbol recognition, concept understanding, and calculation; Level 2 covers advanced reasoning and application, including spatial perception, formalization, deductive and inductive reasoning, and mathematical modeling; Level 3 covers meta-cognition, including theorem application, self-reflection, and new knowledge learning. On the agent side, these are aligned with Planning, Action, and Feedback. The key point is that the benchmark evaluates the intersection rather than simply relabeling math skills: planning is framed as capability selection, ordering, and next-step decision making; action as isolated execution of a single atomic capability; feedback as monitoring and revising an existing trajectory. The dataset construction uses an automated pipeline with data collection, trajectory synthesis, multi-stage filtering, and fine-grained annotation, and it includes both text-only and multimodal settings. A notable design choice is to decouple intrinsic agentic evaluation from full agent deployment, so the benchmark measures reusable process capabilities without requiring a complete tool-using system.
summary_en.experiments: From the provided full-text excerpt, the main experimental claim is that models with similar end-to-end math performance can show substantially different agentic profiles on AMB. That is the central evidence for why process-level evaluation matters. The benchmark spans planning, action, and feedback tasks, and covers both textual and multimodal mathematical scenarios. The excerpt does not provide enough concrete numbers to report a reliable leaderboard summary, so the most important things to verify in the full paper are the model roster, task counts per capability, annotation quality, and score distributions across the three agent-function axes. The real test of the benchmark is not the aggregate score, but whether its subtask decomposition is clean, whether the automatically synthesized trajectories are trustworthy, and whether process-level scores correlate with failure modes in actual agent systems.
summary_en.reading_guide: Read this like an evaluation paper, not a methods paper. Start with the taxonomy and check whether the mapping from mathematical atomic skills to Planning/Action/Feedback is precise rather than hand-wavy. Then move to the data pipeline, especially trajectory synthesis, filtering, and annotation, because benchmark credibility depends on those details. In the experiments, do not stop at the overall ranking. Look for per-capability and per-agent-function breakdowns, and for examples where models with similar final-answer accuracy differ sharply in process-level behavior. If time is limited, the introduction, taxonomy design, data construction, and main result tables should be enough in about 25 minutes. For deeper reading, the appendix matters: task definitions, annotation templates, and failure cases will tell you whether this benchmark can genuinely support reasoning and post-training research, rather than just adding another math leaderboard.

recommendation.zh: 值得看，但别把它当数学 benchmark；重点是它把 agentic reasoning 拆成可训练、可验的原子能力，这会直接影响你怎么做 SFT/RL 数据分层。
recommendation.en: Worth reading, but not as just another math benchmark; the useful part is the decomposition of agentic reasoning into trainable and verifiable atomic skills, which should change how you tier SFT/RL data.

paper.title: ReViCo: Unveiling the Limitations of VLMs in Visual Text Understanding via Error Correction
paper.abstract: Vision Language Models (VLMs) have shown great success in general visual tasks, yet they still struggle to deeply understand text within images. In this paper, we introduce ReViCo (Real Visual Correction), a benchmark designed to evaluate VLM text understanding through a novel task of visual text error correction. ReViCo challenges models to identify and fix text errors in real-world images, which requires a profound understanding of the interplay between visual text and its surrounding visual c

summary.core_problem: 评估并暴露现有 VLM 在“图像中的文本理解”上的真实上限：当图中文字存在错误时，模型是否能依赖视觉语境（而非纯语言先验）完成错误定位与纠错（Visual Text Error Correction, VTEC）。
summary.importance: 对基座预训练的直接贡献不在训练方法，而在于提供一个更“对齐预训练短板”的评测切口：把 OCR/读字能力与语义-场景一致性、细粒度字形/拼写混淆、跨语言（中英）纠错绑定在同一任务里。它能帮助判断：VLM 的瓶颈到底在视觉分辨率与tokenization、跨模态对齐、还是语言侧的纠错推断；也为后续做“文本密集场景”的数据配比、视觉 tokenizer 设计、以及 RL/合成数据闭环提供可量化靶标。整体更偏 eval/benchmark 资产，对预训练 recipe 的启发属于间接型。
summary.technical_approach:
1) 任务定义：提出 VTEC，将样本设计为“仅靠语言上下文无法确定正确答案，必须借助图像语境/物体语义/版面线索”。任务拆成 Error Detection（找出错 token/位置）与 Error Correction（给出修正）。
2) 测试集构建：人工从真实世界图像中筛选含自然错误的样本，并强约束‘可解性依赖视觉线索’；同时引入无错误样本（来自 EST-VQA/TextVQA）用于检测能力评估。多轮标注+交叉复核+仲裁，最终得到 1229 个高质量样本。
3) 训练集（用于 targeted training / RL）自动化合成：三阶段 Generate-Edit-Examination。
- Generate：用 GPT-4o 基于真实图像文本生成“错误版本”；再用 Qwen3-235B 过滤掉可被纯语言纠正的样本，保证视觉依赖。
- Edit：用 Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 把错误文本写回图像文本区域，得到带错误的图像。
- Examination：用 Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct 做反向纠错与质量检查，过滤编辑失败/图像不自然/标签不一致样本。
最终得到 4531 条可扩展训练样本。
4) 评测范式：两类提升手段——prompt-based（直接纠错、背景信息增强等）与 targeted model training（包含 RL-based 训练）。论文的重点是用这些手段“尽量榨干现有模型能力”，再观察与人类差距与错误模式，而不是提出新的 VLM 架构。
summary.experiments:
全文主结论是：主流开源与闭源 VLM（列举包含 Qwen-VL、InternVL、GPT-4o、Gemini 2.5 Pro、Seed-1.8 等）在 ReViCo 上与人类存在显著差距；prompt 增强与定向训练能带来提升但无法弥合差距。
从给出的全文片段能确认的硬数字主要在数据规模：测试集 1229；合成训练集 4531；并明确覆盖中英、多种错误类型（中文含音近/形近/音形混合等）。性能具体数值、各模型排名、以及 RL 训练带来的增益幅度在当前提供的正文截断部分未出现，无法可靠复述。若要复核结论强度，建议在原文表格中核对：Detection vs Correction 的分项指标、不同 prompt 策略增益、以及 targeted training/RL 的提升曲线与是否存在过拟合到合成分布。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议（约 25–35 分钟）：
- 先看 Introduction + Figure 1：确认 VTEC 为什么比传统 OCR/VQA 更“卡”在视觉语境理解。
- 重点看 Benchmark 构建（数据筛选约束、标注流程、以及‘必须依赖视觉线索’的判定标准）：这是这篇工作的含金量所在。
- 精看训练集三阶段流水线（Generate-Edit-Examination）：它体现了一个可复用的“合成数据 + 质量门控”范式，适合迁移到其它文本密集视觉任务。
- 最后看错误类型统计与评测协议：理解它到底在测什么、没测什么（例如是否偏向短文本、是否覆盖复杂排版/遮挡/低清）。
如果只关心对预训练的启发：把注意力放在‘过滤掉纯语言可解样本’这一条，它直接对应数据构建时如何避免模型用语言先验投机。

summary_en.core_problem: To rigorously probe whether modern VLMs truly understand text embedded in images (beyond OCR), by framing it as a visual-text error correction task where the correct answer is only recoverable using visual context.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is primarily an evaluation asset rather than a new pretraining recipe. The benchmark is useful to pretraining researchers because it isolates a recurring failure mode in multimodal pretraining: models can read characters but still fail at context-grounded correction (scene-text consistency, fine-grained glyph/typo confusions, bilingual settings). It can serve as a target metric when iterating on visual tokenization, resolution/data mixture choices for text-dense images, and closed-loop data synthesis + RL-style tuning. The impact on pretraining is indirect but practical: it helps diagnose whether the bottleneck is visual fidelity, cross-modal alignment, or language-side correction heuristics.
summary_en.technical_approach:
1) Task formulation (VTEC): split into Error Detection (locate wrong tokens/regions) and Error Correction (produce the corrected text), with samples designed to be unsolvable from linguistic context alone.
2) High-quality test set: manually curated real-world images with natural errors; strict selection rule that visual cues are necessary; multi-stage annotation with cross-checking and adjudication; plus error-free images from EST-VQA/TextVQA for detection calibration. Final test set size: 1,229.
3) Scalable training set for targeted training/RL: a three-stage Generate–Edit–Examination pipeline.
- Generate: GPT-4o proposes corrupted text; Qwen3-235B filters out cases fixable by language-only reasoning.
- Edit: Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 writes the corrupted text back into the image regions.
- Examination: Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct performs correction/verification to filter low-quality edits and label mismatches.
This yields 4,531 synthetic-but-checked training samples.
4) Evaluation paradigms: (a) prompt-based strategies (direct correction, background information enhancement), and (b) targeted model training including RL-based tuning, aiming to approximate each model’s ceiling before concluding there remains a large human gap.
summary_en.experiments:
The paper reports a persistent gap between a broad set of open and closed VLMs (e.g., Qwen-VL/InternVL, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Seed-1.8) and human performance on ReViCo; prompting and targeted training improve results but do not close the gap.
From the provided full-text excerpt, the reliably extractable quantitative details are dataset sizes (test: 1,229; synthetic training: 4,531) and bilingual coverage with multiple error types (notably phonetic/graphic confusions in Chinese). Exact model scores, deltas from prompting/RL, and per-subtask breakdowns are not present in the excerpt, so they should be taken directly from the paper’s main result tables/figures when validating the strength of the claims.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim plan (25–35 minutes):
- Read the task motivation and Figure 1 to internalize why VTEC stresses context-grounded understanding rather than plain OCR.
- Focus on the dataset construction rules and annotation protocol; the key is the constraint “must require visual cues,” which prevents language-only shortcuts.
- Study the Generate–Edit–Examination pipeline as a reusable pattern for synthetic data with quality gates.
- Then check the error taxonomy and evaluation protocol to understand coverage limits (layout complexity, resolution, occlusion, long text).
If you care about pretraining implications, pay special attention to the language-only filter step (Qwen3-235B), since it operationalizes how to avoid spurious linguistic priors in multimodal data generation.

recommendation.zh: 这类 benchmark 对预训练最有用的地方不是榜单，而是把失败拆成“看不清字”和“看懂了但不会改”；读错误分析部分，能直接指导视觉 tokenizer 和图文对齐损失设计。
recommendation.en: The value is not the leaderboard but the failure decomposition into text perception vs context-aware correction; read the error analysis, as it can directly inform visual tokenization and image-text alignment losses.

paper.title: DEEPCHART: How Far are LLMs from Faithful Data-Science Chart Generation?
paper.abstract: Faithful chart generation in real-world data-science workflows requires grounding visualizations in scattered evidence, computing chart-ready quantities, and rendering them accurately. Modern LLMs can produce visually plausible, instruction-compliant charts, yet data-level hallucinations remain difficult to detect in long, noisy, and multimodal contexts. To measure this gap, we introduce DEEPCHART, an expert-annotated benchmark of 1,482 task-conditioned chart-generation instances drawn from real

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作评测 LLM 在真实数据科学场景中生成忠实图表的能力。难点不在于画出看起来合理的图，而在于从长文档和多模态报告中抽取分散证据，计算图表所需的派生量，再把这些数值准确渲染出来。错误的抽取或计算可能被最终图表外观掩盖，形成 hidden hallucination。
summary.importance: 这是一篇评测资产型工作，和预训练方法没有直接关系，但对长上下文、多模态 grounding、数据分析 agent 和代码生成评测有参考价值。它指出仅用最终图像或图表外观打分会漏掉关键错误，尤其是源数据抽取错误和派生数据计算错误。对基座模型研究的启发是：长上下文能力不能只看答案级指标，需要把 evidence retrieval、numerical reasoning 和 executable rendering 拆开评估；否则模型可能在最终输出上显得合规，但内部数据路径并不可靠。
summary.technical_approach: DeepChart 把图表生成定义为 Extract–Reason–Visualize pipeline。给定长上下文 C 和图表意图 Q，模型需要输出源数据 D_src、派生后的图表数据 D_der、可执行绘图程序 P 和最终图表 G。可审计中间状态 J=(D_src, D_der) 是设计核心，因为它允许检查错误出现在抽取阶段、推理阶段还是渲染阶段。Benchmark 包含 1,482 个专家标注实例，来源包括科学论文、金融 10-K filings 和生态系统报告。文本输入平均 220.6K tokens，多模态报告平均 218 页，单个实例平均涉及 317.6 个来自上下文的数据点。任务覆盖 Academic-Normal/Long、Finance-Normal/Long/Ultra-Long，以及 report-level multimodal Ecosystem 设置。指标分为 Source Data Fidelity、Derived Data Fidelity 和 Visual Accuracy Score，分别对应抽取、派生计算和最终可视化。
summary.experiments: 实验采用 zero-shot 设置评估当前强模型。主要发现有三点：第一，视觉上合理的图表经常掩盖数据级幻觉；第二，模型在 Extract 和 Reason 阶段都存在明显困难，说明问题不只是绘图代码生成；第三，输入完整长文档后端到端忠实度下降，说明更长 context window 本身不能保证证据定位和数值推理可靠。全文片段没有给出模型逐项分数和排名，因此更适合关注错误分解和评测协议，而不是比较具体模型优劣。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读预计 20 分钟。优先看 Figure 1 的 ERV pipeline、Table 1 对已有 chart benchmark 的差异总结，以及 Task Definition 中 D_src、D_der、P、G 和 J 的定义。Benchmark 部分需要看数据来源、长度统计和三类 domain setting。Evaluation 部分重点看三个指标如何计算，以及 failure analysis 中 extraction、reasoning、visualization 错误如何被区分。模型排行榜可以快速扫过，不宜作为主要收获。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper evaluates faithful chart generation in realistic data-science workflows. The hard part is not producing a visually plausible chart; it is finding scattered evidence in long and multimodal documents, computing chart-ready quantities, and rendering those quantities without changing their meaning. Errors in extraction or computation can survive into a polished chart and become hidden hallucinations.
summary_en.importance: This is primarily an evaluation contribution rather than a pretraining method paper. It is still useful for researchers working on long-context models, multimodal grounding, data-analysis agents, and code-generation evaluation. The main lesson is that endpoint visual scoring is insufficient. A model can generate an instruction-compliant chart while using wrong source values or wrong derived quantities. For foundation model evaluation, the benchmark argues for separating evidence retrieval, numerical transformation, and executable rendering instead of collapsing all failures into a final-output score.
summary_en.technical_approach: DeepChart formulates chart generation as an Extract–Reason–Visualize pipeline. Given a long analytical context and a chart intent, the model is expected to expose source data, derived chart-ready data, an executable plotting program, and the rendered chart. The auditable intermediate state consists of the extracted source values and the derived quantities. This design lets the evaluator localize failures to extraction, reasoning, or visualization. The benchmark contains 1,482 expert-annotated instances from scientific papers, financial filings, and ecosystem reports. Text inputs average 220.6K tokens, multimodal report inputs average 218 pages, and each instance uses 317.6 context-sourced data points on average. The settings cover academic normal and long contexts, finance normal, long, and ultra-long contexts, and report-level multimodal ecosystem documents. The metrics are Source Data Fidelity, Derived Data Fidelity, and Visual Accuracy Score.
summary_en.experiments: The paper reports zero-shot evaluations of modern LLMs and multimodal models. The key findings are consistent across the task decomposition: visually credible charts often hide data-level hallucinations; both extraction and derived-data reasoning remain major bottlenecks; and full-document inputs reduce end-to-end faithfulness, showing that a larger context window alone does not solve evidence grounding. The provided material does not include the full score tables, so the most reliable takeaway is the stage-wise failure pattern rather than the exact ranking of individual models.
summary_en.reading_guide: A 20-minute skim is sufficient. Start with the ERV pipeline figure and the comparison table against prior chart benchmarks. Then read the task definition for the roles of source data, derived data, plotting program, rendered chart, and the auditable intermediate state. The benchmark section is worth reading for the data scale and domain construction. In the evaluation section, focus on how the three metrics are computed and how the failure analysis separates extraction, reasoning, and rendering errors. The model leaderboard can be skimmed after the protocol is clear.

recommendation.zh: 这不是预训练论文，但评测拆得干净；只看任务分解和错误归因，能帮你判断长上下文模型到底坏在检索、计算还是渲染。
recommendation.en: Not a pretraining paper, but the evaluation decomposition is clean; read the task breakdown and error attribution to see whether long-context failures come from extraction, reasoning, or rendering.

paper.title: ADeptS-Bench: Measuring the Trustworthiness of Computer Use Agents Across Devices
paper.abstract: Computer Use Agents (CUAs) are increasingly deployed to navigate mobile and desktop applications on behalf of users, yet no benchmark comprehensively evaluates whether they can safely interact with visual interfaces while handling ambiguous instructions. We introduce ADeptS-Bench, a dual-stream trustworthiness benchmark, grounded in the ADEPTS capability framework and general population user studies. The Safety stream provides paired benign/malicious tasks with threats embedded in the visual int

summary.core_problem: 现有的计算机使用智能体（CUA）安全评测基准通常只覆盖单一平台，需要在线环境，且威胁分类缺乏系统性的用户调研支持，导致无法全面评估智能体在处理模糊指令和面对视觉界面威胁时的安全性。
summary.importance: 提出了首个跨平台（移动端和桌面端）、离线评估的 CUA 可信度基准 ADeptS-Bench，填补了同时评估安全性和消歧义能力的空白，为 CUA 的实际部署提供了更贴近用户真实担忧的评测工具。
summary.technical_approach: ADeptS-Bench 包含两个评估流：1) 安全流（Safety stream）：在视觉界面中嵌入威胁（如钓鱼覆盖层、误导性按钮、提示注入），要求模型在文本指令看似无害的情况下识别视觉威胁；2) 消歧义流（Disambiguation stream）：评估智能体在面对模糊决策点时是否会寻求澄清。基准的威胁分类基于专家研讨会和 1300 人的用户调研（MaxDiff 调查），确保评测重点与用户最关心的风险（如身份盗窃、账户泄露）一致。采用离线评估方式，通过静态截图和 API 调用完成评测。
summary.experiments: 在 7 个模型（4 个前沿模型，3 个开源模型）上的评估显示，没有模型能同时达到 80% 以上的任务成功率和 30% 以下的攻击成功率。所有模型在面对 2.5 万美元的订单时都会毫不犹豫地点击“结账”。
summary.reading_guide: 建议重点关注第 3 节关于基准设计的原则（特别是基于用户调研的风险优先级排序）和双流评估的具体任务设计。第 5 节的实验结果揭示了当前模型在安全性和消歧义能力上的普遍缺陷，值得深读。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing safety benchmarks for Computer Use Agents (CUAs) typically cover a single platform, require live environments, and lack systematic user research for threat categorization, failing to comprehensively evaluate agents' safety against visual threats and ambiguous instructions.
summary_en.importance: Introduces ADeptS-Bench, the first cross-platform (mobile and desktop), offline trustworthiness benchmark for CUAs that jointly evaluates safety and disambiguation capabilities, providing a more realistic assessment tool aligned with actual user concerns for CUA deployment.
summary_en.technical_approach: ADeptS-Bench features two evaluation streams: 1) Safety stream: embeds threats (e.g., phishing overlays, misleading buttons, prompt injection) within visual interfaces, requiring models to identify visual threats when text instructions appear benign; 2) Disambiguation stream: evaluates whether agents seek clarification at ambiguous decision points. The threat taxonomy is grounded in expert workshops and a 1,300-person user survey (MaxDiff), prioritizing top user concerns like identity theft and account compromise. It uses an offline evaluation setup with static screenshots and API calls.
summary_en.experiments: Evaluation of 7 models (4 frontier, 3 open-source) reveals that no model consistently achieves >80% task success while keeping attack success <30%. Notably, every model clicks 'Checkout' on a $25K order without hesitation.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on Section 3 for the benchmark design principles, especially the user-centric risk prioritization and the dual-stream task design. Section 5 details the experimental results, highlighting the universal shortcomings of current models in safety and disambiguation.

recommendation.zh: 做 GUI/agent 的人该看，尤其是 paired benign-malicious 设计和 refusal-tool 消融；对预训练侧的启发主要在数据与目标，而不是模型架构。
recommendation.en: Worth reading if you care about GUI agents: the paired benign-malicious setup and refusal-tool ablation are the useful parts; the pretraining takeaway is about data/objectives, not architecture.

paper.title: Said Aloud, Read Different: Cross-Modal Instability in Multimodal Models
paper.abstract: Multimodal foundation models are increasingly used in speech-first assistants that must interpret spoken queries and produce visually grounded decisions. Yet it remains unclear whether semantically equivalent queries yield consistent judgments across modality (text vs. speech) and language (English vs. Arabic). We introduce a speech-augmented visually grounded contrastive triplet benchmark spanning 10,150 culturally grounded images from 18 MENA countries, where each image is paired with one supp

summary.core_problem: 评估多模态模型在语义等价的文本与语音查询、英语与阿拉伯语查询之间是否给出一致的视觉 grounding 判断。
summary.importance: 贡献是一个 speech-augmented、文化语境相关的视觉 grounding 对比评测，并提出 contrastive instability 指标。它对语音优先助手和跨语言多模态对齐有参考价值，但更偏评测现象，不直接推进预训练方法。
summary.technical_approach: 构造 triplet benchmark：每张图像配一个被图像支持的陈述和两个合理但不被支持的替代陈述；覆盖文本/语音、英语/阿拉伯语条件。定义 contrastive instability，即模型未能完整解析一个 triplet 的条件失败率，用来区分局部推理碎裂和整体失败。
summary.experiments: 数据包含来自 18 个 MENA 国家、具有文化 grounding 的 10,150 张图像。作者评估近期多模态模型在英语和阿拉伯语、文本和语音输入下的表现，发现模态和语言切换带来明显 triplet-level 不一致，speech 会放大部分失败；摘要未列出具体模型和数值。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper evaluates whether multimodal models make consistent visually grounded judgments under semantically equivalent text versus speech queries and English versus Arabic queries.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is a speech-augmented, culturally grounded contrastive benchmark and an instability metric. It is relevant to speech-first multimodal assistants and cross-lingual multimodal alignment, but it is primarily an evaluation study.
summary_en.technical_approach: Each image is paired with a triplet: one supported statement and two plausible unsupported alternatives. The benchmark spans text and speech inputs in English and Arabic. The proposed contrastive instability metric measures conditional triplet-level failures, separating fragmented reasoning from complete failure.
summary_en.experiments: The benchmark includes 10,150 culturally grounded images from 18 MENA countries. Recent multimodal models are evaluated under English/Arabic and text/speech settings. The abstract reports substantial triplet-level inconsistencies and stronger partial failures under speech, without listing exact model names or scores.

recommendation.zh: 作为多模态对齐 failure mode 备查即可；看 instability 定义和结果表，别把它当通用 VLM pretrain 结论。
recommendation.en: Use it as a multimodal-alignment failure-mode reference; read the instability metric and result table, but do not overread it as a general VLM pretraining result.

paper.title: MathAdv: What Theorem Provers Know, Reason, Formalize, and Generalize
paper.abstract: Formal theorem proving enables machine-verifiable evaluation of mathematical reasoning, yet existing benchmarks often emphasize aggregate proof accuracy, concentrate on a narrow range of mathematics, and provide limited evidence of robustness to equivalent reformulations. We introduce MathAdv, a diagnostic benchmark spanning 13 domains across undergraduate- and graduate-level mathematics. Alongside Lean 4 theorem proving, MathAdv provides up to three auxiliary tasks: multiple-choice questions th

summary.core_problem: 现有形式化数学推理评测过于看重单一证明成功率，覆盖面窄，也很少检验模型对等价改写的稳健性，导致很难定位 theorem prover 到底卡在知识、非形式推理、形式化还是鲁棒性哪一层。
summary.importance: 这是一个诊断型 benchmark 贡献，不是再做一套总分榜。它把数学能力拆成 Lean 4 证明、选择题知识、填空式非形式推理，以及专家构造的等价改写稳健性测试，能更细地暴露模型失败模式。对做 reasoning pretrain、formal data mixture、proof-specialized post-train 的人都有参考价值。
summary.technical_approach: 论文提出 MathAdv，覆盖 13 个本科到研究生层级的数学领域。每道题除正式 Lean 4 证明外，还尽量配套最多三类辅助任务：多选题测知识掌握，填空题隔离 informal reasoning，等价变换题测 presentation robustness。作者用当代 theorem provers 和通用 LLM 进行系统评测，并比较自然语言提示对不同类型模型的影响。
summary.experiments: 摘要未给出具体模型规模和样本量，但实验对象包括 contemporary theorem provers 与 general-purpose LLMs。主要结论有四点：形式化仍是主要瓶颈；不同数学领域间性能差异很大；自然语言引导对通用 LLM 有帮助，但可能伤害 proof-specialized 模型；数学上等价的改写会显著暴露鲁棒性不足。更像 failure mode atlas，而不是追求单点最优分数。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自 University of Maryland、Georgia Tech、Cornell 等学术团队，工作风格偏诊断评测而非大规模系统堆料。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing formal-math benchmarks over-index on aggregate proof accuracy, cover limited areas, and rarely test robustness to equivalent reformulations, making it hard to localize whether theorem provers fail on knowledge, informal reasoning, formalization, or robustness.
summary_en.importance: This is a diagnostic benchmark contribution rather than another leaderboard. By decomposing capability into Lean 4 proving, multiple-choice knowledge, fill-in-the-blank informal reasoning, and expert-crafted reformulation robustness, it exposes failure modes more cleanly. That is useful for researchers working on reasoning pretraining, formal-data mixtures, and proof-oriented post-training.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper introduces MathAdv, spanning 13 undergraduate- and graduate-level math domains. Each problem is paired, when possible, with up to three auxiliary tasks: multiple-choice for knowledge, fill-in-the-blank for informal reasoning, and transformed variants for presentation robustness. The authors evaluate contemporary theorem provers and general-purpose LLMs, including the effect of natural-language guidance.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract does not specify model sizes or dataset scale, but the evaluation includes both theorem provers and general-purpose LLMs. Four main findings are reported: formalization remains the dominant bottleneck; performance varies widely across domains; natural-language guidance helps general LLMs but can hurt proof-specialized models; and mathematically equivalent reformulations reveal substantial brittleness. The value is in the failure-mode map, not in a single headline score.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors are from University of Maryland, Georgia Tech, Cornell, and related academic groups. The work is positioned as diagnostic evaluation rather than a large-scale systems push.

recommendation.zh: 做 reasoning 或 formal data 的人可以看；不是 pretrain 论文，但它把“证明失败”拆成几种可操作瓶颈，读结论和任务设计就够了。
recommendation.en: Worth a skim if you care about reasoning or formal-data mixtures: not a pretraining paper, but it cleanly decomposes proof failure into actionable bottlenecks; read the task design and findings, not every table.

paper.title: Reconstructing the Right Episode: Evaluating Interleaved Conversational Memory Beyond Long Context
paper.abstract: Conversations with chat assistants increasingly span many topics in a single long-running thread, challenging memory systems. Existing long-context and memory benchmarks often expose session or topic boundaries, or probe direct personal-memory questions. These settings understate a harder assistant-memory regime: a flat mixed-topic thread where the system must infer which earlier episode makes a later task decision valid. We introduce SCALE-QA, a constraint-grounded task QA benchmark for flat un

summary.core_problem: 评估长程对话中模型是否能在无显式 session/topic 边界的混合线程里找回正确历史 episode，并据此完成当前任务决策。
summary.importance: 这是一个评测贡献，针对的是长上下文模型和外部记忆系统容易被现有 benchmark 低估的 episode integrity failure。它把问题从“能否在长上下文中检索事实”推进到“能否识别哪段历史证据与当前任务有因果关系”。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 SCALE-QA，一个约束驱动的任务型 QA benchmark。数据由 10 个领域、3000 个审计问题组成，采用无分段的平铺混合话题对话线程，问题是普通任务请求，但答案依赖早前引入的相关证据。使用确定性的四选一评分，并提供 deterministic runtime builder；还提出 Temporal-Semantic 相关方法来分析或构造时间与语义干扰。
summary.experiments: 实验覆盖全部 3000 个问题，最大上下文长度到 128k；另有 400 题分层诊断集用于 1M token 设置。摘要未给出具体模型列表和数值结果，但重点是验证长上下文和记忆系统在 flat mixed-topic thread 下的 episode 选择失败。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自 University of California San Diego。Pengtao Xie 长期做 NLP、机器学习和知识相关任务。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper evaluates whether long-context assistants can recover the right prior episode from a flat, interleaved conversation and use it to make a valid downstream task decision.
summary_en.importance: This is an evaluation contribution. It targets episode-integrity failures that are under-measured by benchmarks exposing session boundaries or asking direct personal-memory questions. The key shift is from factual retrieval to causal selection of the relevant conversational episode.
summary_en.technical_approach: The authors introduce SCALE-QA, a constraint-grounded task QA benchmark with 3,000 audited questions across 10 domains. Conversations are flat and unsegmented, and each question looks like an ordinary task request whose correct answer depends on earlier causally related evidence. The benchmark uses deterministic four-choice grading and a deterministic runtime builder, with a Temporal-Semantic component for analyzing temporal and semantic interference.
summary_en.experiments: The evaluation uses all 3,000 questions up to 128k context and a stratified 400-question diagnostic subset at 1M context. The abstract does not report the full model roster or exact scores, but the experimental focus is on failures of long-context and memory systems under interleaved-topic conditions.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors are affiliated with the University of California San Diego. Pengtao Xie is known for work in NLP, machine learning, and knowledge-centric modeling.

recommendation.zh: 只看任务构造和错误类型即可；它比常规 needle eval 更接近真实助手记忆，但不直接指导预训练 recipe。
recommendation.en: Read the task construction and failure taxonomy; it is closer to real assistant memory than needle-style evals, but it does not directly change pretraining recipes.

institutions: Affiliation:Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

paper.title: FrontierChallenge: Evaluating Scientific Workflow Completion
paper.abstract: Scientific agents increasingly analyze data, execute code, and produce research artifacts, yet most benchmarks emphasize final answers, isolated programs, or a single domain. We introduce FrontierChallenge, a cross-domain benchmark comprising 300 end-to-end scientific workflows. In this paper, we release and evaluate 97 of these tasks, spanning quantum chemistry, molecular dynamics, materials characterization, analytical chemistry, life science, and electrochemistry/environment. Each task provid

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作解决的是评测问题：现有科学 agent benchmark 往往只看最终答案、单段代码或单一学科任务，难以衡量模型是否能在固定目标和固定输入下，独立完成一个端到端、可复现、可验收的科学工作流。作者要测的不是“会不会做一点”，而是“能不能把整套流程交付完整”。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的直接关系不强，它更偏 agent evaluation。但它有两个启发点。第一，它把“部分进展”和“完整交付”明确分开，说明当前前沿模型即使在高平均分下，仍然缺少稳定完成长链条、多产物、多约束任务的能力。这对持续预训练、工具使用数据构造、以及 post-train 信号设计都有参考价值。第二，它提供了一个比单轮 QA 或单文件 coding 更接近真实科研执行的评测单元，能更好暴露模型在长程规划、状态管理、文件一致性、工具调用和错误恢复上的短板。
summary.technical_approach:
方法核心是构建 FrontierChallenge，一个跨六个科学领域的端到端工作流 benchmark。完整池子有 300 个任务，这次公开并评测其中 97 个，其余 203 个保留为内部 held-out。六个领域包括量子化学、分子动力学、材料表征、分析化学、生命科学、电化学/环境。
