每个任务都被打包成自包含单元，至少包含五类元素：任务描述、固定输入、执行环境、交付物契约，以及 task-specific grader。作者强调四个设计原则：代表性、复杂性、多样性、可验证性。也就是说，任务必须像真实专业流程，必须是依赖多步分析和多种产物的完整流程，而不是把同一模板换参数；同时输出必须能通过文件、数值、图表或明确 acceptance criteria 自动评分。

评测指标上，主指标是 Pass Rate，即是否满足完整 task contract；Avg. Score 只作为辅助，表示部分完成度。这个设计很关键，因为很多 agent 在中间步骤上能做出不少东西，但最后交付包不一致、缺文件、数值不合格、图表与报告不匹配，实际并不能交付。作者还比较了 12 个前沿模型和 3 种 agent scaffold，并对 970 条 Claude Code 轨迹做了错误和最终状态分析，用来定位失败模式。
summary.experiments:
实验规模上，公开评测集是 97 个任务，模型数 12，agent scaffold 3 种。任务要求调用真实领域软件，例如 ORCA、CP2K、LAMMPS、AmberTools、PLUMED，并生成代码、分析结果、图表和报告等成套产物。

最关键的结果是“高部分分数、低完整通过率”的明显落差。表现最好的配置是 GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex 和 Grok 4.6 with Claude Code，完成 97 个任务中的 20 个，Pass Rate 只有 20.6%。但最高 Avg. Score 达到 87.9，说明模型经常能做对很多局部步骤，却无法满足完整交付契约。

这种落差在某些领域更明显。分析化学任务中，最高 Avg. Score 达到 87.6，但最高 Pass Rate 只有 4%；电化学/环境任务中，最高 Avg. Score 达到 94.9，但最高 Pass Rate 是 0%。这说明问题不只是知识缺失，而是长链条执行中的最后一公里：文件组织、结果一致性、格式要求、边界条件处理、以及多产物之间的相互约束。

作者还做了 failure analysis，统计 contract-breach signatures 和 Claude Code 轨迹中的 final-status / error behavior。虽然给出的正文片段没有展开全部细节，但从任务设计和指标定义可以看出，benchmark 更关注 agent 是否能在真实环境里把流程跑通，而不是在某个局部子任务上拿高分。
summary.reading_guide:
这篇适合泛读，不需要逐段精读。先看 Introduction，把 benchmark 的目标边界看清：它不是 autonomous science，也不是开放式科研发现，而是在目标、输入和环境固定后，测试 agent 是否能完成指定工作流。

然后重点看 FrontierChallenge 的任务构造原则和评测协议，尤其是 task package 的组成、Pass Rate 与 Avg. Score 的区别、以及为什么完整交付要作为主指标。这部分决定了 benchmark 的信息含量。

最后看结果表和 failure analysis，重点关注两个现象：一是不同 scaffold 对结果的影响，二是高 Avg. Score 却低 Pass Rate 的领域分布。预计 20-30 分钟可以完成一次有效泛读。

如果从基座研究角度带着问题去看，建议关注：哪些失败更像模型能力问题，哪些更像 post-train agent scaffold 问题；以及这类 benchmark 是否能反向指导 continual pretraining 或 tool-use 数据合成。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses an evaluation gap: most scientific-agent benchmarks measure final answers, isolated code snippets, or single-domain tasks, but do not test whether an agent can complete an end-to-end scientific workflow with fixed inputs, real tools, multiple dependent steps, and a verifiable bundle of deliverables. The target is not partial competence, but contract-level completion.
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining-method paper, but it is still relevant as an evaluation asset for long-horizon agentic capability. Two points matter. First, it cleanly separates partial progress from full delivery, showing that frontier models can score highly on intermediate rubric items while still failing to produce a usable final artifact package. That has implications for continual pretraining, tool-use data generation, and post-training reward design. Second, it evaluates a more realistic unit of work than single-turn QA or single-file coding, exposing weaknesses in planning, state tracking, file consistency, tool execution, and recovery from intermediate errors.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The core contribution is FrontierChallenge, a cross-domain benchmark of end-to-end scientific workflows. The full collection contains 300 tasks; 97 are released and evaluated in this work, while 203 remain held out internally. The released tasks span six domains: quantum chemistry, molecular dynamics, materials characterization, analytical chemistry, life science, and electrochemistry/environment.

Each task is packaged as a self-contained unit with aligned components including a task description, fixed inputs, an execution environment, a deliverable contract, and a task-specific grader. The curation follows four principles: representativeness, complexity, diversity, and verifiability. In practice, that means tasks must resemble real professional workflows, require dependency-aware multi-step execution, avoid trivial template variation, and support automated, repeatable scoring through files, numerical checks, plots, or explicit acceptance criteria.

The evaluation protocol is built around two metrics. Pass Rate is the primary metric and requires satisfying the full task contract. Avg. Score is secondary and measures partial progress under task-specific rubrics. This distinction is central to the paper: many agents can produce some correct intermediate outputs, but still fail the workflow because the final bundle is incomplete, inconsistent, or not reproducible. The authors evaluate 12 frontier models under 3 agent scaffolds and also analyze 970 Claude Code trajectories to characterize failure modes and end states.
summary_en.experiments:
The released benchmark contains 97 tasks, evaluated with 12 frontier models and 3 agent scaffolds. Tasks require real scientific software such as ORCA, CP2K, LAMMPS, AmberTools, and PLUMED, and demand executable code, quantitative analysis, visualizations, and evidence-grounded reports.

The main empirical result is a large gap between partial progress and full completion. The best-performing configurations—GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex and Grok 4.6 with Claude Code—complete only 20 of 97 tasks, corresponding to a Pass Rate of 20.6%. Yet the highest Avg. Score reaches 87.9. So the models often make substantial progress on substeps while still failing to satisfy the complete deliverable contract.

This gap is even sharper in some domains. In analytical chemistry, the highest Avg. Score is 87.6, but the best Pass Rate is only 4%. In electrochemistry/environment, the highest Avg. Score is 94.9, while the best Pass Rate is 0%. That pattern suggests the bottleneck is often not local scientific knowledge alone, but end-to-end execution reliability: file organization, consistency across outputs, formatting constraints, edge-case handling, and coherence among code, figures, tables, and prose.

The paper also includes failure analysis through contract-breach signatures and final-status/error behavior in 970 Claude Code trajectories. Even from the available text, the benchmark is clearly designed to stress workflow completion rather than isolated subskill performance.
summary_en.reading_guide:
This is a skim paper. Start with the introduction to understand the scope boundary: the benchmark is not about autonomous science or open-ended discovery, but about executing a specified workflow once the objective, inputs, and environment are fixed.

Then read the benchmark construction and evaluation protocol carefully, especially the task-package design, the distinction between Pass Rate and Avg. Score, and the rationale for using contract-level completion as the primary metric. That is where the benchmark gets its value.

Finally, inspect the main result tables and failure analysis. The two patterns worth tracking are the effect of different agent scaffolds and the domain-specific cases where Avg. Score is high but Pass Rate remains very low. A useful skim should take around 20-30 minutes.

From a foundation-model angle, the most useful questions are whether the observed failures are primarily model-capability failures or scaffold failures, and whether this benchmark can guide continual pretraining or tool-use data synthesis.

recommendation.zh: 一个极具挑战性的跨领域科学工作流 Benchmark，揭示了当前最强模型在长程、复杂科学任务上的严重不足（通过率仅20%），对评估模型的高级推理和规划能力很有价值。
recommendation.en: A highly challenging cross-domain scientific workflow benchmark revealing severe shortcomings of current top models in long-horizon, complex scientific tasks (only 20% pass rate). Valuable for evaluating advanced reasoning and planning capabilities.

paper.title: VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning
paper.abstract: Native visual reasoning treats visual generation as the medium of reasoning itself: visual states (i.e. images and videos) are not merely inputs to be understood or outputs to be rendered, but first-class substrates for problem solving beyond language. Yet progress remains bottlenecked by the lack of scalable training tasks, reliable feedback, and controlled comparisons across generative substrates. In this work, we introduce VBVR-Pro, a closed-loop testbed that makes native visual reasoning thr

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文处理的不是单一模型结构，而是一个更上游的问题：如果把“视觉生成过程本身”当作推理载体，而不是把图像/视频只当输入输出，那么这个方向缺少可规模化训练任务、可靠反馈信号，以及不同生成 substrate 之间的可控比较框架。作者想解决的是 native visual reasoning 研究里的基础设施缺口。全文围绕三个痛点展开：第一，现有 benchmark 多半只适合评测，不适合持续训练；第二，VLM-as-a-judge 在细粒度视觉规则判断上不够可靠，难以作为优化信号；第三，图像生成、视频生成、图文交错生成到底哪种更适合承载视觉推理，过去缺少同分布、同任务、同反馈下的公平比较。
summary.importance: 对纯文本 LLM 预训练的直接影响不大，但对多模态预训练、可验证奖励、以及“非语言 substrate 上的推理训练”有中等启发。它的重要性主要体现在两点。其一，它把 native visual reasoning 从零散 benchmark 变成了一个闭环训练环境：任务可程序化生成，输出可验证打分，奖励可直接用于 RL，且不同生成形式可以在同一任务分布下比较。这种设计思路与基座模型研究里越来越重视的 verifiable reward、synthetic curriculum、closed-loop optimization 是一致的。其二，论文强调 instance-level reward fidelity，而不是只看模型级 rank correlation，这一点对后训练和可验证优化很有借鉴意义。若把视角放宽到 pretrain ↔ posttrain 接口，这篇工作更像是在为“生成式推理能力如何被稳定训练出来”提供实验平台，而不是直接提出新的预训练 recipe。
summary.technical_approach: VBVR-Pro 的核心是一个闭环 suite，而不是单个模型。方法上有三层。第一层是任务生成。作者构建了 300 个 procedural tasks，每个任务都能随机化参数，自动生成训练样本，并同时导出多种对齐模态：视频、关键帧图像、以及带文本注释的 interleaved 表示。这样做的目的不是单纯扩数据，而是保证 image generator、video generator、interleaved generator 在同一底层任务分布上训练和比较，减少数据分布差异带来的结论污染。第二层是可验证反馈。作者没有依赖通用 MLLM judge，而是为任务配套 structured semantic extraction 和 task-grounded verification scorer。也就是说，模型生成的视觉轨迹先被解析成结构化语义，再根据任务规则做程序化核验，得到可用于评测和 RL 的 reward。全文特别强调，这类 scorer 的质量不是用 aggregate correlation 粗略验证，而是通过 arena-style human study 在单样本层面检查与人工判断的一致性。第三层是优化与 substrate 比较。基于这些 verifiable rewards，作者对多任务 visual reasoning 做强化学习，并在 image、video、interleaved 三类生成 substrate 上做受控实验，分析不同视觉推理载体的效率、表达能力和泛化差异。论文还加入了若干诊断分析，例如最近邻检索和 same-prompt visual counterfactual，用来排除“只是记住指令模板”这种解释。
summary.experiments: 实验部分的主结论有三类。第一类是 transfer。作者声称，基于 VBVR-Pro 训练的模型在七个外部视觉推理 benchmark 上都有稳定收益，很多设置下提升超过 20 个百分点。文中点名的外部评测包括 RISE-Video、V-ReasonBench、RULER-Bench、MME-CoF-Pro、VideoThinkBench、BabyVision 和 IntelligentVBench。作者据此主张，任务机制覆盖面的广度比在少数任务上单纯堆更多样本更重要。第二类是 reward quality。论文系统分析了 GPT-5.5、Qwen-3.7-plus、Gemini-3.1-Pro 等 MLLM 作为 judge 的失败模式，包括数值不精确、忽略细粒度证据、误解规则等；与之相比，任务定制的 verifier 在 instance-level arena 人评中与人工更一致，并且能提供方向明确的学习信号。第三类是 optimization。使用这些 verifiable rewards 做多任务 RL 时，即便在较强 baseline 上也能持续提升，说明 reward 不只是“能打分”，而是真的“能训练”。此外，论文还做了数据泄漏和模式拟合层面的诊断：最近邻分析显示外部 benchmark 样本并不能由训练集近邻解释；same-prompt counterfactual 表明模型会随视觉状态变化而改变输出，而不是只跟着文字提示走。由于给出的全文片段没有完整表格，无法在这里逐项复述所有模型规模和绝对分数，但从作者叙述看，实验重点不是单一模型刷榜，而是证明 suite 作为训练基础设施是可扩展、可验证、可优化的。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读时先抓住它不是方法论文意义上的“新模型”，而是训练与评测基础设施。建议先看 Introduction 里三条主线：task scaling、verifiable reward、substrate comparison。然后看任务构造部分，确认 300 个 procedural tasks 如何同时生成 image/video/interleaved 数据，以及为什么这种 aligned generation 对公平比较重要。接着重点看 reward 设计与 judge 分析，这是全文最有借鉴意义的部分，尤其是 instance-level human study 的协议和 verifier 的构造方式。之后再看 transfer 和 RL 优化结果，判断这些奖励是否真的能支撑学习，而不只是离线评测。若时间有限，优先读任务设计、reward verification、外部 benchmark transfer 三部分，40 分钟左右可以建立完整印象；若要深挖，值得仔细看 counterfactual 和 nearest-neighbor 诊断，因为它们直接关系到“学到的是推理操作还是模板匹配”这个关键问题。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses an infrastructure gap rather than a single-model problem. If visual generation itself is treated as the medium of reasoning, instead of using images or videos only as inputs and outputs around a language reasoner, then the field lacks scalable training tasks, reliable feedback, and controlled comparisons across generative substrates. The authors frame native visual reasoning as being bottlenecked by three missing pieces: trainable task sources rather than evaluation-only benchmarks, reward signals that are precise enough for optimization rather than loose VLM judging, and a common task distribution that allows image, video, and interleaved generation to be compared fairly.
summary_en.importance: Its direct relevance to text-only LLM pretraining is limited, but it is meaningfully relevant to multimodal pretraining, verifiable rewards, and non-language reasoning substrates. The main value is that it turns native visual reasoning into a closed-loop setup: tasks are procedurally generated, outputs are verifiably scored, rewards can be used for RL, and different generative substrates can be studied under matched conditions. That design is aligned with broader trends in foundation-model research, where synthetic curricula, verifier-based optimization, and closed-loop training environments are becoming more important. Another useful contribution is the emphasis on instance-level reward fidelity rather than model-level rank correlation. That point transfers well to post-training and verifier design more generally. So the paper is less about a new pretraining recipe and more about building an experimental platform for training generative reasoning capabilities in a stable way.
summary_en.technical_approach: VBVR-Pro is a suite, not a single architecture. Its method has three main layers. First, task generation: the authors build 300 procedural tasks with randomized parameters, allowing scalable sample generation. Each task emits aligned outputs in multiple modalities, including videos, keyframe images, and interleaved text-visual representations. This is important because it lets image generators, video generators, and interleaved generators be trained and compared on the same underlying task distribution rather than on loosely matched datasets. Second, verifiable feedback: instead of relying on generic MLLM judges, the suite pairs tasks with structured semantic extraction and task-grounded verification scorers. Generated visual trajectories are parsed into structured semantics and then checked against task rules programmatically, producing rewards that can be used both for evaluation and reinforcement learning. The paper stresses that reward quality is validated at the instance level through arena-style human studies, not just through aggregate correlations. Third, optimization and substrate comparison: with these verifiable rewards, the authors run multi-task RL for visual reasoning and compare image, video, and interleaved generative substrates under controlled conditions. They also include diagnostics such as nearest-neighbor analysis and same-prompt visual counterfactuals to test whether gains come from reusable reasoning operations rather than instruction-template fitting.
summary_en.experiments: The empirical story has three main parts. First is transfer. Models trained on VBVR-Pro reportedly gain consistently on seven external visual reasoning benchmarks, often by more than 20 percentage points. The named benchmarks include RISE-Video, V-ReasonBench, RULER-Bench, MME-CoF-Pro, VideoThinkBench, BabyVision, and IntelligentVBench. The authors use this to argue that broad coverage of reasoning mechanisms matters more than simply scaling the number of examples from a narrow task family. Second is reward quality. The paper analyzes failure modes of strong MLLM judges such as GPT-5.5, Qwen-3.7-plus, and Gemini-3.1-Pro, highlighting numerical imprecision, missed fine-grained evidence, and rule misunderstanding. In contrast, the task-grounded verifiers show stronger agreement with human judgments in instance-level arena studies and provide cleaner learning signals. Third is optimization. When these verifiable rewards are used for multi-task RL, performance improves steadily even from strong baselines, suggesting that the rewards are useful for training rather than only for offline scoring. The paper also includes anti-shortcut diagnostics: nearest-neighbor analysis suggests that external benchmark gains are not explained by close training-set matches, and same-prompt counterfactuals show sensitivity to changes in visual state rather than just textual prompts. The provided full-text excerpt does not include all detailed tables, so I cannot reproduce every model size and absolute score here, but the experimental emphasis is clearly on validating the suite as scalable, verifiable, and optimizable infrastructure.
summary_en.reading_guide: Read it as an infrastructure paper, not as a new-model paper. Start with the introduction and keep the three threads in mind: task scaling, verifiable rewards, and substrate comparison. Then move to the task-construction section to understand how the 300 procedural tasks generate aligned image, video, and interleaved data, and why that alignment matters for fair comparison. After that, focus on the reward-design and judge-analysis sections. Those are the most transferable parts, especially the instance-level human evaluation protocol and the construction of the verifiers. Then read the transfer and RL sections to check whether the rewards actually support learning rather than just evaluation. If time is limited, prioritize task design, reward verification, and external transfer results; about 40 minutes should be enough for a solid pass. For deeper reading, the counterfactual and nearest-neighbor diagnostics are worth attention because they directly address whether the models learned reasoning operations or only matched superficial templates.

recommendation.zh: 如果你关心 reasoning 不再只靠 text token，这篇值得看任务生成和 verifier 设计；先读 task taxonomy 与 reward 章节，模型结果反而次要。
recommendation.en: If you care about reasoning beyond text tokens, read this for the task generation and verifier design; the model numbers are secondary.

paper.title: VisDocAgentBench: Benchmarking Agents for Visually Rich Document Retrieval
paper.abstract: Visually rich documents encode relevance through language, layout, structured visual elements, and corpus context, yet retrieval is typically evaluated by one-shot query--page matching. Agentic-search benchmarks usually score downstream question answering or report generation, leaving document ranking under iterative evidence acquisition underexplored. We introduce VisDocAgentBench, a closed-corpus benchmark comparing static and agentic retrieval under a shared ranked-output contract. It contain

summary.core_problem: 如何评测“视觉富文档”场景下，检索系统/Agent 在多跳证据获取与迭代搜索中的真实排序能力，而不是一次性 query-page 匹配。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是 benchmark：把 visually rich document retrieval 从“静态匹配”拉到“闭集、可迭代、输出统一为 ranked list”的合同式评测；用 direct/one-bridge/two-bridge 结构把“需要语料上下文的相关性”显式化，能暴露现有强检索器在多跳上的系统性失效。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 VisDocAgentBench：闭集语料（100 文档、2,375 页）+ 120 个 unique-target queries；查询按证据结构分层（direct/one-bridge/two-bridge），并覆盖 semantic/relational/visual 三类查询意图；构造流程强调 relation-preserving（保持实体/关系链），并通过全篇审阅与 hard-negative 验证提高难度与可判别性；评测对比 static retriever 与 agentic retrieval，在同一“输出为排序结果”的接口下比较。
summary.experiments: 报告显示强 late-interaction visual retriever 在 direct 查询上 Recall@1 可达 97.50%，但在 two-bridge 上仅 2.50%，体现多跳/语料上下文依赖时静态匹配的崩溃；论文还声称 agent 能在该设置下显著恢复多跳检索表现（摘要截断，具体幅度需看正文表格）。

summary_en.core_problem: How to evaluate visually-rich document retrieval under iterative, multi-hop evidence acquisition (agentic search) rather than one-shot query–page matching.
summary_en.importance: Benchmark contribution: it standardizes static vs agentic retrieval with a shared ranked-list output contract, and explicitly stratifies queries by evidence structure (direct/one-bridge/two-bridge) to surface failures when relevance depends on corpus context.
summary_en.technical_approach: VisDocAgentBench: a closed corpus (100 documents, 2,375 pages) with 120 unique-target queries balanced across evidence hops; queries cover semantic/relational/visual intents; construction is relation-preserving and validated via full-document review plus hard-negative checking; evaluates static retrievers and agents under the same ranking interface.
summary_en.experiments: A strong late-interaction visual retriever reaches 97.50% Recall@1 on direct queries but only 2.50% on two-bridge queries, indicating a sharp breakdown in context-dependent multi-hop retrieval; the abstract suggests agents recover performance (details require the main tables due to truncation).

recommendation.zh: 把“检索”从一次匹配改成多跳证据获取的排序合同，能直接暴露 retriever 的结构性短板；只需看 two-bridge 的设定与主表，别被 direct 的高分误导。
recommendation.en: It reframes retrieval eval into a multi-hop, iterative evidence-acquisition ranking contract that exposes structural retriever failures; read the two-bridge setup and main tables—direct-query scores are a red herring.

paper.title: MMJailBench: A Factorized Benchmark for Disentangling Multimodal Jailbreak Vulnerabilities
paper.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, yet how different factors shape their jailbreak vulnerabilities remains poorly understood. Existing benchmarks often couple harmful intent, prompt framing, visual semantics, and instruction carrier within individual jailbreak instances, obscuring the specific sources of observed vulnerabilities. To address this limitation, we introduce MMJailBench, a factorized benchmark that systematically varies and

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解决的不是“某个多模态越狱技巧是否有效”，而是更基础的问题：现有多模态安全 benchmark 把有害意图、提示词叙事方式、图像语义线索、指令载体混在同一个样本里，导致攻击成功率只能反映总体脆弱性，不能解释脆弱性究竟来自哪里。MMJailBench 试图把这些因素拆开，在可控组合下做 matched comparison，从而回答模型到底是被哪一类上下文因素带偏了安全判断，尤其是视觉上下文是否会改变模型对“合法性”“授权性”“专业性”的感知。
summary.importance: 对基座研究的直接价值不在于提出新的训练方法，而在于把多模态安全评测从“黑盒打分”推进到“可归因诊断”。这对原生多模态预训练和后训练都有意义。若一个模型在 authority-like visual cues 下系统性放松拒答，问题就不只是 safety policy 不够强，也可能涉及视觉 token、跨模态对齐、instruction grounding 和 refusal head 的耦合方式。对做 VLM/MLLM 预训练的人，这类 factorized benchmark 能帮助区分：是模型真的理解了图像中的授权语义，还是把某些视觉模式误当成高可信信号。贡献类型更像评测基础设施和诊断工具，而不是范式级方法创新。
summary.technical_approach:
方法核心是一个因子化设计。作者把多模态越狱样本拆成四个维度：1）harmful intent，共 272 个有害意图；2）prompt framing，共 6 种提示模板，控制叙事结构、任务包装和输出要求；3）visual semantics，共 5 类与任务相关的视觉语义，用来模拟不同上下文线索；4）instruction carrier，区分指令是直接文本给出，还是以图像中的文字/视觉载体给出。这样每个测试实例都可以看成同一底层 harmful intent 在不同上下文配置下的一个投影。

这个设计的关键不是简单做笛卡尔积，而是强调 matched comparison：固定其余因素，只改变一个因素，观察拒答/服从行为如何变化。这样才能把 aggregate ASR 拆成 factor-level attribution。论文还配了一个模块化评测套件，支持 full 和 lightweight 两种配置、多个 judge 选项以及多维指标，目标是让评测既能大规模跑，也能控制成本。

从全文描述看，作者还做了一个代表性开源模型的诊断分析，关注内部表征和 cross-modal interaction。虽然这部分更偏分析而非方法，但它补上了一个重要环节：不仅知道“哪些因素会让模型更容易被越狱”，还尝试看这些脆弱性是否对应到内部表示模式变化，例如视觉 authority cue 是否会改变模型对 harmful request 的条件化方式。和以往固定 prompt-image 对的 benchmark 相比，MMJailBench 的区别在于它不把单个攻击样本当作最终对象，而把“因素组合空间”当作评测对象。
summary.experiments:
实验覆盖 16 个开源和闭源 MLLM。最重要的结论有四个。第一，脆弱性在 harm domain 上明显不均匀，cyber abuse、economic harm、privacy violations、deception/manipulation 更容易出现越狱成功，这说明安全能力不是一个单一标量，而是分布在不同风险子空间中的不均衡能力。第二，prompt framing 是影响最大的因素。即便 harmful intent 不变，只改叙事包装或输出格式要求，拒答率和服从率也会明显变化，说明很多模型的安全边界仍然高度依赖表面语言形式。第三，task-relevant visual semantics 会系统性削弱拒答，尤其是 authorization documents、identity credentials 这类带“权威/授权”意味的视觉线索，暴露出更强脆弱性。第四，instruction carrier 的影响高度依赖模型，不是所有模型都会因为“指令写在图里”而更容易被攻破。

从摘要和正文可见，作者还做了 judge、配置规模和多维指标设计，但当前给出的全文片段里没有足够具体的数值表格，无法可靠复述各模型的精确 ASR 排名或每个因子的绝对增幅。能确定的是：论文强调的是异质性和可归因性，而不是给出一个统一的平均分结论。
summary.reading_guide: 这篇适合泛读，不需要逐页精读。建议先看 Introduction 和 Figure 1/2，理解作者为什么认为现有 benchmark 的 factor entanglement 会遮蔽诊断信号。然后重点看 benchmark construction 部分，确认四个因素是如何定义、如何组合、如何保证 matched comparison 的。接着看主结果图表，尤其是按 harm domain、prompt framing、visual semantics、instruction carrier 分解的结果，这部分最能体现 benchmark 的信息增量。若你做多模态预训练或安全对齐，再看代表性开源模型的内部分析，关注作者如何把行为层面的 vulnerability 和 cross-modal representation 联系起来。预计 25 到 40 分钟可以抓住主要内容；若只关心是否值得纳入内部评测体系，看设计和主结果即可。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper is not mainly about proposing another multimodal jailbreak attack. It targets a more basic evaluation problem: existing MLLM safety benchmarks entangle harmful intent, prompt framing, visual context, and instruction carrier inside fixed prompt-image pairs, so the resulting attack success rate is hard to interpret. MMJailBench tries to disentangle these factors and measure which ones actually drive refusal failures, especially whether visual context changes a model’s perception of legitimacy, authority, or authorization.
summary_en.importance: Its value for foundation-model research is diagnostic rather than algorithmic. The benchmark turns multimodal safety evaluation from aggregate scoring into factor-level attribution. That matters for native multimodal pretraining and post-training because a failure under authority-like visual cues may reflect more than weak safety tuning; it may expose how visual tokens, cross-modal alignment, instruction grounding, and refusal behavior interact. For researchers building VLM/MLLM pretraining pipelines, this kind of benchmark helps separate genuine visual understanding from spurious reliance on high-credibility visual patterns.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The core idea is a factorized benchmark design. Each jailbreak instance is decomposed along four axes: (1) harmful intent, with 272 intents; (2) prompt framing, with 6 templates controlling narrative structure and output requirements; (3) visual semantics, with 5 types of task-relevant visual context; and (4) instruction carrier, distinguishing direct textual instructions from visually rendered instructions. The benchmark then evaluates matched configurations where one factor changes while others are held fixed.

That matched-comparison setup is the key methodological choice. Instead of treating each prompt-image pair as an indivisible attack example, the benchmark treats the combinatorial factor space as the object of evaluation. This allows factor-level attribution rather than only aggregate jailbreak rates. The paper also provides a modular evaluation suite with full and lightweight settings, multiple judge options, and multidimensional metrics, aiming for reproducible and scalable auditing.

The paper further includes diagnostic analysis on a representative open-weight model, looking at internal representations and cross-modal interactions associated with vulnerability. That part is less about a new method and more about linking behavioral failures to representation-level patterns. Compared with prior benchmarks built from fixed multimodal attack instances, the main difference is that MMJailBench is structured for controlled causal-style comparisons across factors.
summary_en.experiments:
The evaluation covers 16 open-weight and proprietary MLLMs. Four findings stand out. First, vulnerability is highly uneven across harm domains, with cyber abuse, economic harm, privacy violations, and deception/manipulation showing higher susceptibility. Second, prompt framing is the dominant source of variation: even with the same harmful intent, changing the narrative wrapper or requested output format can substantially alter refusal behavior. Third, task-relevant visual semantics systematically weaken refusal, and authority-like cues such as authorization documents or identity credentials are especially effective. Fourth, the effect of instruction carrier is strongly model-dependent; visually rendered instructions do not uniformly increase vulnerability.

The paper also discusses judge choices, full vs. lightweight configurations, and multidimensional metrics. However, from the provided full-text excerpt, there is not enough reliable table-level detail to restate exact model rankings or precise per-factor deltas. The main empirical contribution is the heterogeneity and attribution structure, not a single leaderboard number.
summary_en.reading_guide: This is a skim paper rather than a deep read. Start with the introduction and the main benchmark-design figures to understand why factor entanglement in prior benchmarks limits diagnosis. Then read the benchmark construction section carefully: how the four factors are defined, combined, and controlled is the real contribution. After that, inspect the main result tables/figures broken down by harm domain, prompt framing, visual semantics, and instruction carrier. If your work touches multimodal pretraining or safety alignment, the diagnostic analysis on internal representations is worth a quick pass. Around 25–40 minutes should be enough to extract the main ideas.

recommendation.zh: 只看因子化设计和模型间差异图；它比普通 jailbreak 榜单更能暴露多模态对齐的薄弱轴。
recommendation.en: Skim the factorization design and cross-model variance plots; it is more diagnostic than a flat jailbreak leaderboard for multimodal alignment.

paper.title: LifePlanner: Evaluating LLM Agents for Geo-spatial Planning with Social Media Data
paper.abstract: Geo-spatial planning, like trip design, is a realistic testbed for LLM agents because it requires grounded tool use, noisy evidence retrieval, and multi-constraint reasoning. Most benchmarks, however, only provide clean geospatial data and tools, missing the open-ended social signals that people use in daily planning. We introduce LifePlanner, a benchmark that enriches map data with large-scale local social media posts and provides access through an MCP toolset. LifePlanner provides an evaluatio

summary.core_problem: 如何用更接近真实用户决策的信息源（带噪声、时效性强、指代含混的本地社媒内容）来评测 LLM agent 的地理空间规划能力，并把失败原因从“答错了”细化到“证据没找全/约束没整合好/工具调用不可靠”等可诊断层面。
summary.importance: 对预训练本身的直接贡献有限，但对“预训练↔后训练闭环”里的评测与数据形态有启发：1）把开放域、弱结构的社媒证据引入规划评测，能更真实地暴露 agent 的检索-证据整合短板；2）提供了一个可复现的 MCP 工具环境与结构化输出评分框架，适合用作 tool-use / evidence-grounded planning 的对齐与数据合成靶场；3）从结果归因上强调“失败更多来自证据获取不全而非纯幻觉”，这会影响后续训练信号设计（例如把探索/覆盖率作为奖励或过程监督）。整体更像 agent-eval 资产，而不是预训练方法论文。
summary.technical_approach:
LifePlanner 的方法核心是“环境 + 协议”两件事。
1）环境（database + tools）：在约 10km^2 城市区域内构建地理空间骨架（高德 API + OSM），清洗去重后得到约 3,600 个地点（spatial anchor）。然后为每个地点抓取本地社媒证据（小红书 RedNote）：按地点名检索最多 20 条 note，每条 note 取最多 10 条评论；保留标题、正文、发布时间、互动指标、tag 等，形成约 200,000 条 notes/comments 的弱结构语料。关键点是：证据允许歧义、冗余、无关信息存在，逼迫 agent 做交叉验证与消歧。
2）属性蒸馏（用于构造题目而非给模型看）：用 Gemini-2.5-Flash 从社媒抽取静态属性（设施/供给）与动态属性（短期状态如临时关闭、新品等），这些“dynamic memory fields”只用于生成/筛选测试用例，评测时不暴露给 agent，避免把答案泄露成结构化字段。
3）访问隔离与工具箱：评测时 agent 只能通过 MCP 工具检索原始 posts/comments 与地图信息、做基础空间分析/路径规划；不能直接读取蒸馏属性。这样把难点锁定在“工具检索→证据阅读→约束整合→规划输出”。
4）评测协议：667 条合成但贴近日常的查询，覆盖四类任务（Place Perception / Nearby Discovery / Routing / Trip Design），每类三档难度：L0 单次检索即可；L1 多次检索+计算；L2 在证据基础上做决策并满足额外用户约束。模型输出结构化 JSON，便于多视角打分与错误归因。
summary.experiments: 论文给出的关键信号是难度分层下的性能断崖：前沿模型在简单检索类任务表现较好，但在复杂规划（尤其 L2）显著退化，整体 Pass Rate 下降到 40.2%（文中描述为复杂规划场景的显著下滑）。作者的诊断结论是：主要失败来自不完整的证据获取与薄弱的约束整合，而不是典型的无中生有式幻觉；同时，单纯扩大模型规模或让模型写更长的推理轨迹不足以解决问题，暗示瓶颈在“探索/检索策略 + 证据覆盖率 + 约束一致性检查”而非纯语言推理长度。由于你提供的全文片段在实验细节处截断，具体到各模型（18 个模型/具体型号）与各子任务分数、消融（如工具可用性、检索次数上限、是否给路线工具等）的数字需要以论文实验章节为准。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议（约 20–30 分钟）：
1）先看任务分层定义（四类任务 + L0/L1/L2），理解作者如何把“检索/计算/决策”拆开；这决定了它能否用于训练信号设计。
2）重点看数据库构建与“访问隔离”设计：蒸馏属性只用于出题、不用于评测输入，这一点决定 benchmark 是否会被“结构化字段投机”。
3）看失败归因部分：作者把问题归到 evidence acquisition 与 constraint integration，适合映射到后训练（过程奖励、检索覆盖率、工具调用可靠性）而不是继续堆 CoT。
4）如果要用于训练：关注 MCP 工具接口与 JSON 输出 schema，评估能否直接做轨迹数据收集与 verifier 设计。

summary_en.core_problem: How to evaluate LLM agents on geo-spatial planning with realistic, noisy, time-sensitive local evidence (social media posts/comments), and to diagnose failures at the level of evidence acquisition and constraint integration rather than only final-answer correctness.
summary_en.importance: Limited direct impact on pretraining recipes, but useful as an evaluation asset that stresses a data regime closer to real-world agent use: weakly-structured social evidence + tool-mediated retrieval + multi-constraint planning. The paper’s main takeaway for training is the diagnosis that many failures come from incomplete evidence gathering and weak constraint integration (not pure hallucination), which suggests training signals around exploration/coverage, tool-use reliability, and evidence-grounded verification. It is primarily an agent-eval benchmark rather than a pretraining-method contribution.
summary_en.technical_approach:
LifePlanner is built around (1) a realistic environment and (2) a structured evaluation protocol.
1) Environment: a ~10 km^2 urban region with ~3,600 deduplicated places (spatial anchors) built from AMap API + OpenStreetMap. Each anchor is enriched with weakly-structured local social media evidence from RedNote: up to 20 notes per place via name search, and up to 10 comments per note, retaining full text, timestamps, engagement stats, and tags—yielding ~200k notes/comments. Ambiguity and irrelevant content are intentionally preserved.
2) Attribute distillation for case construction: Gemini-2.5-Flash extracts static tags (facilities/offerings) and dynamic states (temporary closures/new arrivals). Crucially, these distilled “dynamic memory” fields are used to construct tasks but are hidden from evaluated agents to prevent leakage.
3) Access separation + MCP tools: during evaluation, agents must retrieve and interpret raw posts/comments through an MCP toolset, alongside map/routing utilities.
4) Evaluation protocol: 667 synthetic yet realistic queries across four task families (Place Perception, Nearby Discovery, Routing, Trip Design) and three difficulty tiers: L0 single retrieval; L1 multi-retrieval + calculation; L2 decision-making under additional user constraints. Agents output structured JSON for multi-aspect scoring and analysis.
summary_en.experiments: The headline result is a sharp performance cliff from simple retrieval to complex constrained planning: models do reasonably on easier tiers but degrade substantially on harder planning, with pass rate reported to drop to 40.2% in complex settings. The paper attributes failures mainly to incomplete evidence acquisition and weak constraint integration, and argues that scaling models or producing longer reasoning traces is not sufficient—pointing to bottlenecks in retrieval/exploration strategy and grounded verification. The provided full-text excerpt is truncated before detailed tables; model-by-model breakdowns and any ablations should be taken from the experiments section of the paper.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim plan (20–30 minutes):
- Read the task taxonomy and L0/L1/L2 definitions first; this is the core design that makes errors diagnosable.
- Focus on the dataset construction and the “distill-for-construction, hide-for-eval” access separation; it determines whether agents can game the benchmark.
- Check the failure analysis: how they operationalize evidence acquisition vs constraint integration.
- If you want to reuse it for training, inspect the MCP tool API and the JSON output schema to see whether trajectories can be collected and verified cleanly.

recommendation.zh: 一个结合社交媒体数据的 Agent 规划 Benchmark，揭示了当前模型在复杂约束和噪声检索下的短板，可作为 Agent 评测的参考。
recommendation.en: An agent planning benchmark incorporating social media data, revealing current models' shortcomings in complex constraints and noisy retrieval; useful reference for agent evaluation.

paper.title: DataKernelBench: Can LLMs Optimize Database Queries on GPUs?
paper.abstract: GPUs increasingly accelerate database systems, but query-specific peak performance still often relies on hand-written kernels. Existing LLM kernel benchmarks focus on machine learning operators, leaving irregular, heterogeneous, data-movement-heavy database-style operators untested. We introduce DataKernelBench, which translates SQL into validated PyTorch TorchPlan programs and evaluates LLMs that optimize either the core tensor-bounded snippet or the full query in CUDA or Triton through executi

summary.core_problem: 论文提出一个面向数据库 GPU 查询优化的 LLM benchmark，检验现有模型能否在不规则、数据搬运密集的 workload 上生成高性能 CUDA/Triton kernel，而不是只会优化常见 ML operator。
summary.importance: 它的贡献是 benchmark 与执行式评测框架。对基座预训练本身不直接，但对代码模型能力边界、训练数据覆盖盲区和 execution-guided synthesis 的评测设计有一定参考价值。
summary.technical_approach: 作者构建 DataKernelBench：把 SQL 转成可验证的 PyTorch TorchPlan 程序，再让 LLM 优化核心 tensor-bounded 片段或整条查询，目标代码为 CUDA 或 Triton，并通过 execution-guided repair 提高可执行率。评测重点是 full-query specialization、kernel fusion、执行策略变化和 workload context 的作用。
summary.experiments: 在 TPC-H SF10、H100 GPU 上评测 10 个 proprietary/open-weight 模型。最强的 full-query CUDA 配置在 full pass rate 下相对 torch.compile 达到 2.11× 加速。作者还扩展 TorchPlan 与 Dask 以处理超出 GPU 显存的数据。结果显示，强模型更受益于 full-query specialization，workload context 比 hardware context 更重要。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自 IBM Research 和 TU Wien。更接近代码生成/系统 benchmark，而不是 LLM 基座训练论文。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper introduces a benchmark for testing whether LLMs can optimize GPU database queries, targeting irregular and data-movement-heavy workloads rather than standard ML operators.
summary_en.importance: Its main contribution is an evaluation asset and execution-based benchmark. It is not directly about pretraining, but it is mildly useful for understanding code-model blind spots, training-data coverage, and execution-guided synthesis evaluation.
summary_en.technical_approach: DataKernelBench translates SQL into validated PyTorch TorchPlan programs, then asks LLMs to optimize either the core tensor-bounded snippet or the full query into CUDA or Triton, with execution-guided repair. The benchmark probes full-query specialization, kernel fusion, execution-strategy changes, and the role of workload context.
summary_en.experiments: The study evaluates 10 proprietary and open-weight models on TPC-H SF10 with an H100 GPU. The strongest full-query CUDA setup achieves a 2.11x speedup over torch.compile at full pass rate. TorchPlan is extended with Dask for data larger than GPU memory. Stronger models benefit more from full-query specialization, and workload context matters more than hardware context.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors are from IBM Research and TU Wien. This is closer to a code-generation/systems benchmark than a foundation-model training paper.

recommendation.zh: 不是 pretrain 方向，但 benchmark 设计还算干净；只看 setup 和结论图，能帮助判断代码模型训练语料对系统代码的覆盖缺口。
recommendation.en: Not a pretraining paper, but the benchmark is reasonably clean; skim the setup and key result figures to gauge where code-model pretraining misses systems-style kernels.

paper.title: FuzzingBrain-Bench V1: Evaluating Open-Ended Bug Discovery by LLMs
paper.abstract: Evaluating the ability of large language models (LLMs) to discover software bugs is increasingly important. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate this capability by asking the model to generate a proof-of-concept input that triggers a predefined target vulnerability. However, this setup may overlook valid crashes discovered by the model when they do not match the predefined target. As a result, the evaluation may not reflect the model's real capability.   We present FuzzingBrain-Bench, a benchm

summary.core_problem: 评估 LLM 在开放式软件漏洞发现中的真实能力，而不是只看是否触发预定义目标漏洞。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是 coding / security agent benchmark；它指出传统 PoC-to-target 评测会漏掉模型发现的其他有效 crash，因此分数可能低估或误刻画模型的 fuzzing 能力。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 FuzzingBrain-Bench：给模型一个开源项目和 sanitizer-instrumented harness，并封装在自包含 Docker 镜像中；模型目标是在 harness 下生成输入，触发尽可能多的 distinct crashes；按 distinct crash signatures 数量计分，并用上限和难度系数加权。
summary.experiments: 摘要说明 benchmark 面向开源软件 bug discovery，但未给出挑战数量、评测模型列表、基线表现或具体分数；核心信息是开放式 crash discovery 的任务设计和 scoring scheme。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper evaluates LLMs on open-ended software bug discovery rather than on generating inputs for predefined target vulnerabilities.
summary_en.importance: It is a coding/security agent benchmark contribution. The key point is that target-vulnerability benchmarks can miss valid crashes found by models and therefore misrepresent real bug-discovery capability.
summary_en.technical_approach: FuzzingBrain-Bench gives a model an open-source project and a sanitizer-instrumented harness inside a self-contained Docker image. The model generates inputs to trigger as many distinct crashes as possible, scored by distinct crash signatures with caps and difficulty weighting.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract describes the benchmark design but does not report the number of challenges, evaluated models, baselines, or numerical results.

recommendation.zh: 作为 coding-agent eval 备查即可；开放式 crash 计分比定点 PoC 更干净，但和基座预训练距离较远。
recommendation.en: Keep it as a coding-agent evaluation reference; open-ended crash scoring is cleaner than target PoC matching, but it is far from base pretraining.

paper.title: FLARE: Verifying MILP Reformulations with LLM-Based Theorem Proving
paper.abstract: Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) is a fundamental tool for combinatorial optimization with extensive real-world applications. A central challenge is designing computationally efficient MILP formulations. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to automate the modeling process, from deriving formulations to strengthening them. Reliable automation requires robust methods for verifying that proposed formulations preserve the underlying optimization problem. However, existing app

summary.core_problem: 解决 LLM 自动提出的 MILP reformulation 难以在一般问题实例上被可靠验证的问题，避免只靠数值测试造成的伪正确。
summary.importance: 贡献主要在评测与验证协议：把“reformulation 是否保持原优化问题”形式化到 Lean 中，并给出 LLM+proof assistant 的验证流程与配套基准 FormulationBench。对 LLM 研究员的价值在于：它展示了 theorem proving 式 verifier 如何替代脆弱的 sample-based checking。
summary.technical_approach: 作者提出 FLARE，用 LLM-based agent 与 Lean proof assistant 协作，针对候选 reformulation 与 reference formulation 构造可机检的证明。核心不是提升语言模型本体，而是把验证目标从数值一致性提升到构造性、可形式化的等价性证明。
summary.experiments: 摘要说明同时引入了 FormulationBench，用于评估 reformulation verification。实验应比较数值评估与形式化验证在一般性、可靠性上的差异，并测试 LLM agent+Lean 的验证能力。摘要未给出模型规模、具体通过率或与哪些 LLM 比较的数字。
summary.authors_note: 作者包括 Madeleine Udell、Ellen Vitercik，均在优化与机器学习交叉方向有代表性工作。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper tackles the problem of reliably verifying whether LLM-proposed MILP reformulations preserve the original optimization problem beyond finite numerical tests.
summary_en.importance: The main contribution is an evaluation and verification protocol: it formalizes reformulation correctness in Lean and introduces both an LLM-plus-proof-assistant verifier and a benchmark, FormulationBench. For LLM researchers, the interesting part is how theorem-proving style verification can replace brittle sample-based checking.
summary_en.technical_approach: FLARE combines an LLM-based agent with the Lean proof assistant to verify candidate reformulations against a reference formulation via machine-checkable proofs. The novelty is not a new language model, but a shift from numerical agreement to constructive formal verification.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract indicates the introduction of FormulationBench for evaluating reformulation verification. Experiments likely compare numerical evaluation versus formal verification in terms of generality and reliability, and test the capability of the LLM-agent-plus-Lean pipeline. No model sizes or headline pass-rate numbers are given in the abstract.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors include Madeleine Udell and Ellen Vitercik, both well known for work at the optimization/ML interface.

recommendation.zh: 和 pretrain 不直接相关，但 verifier 设计很干净；只看任务定义和 benchmark 构造，能学到怎样把“看起来对”改成“可机检地对”。
recommendation.en: Not directly about pretraining, but the verifier design is clean; read only the task formalization and benchmark setup to see how to turn ‘looks right’ into machine-checkable correctness.

paper.title: Paint What You See: Benchmarking Dexterous Visual Tool Use in Multimodal Agents
paper.abstract: Evaluation is shifting from static QA toward agentic settings where models act through external tools. We identify a critical yet underexplored capability within this space - dexterous visual tool use: fine-grained, closed-loop parameterized visual action in which models infer tool parameters from visual evidence, and those parameters directly govern the final result. Existing benchmarks cover web navigation, GUI operation, and software engineering, but rarely target this coupling between visual

summary.core_problem: 评估多模态 agent 是否能根据视觉证据执行细粒度、闭环、参数化的视觉工具操作。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是多模态 agent benchmark、训练数据和模型。它补齐了 web/GUI/SWE 评测较少覆盖的能力：视觉理解必须直接转化为精确工具参数，最终结果由动作轨迹决定。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 EASEL，以 reference-guided visual reconstruction 为核心代理任务：agent 逐步绘制画布以匹配参考图像。还包含区域标注、手写、路径规划等语义任务。配套 EASEL-Data，一个 44 万样本的两阶段课程式轨迹监督数据集，并训练 EASEL-9B 用于研究该能力。
summary.experiments: 摘要披露了 440k 轨迹监督数据和 EASEL-9B，但没有给出完整模型对比、指标、得分或相对提升。实验重点应是验证视觉证据到工具参数的闭环控制能力，而不是传统静态 VQA 准确率。

summary_en.core_problem: Evaluate whether multimodal agents can perform fine-grained, closed-loop, parameterized visual tool use grounded in visual evidence.
summary_en.importance: The contribution combines a multimodal-agent benchmark, dataset, and model. It targets a capability under-covered by web, GUI, and SWE benchmarks: translating visual evidence into precise tool parameters that directly determine the final output.
summary_en.technical_approach: EASEL uses reference-guided visual reconstruction as its main proxy task: an agent incrementally paints a canvas to match a reference image. It also includes semantic tasks such as region annotation, handwriting, and path planning. The authors provide EASEL-Data, a 440k-sample two-stage curriculum dataset for trajectory supervision, and an EASEL-9B model.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract reports a 440k-sample trajectory-supervision dataset and EASEL-9B, but does not provide full model comparisons, metrics, scores, or improvement numbers. The experimental focus is closed-loop visual evidence-to-tool-parameter control rather than static VQA accuracy.

recommendation.zh: 看任务设计和 EASEL-Data 课程即可；它更像多模态 agent 能力探针，不是基座预训练 recipe。
recommendation.en: Skim the task design and EASEL-Data curriculum; this is a multimodal-agent probe, not a foundation pretraining recipe.

paper.title: When Seeing Is Not Enough: Benchmarking Interactive Visual Grounding in LVLMs
paper.abstract: Visual grounding is typically evaluated as a one-shot mapping from an informative referring expression to a visual target. This formulation misses a central property of real-world reference: target information is often incomplete, ambiguous, and established through interaction. We introduce a controlled evaluation framework for interactive visual grounding in large vision-language models (LVLMs), varying how much target information is provided upfront and how much must be acquired through dialog

summary.core_problem: 现有的视觉定位（Visual Grounding）评测通常将其设定为单轮的静态匹配任务，假设模型一开始就能获得充分的描述信息。但这脱离了真实世界中目标信息往往不完整、有歧义，需要通过多轮交互来确定的实际情况。
summary.importance: 指出了当前 LVLM 在交互式视觉定位任务上的严重缺陷。这说明仅靠静态图文匹配预训练无法赋予模型在多轮对话中主动获取信息、修正理解的能力，对未来多模态预训练中如何引入交互式数据和目标有启发。
summary.technical_approach: 提出了一个控制变量的交互式视觉定位评测框架。框架包含四个交互协议，逐步减少初始提供的目标信息量：Static（单轮静态匹配）、Full（提供完整描述，允许可选追问）、Partial（提供部分属性，必须追问）、None（无初始描述，完全依赖模型主动提问构建目标表征）。
summary.experiments: 在 8 个 LVLM 上进行了 38,848 次目标选择实验。结果表明，即使在提供额外目标信息的情况下，当前模型的表现也远低于人类基线。模型能够利用后续问题来完善或修复初始描述，但在完全依赖主动提问的 None 协议下表现最差，尽管它们问了最多的问题。此外，模型报告的置信度经常高于实际准确率。
summary.reading_guide: 重点关注 Figure 2 中四种交互协议的设计，以及实验部分不同协议下模型准确率和提问率的对比。可以思考为什么模型在主动提问获取信息（None 协议）时表现如此糟糕，这反映了当前预训练范式在哪些方面的缺失。

summary_en.core_problem: Current visual grounding evaluations typically frame the task as a single-turn static matching problem, assuming the model receives a sufficiently informative description upfront. This ignores the reality that real-world target information is often incomplete, ambiguous, and requires multi-turn interaction to establish.
summary_en.importance: Highlights severe deficiencies in current LVLMs for interactive visual grounding. This suggests that static image-text matching pretraining alone is insufficient for endowing models with the ability to proactively seek information and revise understanding in multi-turn dialogues, offering insights for incorporating interactive data and objectives in future multimodal pretraining.
summary_en.technical_approach: Introduces a controlled evaluation framework for interactive visual grounding. The framework features four interaction protocols that progressively reduce the initial target information provided: Static (single-turn matching), Full (complete description provided, optional follow-up questions allowed), Partial (partial attributes provided, follow-up questions required), and None (no initial description, relying entirely on the model's proactive questioning to build target representations).
summary_en.experiments: Conducted 38,848 target selections across 8 LVLMs. Results show that even with additional target information, current models perform significantly below human baselines. Models can use follow-up questions to refine or repair initial descriptions but struggle most under the None protocol, despite asking the most questions. Furthermore, models' reported confidence frequently exceeds their empirical accuracy.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on the design of the four interaction protocols in Figure 2 and the comparison of model accuracy and question rates across different protocols in the experiments section. Consider why models perform so poorly when proactively asking questions (None protocol) and what this reveals about the shortcomings of current pretraining paradigms.

recommendation.zh: 指出了当前 VLM 在交互式视觉定位（需要主动提问澄清模糊性）上的严重缺陷，这个 benchmark 对后续 VLM 的 post-training（特别是 RL 强化主动探索能力）有指导意义。
recommendation.en: Highlights severe deficiencies of current VLMs in interactive visual grounding (requiring proactive questioning to clarify ambiguity). This benchmark provides guidance for future VLM post-training, especially using RL to enhance proactive exploration capabilities.

paper.title: BenchBench-Protocol: Evaluating Real-World Wet-Lab Protocol Reasoning and Modification
paper.abstract: We introduce BenchBench-Protocol, a benchmark for large language models of 149 protocol-modification tasks recovered from modifications that scientists made to published protocols during real experimental work. Adapting a published protocol to a new experiment is a routine task for a wet-lab scientist, and a correct modification requires accounting for prior choices and downstream steps. Recent life-science benchmarks have moved toward open-ended, rubric-graded tasks, but tasks are typically eli

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作解决的是一个评测问题：现有生命科学 LLM benchmark 虽然越来越开放式，但很多任务是专家“设计出来”的，不一定贴近真实实验室里科学家如何修改 protocol。BenchBench-Protocol 试图用真实工作流中发生过的 protocol 修改记录，构造一个更接近实际科研决策分布的 benchmark，考察模型是否能根据已有 protocol、实验目标和下游依赖，提出合理修改方案。
summary.importance: 对基座预训练研究的直接价值较弱。它不是训练方法、数据配比、优化或建模范式论文，而是一个垂直领域 benchmark。保留它的唯一理由，是它在评测构造上有一点方法论意义：任务不是凭空写，而是从真实版本差异中恢复；rubric 也绑定了具体修改及其 downstream consequences。这种“从真实工作流痕迹反推任务”的做法，对通用 agent 或科研助手评测有参考价值。但如果只从 LLM pretrain 研究视角看，它更接近领域应用评测，不属于优先阅读对象。
summary.technical_approach: 数据构造流程是全文最重要的部分。作者从 Benchling 上科学家修改过的 protocol 版本出发，将其与公开发表的原始 protocol 对比，提取差异；这些差异被转写成第一人称、自然语言风格的 scientist query，同时生成带权重的 rubric，要求回答不仅指出该改什么，还要覆盖相关的下游影响。任务覆盖九个湿实验生物学领域，共 149 个任务，来自 96 个已发表 protocol。每个任务至少经过两位相关领域 PhD 且有三年以上实验经验的科学家独立审阅，审查维度包括问题相关性、科学正确性、rubric 推理深度、rubric 科学准确性和整体质量，只有高评分样本被保留。评测时，模型可使用互联网搜索工具，输出自由文本答案；评分采用 LLM-as-a-judge，对 rubric 中每个 criterion 单独打 0/1/2 分，再按权重汇总成归一化分数。作者还做了 grader 一致性检查，并限制评分尺度较粗，以提高 judge 稳定性。
summary.experiments: 实验评估了 9 个模型，包括 Claude Opus 5、GPT-5.6 系列、Gemini 3.6 Flash、Grok 4.5、Kimi K3、GLM 5.2 和 Inkling。每个任务采样 10 次，若回答格式错误或拒答则记 0 分，并单独统计 invalid-response rate。模型输入包括 query、原始 protocol 和互联网访问权限；闭源模型使用各自原生搜索工具，开源模型通过 Exa 搜索。结果汇总为 0 到 1 的 normalized rubric score。就全文可见内容看，作者更强调 benchmark 构造质量和评分协议，而不是某个模型显著领先多少；关键实验信息在于：1）任务是真实 protocol 修改恢复而来，而非专家虚构；2）rubric 是加权、逐项评分，减少开放式回答评测的随意性；3）做了 grader model 间一致性验证。若关心具体模型排名和不同 intent/domain 的分项表现，需要看表格和附录，因为当前提供的正文片段没有完整数值。
summary.reading_guide: 如果只是判断是否值得读，先看 Introduction 和 Benchmark Design。重点不是模型结果，而是任务来源是否真实、rubric 是否可操作、审稿流程是否足够严。再看 Experimental Setup，确认 tool-use 配置、judge 方案和多次采样协议。预计 10–15 分钟可以完成一次泛读。若只从基座研究角度出发，可以把它当作一个“真实工作流评测构造案例”来看，不必深读全部生物学任务细节。真正值得留意的是任务恢复方式和 weighted rubric 设计，而不是生命科学本身。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses an evaluation problem rather than a modeling one. Many recent life-science LLM benchmarks are open-ended, but the tasks are often written by experts from scratch and may not reflect how scientists actually modify protocols during real lab work. BenchBench-Protocol tries to recover tasks from real protocol edits, so the benchmark measures whether a model can adapt an existing protocol while accounting for prior choices and downstream experimental consequences.
summary_en.importance: Its direct relevance to foundation-model pretraining is limited. This is not a paper about training objectives, data mixture, optimization, scaling, or model architecture. It is a domain-specific benchmark. The part that may still interest LLM researchers is the benchmark-construction methodology: tasks are reconstructed from real workflow traces rather than invented, and the rubric is tied to concrete modifications and their downstream dependencies. That design could be useful for future agent or scientific-assistant evaluation. Still, from a pretraining-centered perspective, this is not a priority read.
summary_en.technical_approach: The main contribution is the dataset and evaluation protocol. The authors start from protocol versions modified by scientists on Benchling and compare them against published source protocols. The observed differences are converted into first-person scientist queries and weighted rubrics. A correct answer is expected not only to propose the modification itself, but also to address downstream implications. The benchmark contains 149 tasks derived from 96 published protocols across nine wet-lab biology domains. Each task is reviewed by at least two independent scientists with a relevant PhD and at least three years of bench experience. Review criteria include question relevance, scientific soundness, rubric reasoning depth, rubric scientific accuracy, and overall quality; only high-quality tasks are retained. During evaluation, models receive the query, the source protocol, and internet access, and produce a free-form answer. Scoring is done with an LLM judge that evaluates each rubric criterion separately on a 0/1/2 scale, then aggregates with criterion weights into a normalized score. The paper also reports grader-consistency checks and intentionally uses a coarse scoring scale to improve judge stability.
summary_en.experiments: Nine models are evaluated, including Claude Opus 5, the GPT-5.6 family, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Grok 4.5, Kimi K3, GLM 5.2, and Inkling. Each task is attempted ten times. Invalid outputs, such as formatting failures or refusals, are assigned zero and tracked separately. Models are given the query, the published protocol, and web access; proprietary models use their native search tools, while open models use Exa. Performance is reported as a normalized weighted-rubric score between 0 and 1. From the available text, the paper emphasizes benchmark quality and evaluation protocol more than headline model gaps. The key empirical points are: (1) tasks come from real protocol modifications rather than synthetic expert-authored prompts, (2) scoring is criterion-wise and weighted, which makes open-ended evaluation more structured, and (3) grader agreement was checked across representative judge models. For exact model rankings and breakdowns by intent or biology domain, the tables and appendices would need to be consulted, since the provided text does not include the full numeric results.
summary_en.reading_guide: If the goal is triage, read the Introduction and Benchmark Design first. The important question is not which model wins, but whether the task source is genuinely realistic, whether the rubric is operational, and whether expert review is strong enough. Then read the Experimental Setup to understand tool-use conditions, the judge protocol, and the repeated-sampling design. A useful skim should take about 10–15 minutes. From a foundation-model perspective, it is best treated as a case study in realistic workflow-grounded benchmark construction rather than as a biology paper to study in depth. The most transferable ideas are the task-recovery pipeline and the weighted rubric design.

recommendation.zh: 看它的“diff→加权 rubric”构造法：比专家拍脑袋出题更干净；但领域偏湿实验，先确认你的 eval 需求再投入复现。
recommendation.en: Focus on the diff-to-weighted-rubric construction—it’s cleaner than expert-elicited prompts; domain is wet-lab heavy, so validate fit before investing in reproduction.

paper.title: OmniJudge or OmniBias? Diagnosing Multimodal Judges through Balanced, Decoupled Lenses
paper.abstract: Multimodal understanding models that can jointly judge text-to-image (T2I), text-to-video (T2V) and text-to-speech (TTS) generation are increasingly used as "OmniJudges" for evaluation and automatic annotation. How reliably they understand what they score remains unclear, since existing benchmarks and training data tend to overemphasize positive examples and to conflate distinct failure modes, so a judge may score well without recognizing failures while its capability gaps stay hidden. Motivated

summary.core_problem: 现有多模态 judge / reward model 评测容易高估模型能力。原因是样本分布偏向正例和高质量输出，且多个失败模式常被混在一个总分里。模型即使不会识别细粒度错误，也可能靠数据先验拿到不错分数。D3-Omni 要诊断的是：OmniJudge 在 T2I、T2V、TTS 三类生成结果上，是否真正理解它正在打分的维度。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的直接价值在于评测信号质量。多模态 judge 正在被用于自动标注、偏好数据构造、reward model 训练和蒸馏教师。如果 judge 对中等质量样本、罕见错误或特定模态存在系统偏差，后续 SFT/RL 数据会把这些偏差放大。D3-Omni 的贡献不是提出更强模型，而是把 judge 评测从粗粒度偏好准确率推进到平衡、可归因的诊断评测。它对构造多模态 post-train 数据和 reward 数据尤其有参考意义。
summary.technical_approach: 方法核心是平衡和解耦。D3-Omni 覆盖 T2I、T2V、TTS 三个任务，共 53 个正交二分类维度，分别为 17、22、14 个维度；样本总数 10,671，三类任务分别为 3,526、1,998、5,147。每个维度尽量控制正负样本比例，同时覆盖不同总质量区间，避免模型通过“多数样本是好样本”这一先验获得虚高准确率。它没有简单重新生成一批媒体样本，而是围绕已有生成结果进行维度化构造、模型辅助过滤、一致性检查和人工核验，把人工成本集中在质量控制上。评测时不只看总分，还看各分数区间的 segment accuracy，以及预测总分相对期望分数的偏差，用来区分 Yes-bias 和 No-bias。
summary.experiments: 实验主要评估多个闭源和开源 omni / multimodal judge。图 1 给出几个稳定现象。第一，T2I、T2V、TTS 上的分段准确率都呈 U 形：低分和高分样本相对容易，中间质量区间明显变难。这说明 judge 对“局部正确但有细节错误”的样本识别不足。第二，TTS 最弱，最高配置 Qwen3.5-Omni-Plus 的整体 segment accuracy 为 65.7%，Gemini-3.1-Pro 为 60.7%，Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash 为 60.4%，Gemini-3-Flash 为 60.2%。T2I 和 T2V 表现较高，但仍不稳：T2I 中 Gemini-3.1-Pro 为 78.6%，Gemini-3.5-Flash 为 77.6%，Gemini-3-Flash 为 77.5%；T2V 中 Gemini-3.5-Flash 为 76.7%，Gemini-3.1-Pro 为 76.0%，Gemini-3-Flash 为 75.2%。第三，总分偏差曲线显示不同模型存在系统性 Yes-bias 或 No-bias，且偏差随期望分数区间变化，不是一个简单可校准的常数偏移。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读，约 20–30 分钟。重点看 introduction 中关于为什么 judge benchmark 需要分布平衡的论证，以及 benchmark construction 部分对“balanced”和“decoupled”的具体定义。图 1 是最关键结果，能快速看到中间分数区间退化和模态差异。若关心多模态 reward data，可以再看维度 taxonomy、样本构造流程和偏差度量方式。对基座预训练本身没有训练 recipe 层面的新方法，但对评估自动标注器和 reward model 的可靠性有实际参考。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing evaluations of multimodal judge and reward models can overestimate judging ability. The main issue is distributional bias: datasets are often dominated by positive or high-quality samples, while different failure modes are collapsed into a single score. A model can look accurate without detecting fine-grained errors. D3-Omni asks whether omni-modal judges actually understand the T2I, T2V, and TTS outputs they score.
summary_en.importance: The work matters for the quality of training signals. Multimodal judges are increasingly used for automatic annotation, preference labeling, reward modeling, and distillation. If these judges miss mid-quality failures or show modality-specific bias, SFT and RL pipelines can inherit and amplify those errors. The contribution is an evaluation asset rather than a new model: it turns judge evaluation into a balanced, diagnosable, dimension-level measurement problem.
summary_en.technical_approach: D3-Omni is built around balance and decoupling. It covers T2I, T2V, and TTS with 53 orthogonal binary dimensions, split into 17, 22, and 14 dimensions. The benchmark contains 10,671 samples: 3,526 for T2I, 1,998 for T2V, and 5,147 for TTS. Each dimension is designed to maintain positive-negative parity and to cover different score intervals, so that a judge cannot rely on the prior that most generations are acceptable. Instead of regenerating all outputs, the construction process uses dimension-oriented sample assembly, model-assisted filtering, consistency checks, and targeted human verification. Evaluation reports segment accuracy across score ranges and total-score deviation, which exposes Yes-bias and No-bias rather than hiding them behind one aggregate number.
summary_en.experiments: The experiments evaluate a range of closed and open omni-modal judges. Figure 1 shows three useful patterns. First, segment accuracy follows a U shape in T2I, T2V, and TTS: very low- and high-quality samples are easier, while mid-score samples are much harder. This is exactly the regime where local errors are embedded in otherwise plausible outputs. Second, TTS remains the weakest modality. The best reported TTS segment accuracy is 65.7% for Qwen3.5-Omni-Plus, followed by Gemini-3.1-Pro at 60.7%, Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash at 60.4%, and Gemini-3-Flash at 60.2%. T2I and T2V are higher but still imperfect: Gemini-3.1-Pro reaches 78.6% on T2I, while Gemini-3.5-Flash reaches 76.7% on T2V. Third, total-score deviation plots reveal systematic Yes-bias or No-bias, and the bias changes across score intervals rather than behaving like a constant calibration error.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 20–30 minutes. The most useful parts are the motivation for balanced judge benchmarks, the exact definition of balanced and decoupled dimensions, and Figure 1. Readers working on multimodal reward data should also inspect the dimension taxonomy, sample construction pipeline, and score-deviation metrics. The work does not provide a new pretraining recipe, but it is useful for auditing the reliability of automatic annotators and reward models.

recommendation.zh: 做多模态自动标注或 judge 训练的人可以看；它不改预训练范式，但 benchmark 设计很干净，适合拿来检查你家的 reward/judge 是否只学会了偏置。
recommendation.en: Worth a skim if you train multimodal judges or use them for auto-labeling; it will not change pretraining priors, but the benchmark design is clean and useful for exposing shortcut-heavy reward models.

paper.title: SA-Bench: Evaluating Semantic Alignment in LLM-Based Paper Reproduction
paper.abstract: LLM agents can generate paper reproduction code, yet often produce scientifically unfaithful implementations. We define this failure mode as semantic drift, where generated code silently diverges from the paper's specifications. We introduce SemanticAlign-Bench(SA-Bench), a diagnostic benchmark covering 30 papers from ICLR, ICML and NeurIPS 2025. For each paper, we decompose its specifications into atomic and verifiable implementation claims, which we call Semantic Alignment Units (SAUs) and eva

summary.core_problem: LLM coding agent 在复现机器学习论文时，常能生成可运行代码，却没有忠实实现论文规格。SA-Bench 把这种问题定义为 semantic drift，即代码在数值、方法、实验协议或执行顺序上悄悄偏离论文描述。
summary.importance: 这项工作对基座研究的价值在于评估长上下文代码 agent 的真实任务理解能力。论文复现不是普通代码补全，模型需要从正文、公式、表格、附录中抽取分散规格，并把它们转成一致的工程实现。这个能力与长文档理解、代码生成、科学推理和 agent scaffold 的设计都有关系。SA-Bench 的启发是：只看代码能否运行或结果是否接近，不能定位科学实现是否忠实；需要把论文规格拆成可验证的原子实现声明，再逐条检查。
summary.technical_approach: SA-Bench 将 paper-to-code 复现评测形式化为静态的 claim-level scoring。输入是一篇论文 P 和一个生成的代码仓库 R，输出是论文级 Semantic Alignment Score 以及每个 claim 的诊断判断。核心单元是 Semantic Alignment Unit，简称 SAU。每个 SAU 必须满足三点：能定位到论文中的具体来源片段；能通过静态代码检查验证；只描述一个独立实现决策。漂移类型分为四类：D1 Numerical Precision，关注超参数、阈值、结构维度；D2 Method / Formula，关注算法步骤、公式和组件接口；D3 Protocol，关注数据处理、训练设置和实验规范；D4 Ordering，关注操作执行顺序。评分不执行代码，而是使用面向不同维度的 LLM judge，按五级 rubric 给出判断。这种设计牺牲了端到端行为验证，但减少了随机种子、环境、算力和数据处理差异带来的混淆。
summary.experiments: 基准包含 30 篇来自 ICLR、ICML、NeurIPS 2025 的论文，覆盖五个机器学习领域和六类研究范式。标注得到 1,491 个经过人工核验的 SAU。实验评估 12 种生成配置，即 4 个模型乘以 3 个 scaffold，共 360 个 paper-level evaluation。主要结论是 semantic drift 在所有配置中都系统存在；面向 executability 优化的 scaffold 对科学复现忠实度帮助有限。换言之，让仓库能跑起来并不等价于实现了论文声称的方法。给出的分类结果还显示，不同漂移类型需要分开看，否则单一总分会掩盖是超参数误读、公式实现错误，还是实验协议偏离。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读，约 25–35 分钟。重点看第 3 节对 SAU 的定义、四类 drift taxonomy，以及 extraction / judging pipeline。Table 1 有助于理解它与 PaperBench、SciCoQA 等工作的差异。若做 coding agent 或 paper-to-code 系统，建议细看 Appendix B.1 的 SAU 标注 schema 和 Appendix C 的 taxonomy 来源。对预训练研究员来说，最有用的是它把“长文档规格理解”拆成可监督、可诊断原子单元的方法，而不是最终 leaderboard 数字。

summary_en.core_problem: LLM coding agents can produce executable repositories for paper reproduction, but the code often fails to implement the paper faithfully. SA-Bench names this failure mode semantic drift: silent divergence from the paper specification in numerical values, method logic, experimental protocol, or execution order.
summary_en.importance: The benchmark is useful for studying long-context code agents and scientific task understanding. Paper reproduction requires a model to gather scattered specifications from methods, equations, tables, and appendices, then translate them into a coherent implementation. This is closer to specification grounding than ordinary code generation. The key lesson is that executability and aggregate reproduction results are not enough; scientific fidelity needs claim-level verification against the source paper.
summary_en.technical_approach: SA-Bench formulates paper-to-code evaluation as static claim-level scoring. Given a paper P and a generated repository R, the system outputs a paper-level Semantic Alignment Score and per-claim diagnostic judgments. The basic unit is the Semantic Alignment Unit, or SAU. An SAU must be localizable to a source span in the paper, verifiable by static code inspection, and atomic enough to represent one independent implementation decision. The taxonomy covers four drift types: D1 Numerical Precision for hyperparameters, thresholds, and architectural dimensions; D2 Method / Formula for algorithmic steps, equations, and component interfaces; D3 Protocol for data processing, training setup, and experimental rules; and D4 Ordering for procedural sequence. The evaluation uses dimension-specific LLM judges with a five-level rubric, without executing the repository. This avoids confounding from seeds, environments, compute budgets, and dataset variations, although it cannot replace behavioral testing.
summary_en.experiments: The benchmark contains 30 papers from ICLR, ICML, and NeurIPS 2025, spanning five ML domains and six research paradigms. It includes 1,491 human-verified SAU claims. The evaluation covers 12 generator configurations, formed by 4 models and 3 scaffolds, for 360 paper-level evaluations. The reported finding is that semantic drift appears systematically across all configurations. Scaffolds optimized for executability provide limited improvement in scientific fidelity. In practice, a repository that runs can still miss the claimed algorithm, use the wrong numerical setting, or follow a different protocol. The four-way taxonomy is therefore important because a single score would hide the type of failure.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 25–35 minutes. Focus on Section 3 for the SAU definition, the drift taxonomy, and the extraction and judging pipeline. Table 1 is useful for comparing the benchmark with PaperBench and related paper-to-code evaluations. For coding-agent researchers, Appendix B.1 on the annotation schema and Appendix C on the taxonomy construction are the most actionable parts. For pretraining researchers, the main value is the decomposition of long-document specification understanding into verifiable atomic units.

recommendation.zh: 把“复现”从跑通提升到“规格对齐”是对的；直接看 SAU 的定义与四类 drift 统计，能校准你对 coding agent 评测的预期。
recommendation.en: Good move: reproduction should be spec-alignment, not just runnable code; read the SAU formulation and drift breakdown to recalibrate coding-agent evaluation.

paper.title: Evaluating Multiple LLM Generations with Validated Task Coverage
paper.abstract: Many LLM applications are most useful when they provide several candidate outputs for comparison, validation, or combination. Predominant evaluation settings, however, still focus on individual outputs or reduce multiple samples to a single success or selected answer. This can miss whether the outputs include several genuinely different useful results. We introduce VTC-Bench, a five-domain benchmark for this setting, together with Validated Task Coverage (VTC) as its core evaluation quantity. Th

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解决的是：当 LLM 一次生成多个候选答案时，传统评测通常只看单样本质量或 top-1 成功，无法衡量这些候选是否覆盖了多个真正有用且彼此不同的解。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是 benchmark + metric。它把“多次采样的价值”从单次命中率扩展到 coverage，适合评估 diverse decoding、best-of-n、sample-and-rerank 这类推理策略。对预训练研究员的价值主要在评测视角，而不是训练方法本身。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 VTC-Bench 和核心指标 Validated Task Coverage (VTC)。VTC 统计在 k 次尝试内获得了多少个既有用、又在任务意义上彼此不同的结果。数据集覆盖五个领域，强调自动、可复现的验证，不依赖 model-based judge，从而尽量减少评测噪声和 judge 偏置。
summary.experiments: 摘要没有给出具体模型名单和数值，但明确比较了多种模型与 inference setting，并指出 VTC 与传统单次质量评测会得出不同结论：单次最强的配置，不一定在多样性覆盖上最好。实验价值主要在揭示 decoding / sampling 策略的排序变化。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a gap in LLM evaluation: when models produce multiple candidates, standard metrics focus on single-output quality or top-1 success and miss whether the set covers several genuinely useful and distinct solutions.
summary_en.importance: This is a benchmark-and-metric contribution. It reframes the value of multi-sample generation in terms of coverage, which is relevant for diverse decoding, best-of-n, and sample-and-rerank settings. For pretraining researchers, the value is mostly evaluative rather than methodological.
summary_en.technical_approach: The work introduces VTC-Bench and the metric Validated Task Coverage (VTC). VTC measures how many useful and task-relevantly distinct outputs are obtained within k attempts. The benchmark spans five domains and is designed so that both usefulness and distinctness can be checked automatically and reproducibly, without model-based judges.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract does not report model lists or exact numbers, but it states that multiple models and inference settings are compared and that VTC changes the ranking relative to conventional single-draw evaluation. The main empirical takeaway is that the best one-shot configuration is not necessarily the best for useful coverage.

recommendation.zh: 如果你在做 best-of-n、采样温度或 rerank，这个 metric 值得记住；但它主要改评测口径，不直接回答训练该怎么改，读定义和主表即可。
recommendation.en: Useful if you work on best-of-n, sampling temperature, or reranking; it mainly changes the evaluation lens rather than training, so the metric definition and main table are enough.

paper.title: Beyond Factual Knowledge: Benchmarking and Learning Step-Level Procedural Rule Reasoning in Large Language Models
paper.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) excel at text understanding and generation, yet still struggle to reliably understand and apply externally provided procedural rules at scale. To evaluate this capability, we introduce RuleWorld, a large-scale benchmark that reformulates rules as globally reusable abstract units rather than instance-specific facts. In RuleWorld, several scenarios, including single-rule, parallel multi-rule, and multi-hop reasoning, are settled for comprehensive evaluation. We further

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的是一个常被现有知识评测忽略的问题：模型能否从一个大规模、共享、可复用的外部规则库里，先找对规则，再按步骤稳定地应用规则完成推理。以往很多 rule reasoning benchmark 会把相关规则直接作为当前样本的前提给出来，模型更像是在做局部条件推理，而不是在一个外部程序性知识库中做定位、检索、组合和状态更新。RuleWorld 把规则设计成抽象、非实体绑定、可跨样本复用的 procedural units，并且让结论继续作为其他规则的前提，逼迫模型同时解决两个难点：一是抽象规则与问题表面的弱匹配，二是多步推理中目标规则会随中间状态变化而变化，导致一次性检索或静态注入都不稳定。
summary.importance: 对基座研究的意义主要不在“规则推理”这个任务名义上，而在它把外部知识注入、内部检索、KV 级记忆操作和 step-wise decoding 绑在了一起。它提供了一个比较干净的测试床，用来研究：当外部知识不是事实片段，而是需要按步骤调用的程序性规则时，现有 RAG、一次性 memory injection、普通 CoT 为什么会失效。这个问题和预训练接口是相关的，因为很多未来系统并不只依赖参数内化知识，而要在推理时调用大规模外部 memory。DynaRule 的价值在于提出了一种“把检索变成模型内部可学习过程”的实现路径：不是先检索再生成，也不是把所有规则静态塞进去，而是在解码过程中用 <search> 触发重新注意和 KV 更新。这个设计对研究 test-time memory、tool-like retrieval token、以及训练期如何让模型学会分步调用外部知识，都有启发。若从贡献量级看，benchmark 本身比方法更稳；方法展示了明确增益，但更像一个有研究味道的原型，而不是已经成熟的通用范式。
summary.technical_approach:
方法分成 benchmark 和模型两部分。RuleWorld 侧，作者构造了 494 万条规则，覆盖 Attributes、Environments、Actions、States 四大类、七个子类，并同时提供 FOL 与自然语言版本。任务分成 Single-Rule、Parallel Multi-Rule、Multi-Hop Rule 三类，共 11 个子任务。设计上的关键点有三个。第一，规则是抽象模板，带占位符，需要先做 grounding，不能靠记忆世界知识蒙对。第二，规则库是共享的，不是每题单独附带的 hint。第三，规则之间可组合，前一步结论会改变后续可用规则集合。

DynaRule 侧，核心思路是把外部规则编码后直接注入 LLM 的 KV cache，并把“何时重新检索、检索哪些规则”做成解码过程中的内部动作。具体做法是：先用预训练句向量编码器把规则编码成向量，再通过单层 adapter 对齐到目标 LLM 的表示空间，然后作为可被注意到的外部 memory 注入若干层的 KV。训练分两阶段。第一阶段先找 confidence layer，也就是对注入规则的注意力熵最低的层；作者把它视为模型最能做出稀疏、确定性规则选择的层。第二阶段在该层做 Stacked Step-Level Attention Training，引入特殊 token <search>。这个 token 的作用不是输出内容，而是触发一次针对规则库的重新注意，让模型在当前推理步重新选择相关规则，并用新选中的规则替换 KV 中过时的条目。这样做的区别在于：传统 RAG 在生成前或少数固定位置检索，检索误差会一路传递；静态 KV 注入虽然避免了外部检索延迟，但目标规则一旦随中间状态变化，就容易被早期注意模式锁死。DynaRule 试图把检索和推理耦合成一个 step-level 闭环。

从机制上看，<search> 更像一种显式的 latent action。它把“需要外部规则支持”这个决策暴露到 token 序列中，再用监督去塑造该动作对应的注意力分布。这个点比单纯加一个 retrieval head 更有意思，因为它直接作用于生成轨迹，而不是只作用于前置检索模块。
summary.experiments:
实验结论很明确：RuleWorld 对现有强模型是困难的，尤其在大规则库和多步场景下。文中给出的关键数字包括：DynaRule 在多种规则注入设置下，平均 QA accuracy 最多提升 19 个点；在某些具体子任务上，提升可达 48 个点。检索指标上，在 10K rules 规模下，Recall@10 超过 90%，Recall@1 超过 85%，比最强基线高 60 多个点。这说明它不仅最终答案更好，前端规则定位本身也更稳。

更值得注意的是实验结构，而不只是 headline 数字。作者比较了 RAG 类方法、内部注入类方法以及自己的动态更新方案。结果显示，当规则是抽象模板、与问题表面词汇弱匹配时，文本检索很脆弱；而当任务进入 parallel aggregation 或 multi-hop state tracking 时，一次性注入会明显退化，因为不同步骤需要的规则集合在变化。消融里，confidence layer 的选择、<search> token 的引入、以及 step-level attention training 都是有效组件。若去掉动态重注意或不做分步训练，性能会明显下降。另一个重要观察是，随着规则库规模增大，基线方法退化更快，而 DynaRule 的退化更缓，说明它的优势主要来自“在大候选集里稳定缩小注意范围”，而不只是多加了一个外部 memory。

不过也要看到边界。文中最强结果主要建立在合成规则世界上，规则语义是可控的、形式化程度较高。它证明了方法在程序性知识调用上的可行性，但离真实企业 policy、复杂文档规章、跨文档冲突规则还有距离。另一个潜在问题是，规则编码器和 adapter 的质量会成为瓶颈；如果规则表达更长、更噪声、更依赖上下文，当前方案未必还能维持这么高的检索精度。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议是先看 Introduction 里对 benchmark 设计缺口的界定，再看 Figure 1 理解 RuleWorld 的任务结构，随后直接看方法图和训练流程。最值得看的部分有四处。第一，RuleWorld 的规则组织方式，以及为什么“共享规则库 + 抽象占位符 + 可组合结论”比传统 premise-given benchmark 更难。第二，confidence layer 的定义和选择依据，这关系到作者对“哪一层最适合做外部规则选择”的判断。第三，<search> token 如何触发 re-attention 与 KV replacement，这是方法真正的核心。第四，主结果表和检索结果表，要把 QA accuracy 和 Recall 指标一起看，才能分清是检索错了，还是检索对了但推理没用好。

如果时间有限，预计 20 到 30 分钟可以完成有效泛读：看引言、方法总览图、主表、关键消融。若要深挖，建议重点追问两个问题：一是 <search> 的监督信号如何构造，是否会引入 teacher forcing 式偏差；二是 KV replacement 的实现细节，是否存在覆盖掉仍然有用规则、导致长程依赖丢失的问题。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper targets a gap that most rule-reasoning evaluations avoid: whether an LLM can localize the right rules from a large shared repository and then apply them reliably across reasoning steps. Prior benchmarks usually attach the relevant rules directly to each instance, so the model mostly performs conditional reasoning over provided premises. That setup does not test reusable procedural knowledge. RuleWorld changes this by making rules abstract, entity-independent, and globally shared across examples. It also makes rule conclusions feed into later rules, so the model must handle both weak surface matching and step-dependent rule selection as intermediate states evolve.
summary_en.importance: Its value for foundation-model research is less about the task label and more about the interface it exposes between external memory and generation. The benchmark is a clean testbed for studying why standard RAG, static memory injection, and plain chain-of-thought break when the external knowledge is procedural rather than factual. This matters for pretraining-adjacent research because future systems will likely rely on external memory that must be queried during decoding, not only on parametric knowledge. DynaRule is interesting because it turns retrieval into an internal learned process: rules are injected into KV cache, and a special token triggers step-wise re-attention and memory refresh. That is relevant to test-time memory, retrieval-trigger tokens, and training schemes that teach models to call external knowledge incrementally. The benchmark contribution feels more durable than the method itself; the method shows a clear gain, but still reads more like a strong research prototype than a settled general recipe.
summary_en.technical_approach:
There are two parts: the benchmark and the model. RuleWorld contains 4.94M rules spanning four major types and seven subtypes, with both first-order logic and natural-language forms. It defines Single-Rule QA, Parallel Multi-Rule QA, and Multi-Hop Rule QA, yielding 11 sub-tasks. The benchmark design matters for three reasons. First, rules are abstract templates with placeholders, so the model must ground them before use. Second, the rule repository is shared globally rather than attached per question. Third, rules are compositional, so earlier conclusions alter what becomes relevant later.

DynaRule injects encoded external rules directly into the LLM’s KV cache and makes re-retrieval part of decoding. Rules are first embedded by a pretrained sentence encoder, then mapped into the LLM space with a lightweight adapter, and finally exposed as external memory in the KV cache. Training has two stages. In stage one, the method identifies a confidence layer, defined as the layer where attention entropy over injected rules is minimized. The intuition is that this layer exhibits the sharpest and most decisive rule selection. In stage two, the model performs Stacked Step-Level Attention Training on that layer using a special <search> token. Emitting <search> triggers re-attention over the rule memory, selects a new subset of relevant rules, and replaces outdated entries in the KV cache.

This differs from standard RAG, where retrieval is front-loaded and retrieval errors propagate through the whole generation, and from static memory injection, where the model can get stuck with early-selected rules even when later reasoning steps require different ones. Mechanistically, <search> acts like an explicit latent action: it externalizes the decision that the model needs fresh procedural support, and supervision shapes the attention pattern associated with that action. That is more interesting than adding a separate retrieval head, because it is integrated into the token-level generation trajectory.
summary_en.experiments:
The empirical message is clear: RuleWorld is hard for current strong models, especially with large rule sets and multi-step reasoning. The headline numbers reported in the paper are substantial. DynaRule improves average QA accuracy by up to 19 points across rule-injection settings, and by as much as 48 points on some sub-tasks. On retrieval, at 10K rules it achieves over 90% Recall@10 and over 85% Recall@1, beating the strongest baseline by more than 60 points.

The more important part is how the experiments are structured. The paper compares RAG-style baselines, internal injection baselines, and the proposed dynamic update mechanism. When rules are abstract and only weakly aligned with the query surface form, text retrieval becomes brittle. When tasks require parallel aggregation or multi-hop state tracking, one-shot injection degrades sharply because the relevant rule set changes across steps. Ablations show that the confidence-layer choice, the <search> token, and step-level attention training all matter. Removing dynamic re-attention or skipping step-wise supervision causes clear drops. Another useful observation is scaling behavior: as the rule repository grows, baseline performance degrades faster, while DynaRule degrades more gracefully. That suggests the gain comes from stable narrowing of attention over a large candidate set, not merely from adding extra memory.

There are also limits. The strongest results are obtained in a synthetic rule world with controlled semantics and relatively formal structure. This is enough to demonstrate feasibility for procedural knowledge use, but it is still some distance from real policy documents, noisy enterprise rules, or conflicting cross-document regulations. A second likely bottleneck is the rule encoder plus adapter. If rules become longer, noisier, or more context-dependent, the current setup may not preserve the same retrieval quality.
summary_en.reading_guide:
For a skim pass, start with the introduction and Figure 1 to understand why the benchmark is harder than premise-given rule QA. Then jump to the method overview and the training pipeline. Four parts deserve attention. First, the benchmark construction: shared repository, abstract placeholders, and compositional rules are the real source of difficulty. Second, the definition of the confidence layer, because it reveals the authors’ view of where external rule selection should happen inside the network. Third, the exact role of the <search> token in re-attention and KV replacement; that is the core mechanism. Fourth, read the QA tables together with the retrieval tables, otherwise it is hard to separate retrieval failure from reasoning failure.

A useful skim should take around 20 to 30 minutes: introduction, method figure, main tables, and key ablations. If reading more carefully, two questions are worth tracking. How is supervision for <search> constructed, and does it introduce teacher-forcing bias?
