And how exactly is KV replacement implemented, especially when previously selected rules may still be useful later?

recommendation.zh: 读 benchmark 设定和 <search> 训练即可；若数字扎实，它是研究规则进 KV 状态的好 ablation 起点。
recommendation.en: Read the benchmark setup and the <search>-based training; if the numbers hold, it is a useful ablation seed for rules-as-KV-state.

paper.title: Beyond What Meets the Eye: Unveiling Situational Illusions for Multimodal Large Language Models
paper.abstract: Real-world situation appearances can deviate from their underlying physical states, challenging the reliability of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in practical applications. In this paper, we term this phenomenon situational illusions and investigate: (1) how MLLMs perform under such illusions, and (2) how to mitigate the limitations. We first develop a comprehensive where-what-how taxonomy that characterizes where situational illusions occur, what targets they take, and how they arise.

summary.core_problem: 多模态大语言模型（MLLM）在面对“情境错觉”（Situational Illusions，即视觉表象与底层物理状态不一致的自然场景）时，能否准确理解并做出可靠决策？
summary.importance: 揭示了 MLLM 在真实物理世界感知中的一个关键盲区。与以往关注人为设计的视觉错觉（如几何错觉、对抗样本）不同，本文关注的是自然场景中因遮挡、视角或光影导致的物理状态误判。这对于具身智能和机器人的可靠部署至关重要，属于 VLM 预训练和对齐阶段需要重点关注的鲁棒性问题。
summary.technical_approach: 1) 构建了情境错觉的细粒度分类体系（Where-What-How），涵盖 4 种场景、12 种误判目标和 5 种形成机制。2) 提出了 MSIBench 评测基准，包含 3,723 个图文对，用于评估 MLLM 的错觉辨别、理解和推理能力。3) 探索了缓解策略，包括针对闭源模型的 Prompting 方法和针对开源模型的监督微调（SFT），引导模型关注视觉证据以更准确地解释情境错觉。
summary.experiments: 评估了 27 种模型配置，发现当前 MLLM 极易受情境错觉影响，整体平均准确率低于 63%，在动作规划任务上甚至低于 45%。通过 Prompting 和 SFT 缓解策略，使用有限数据可将模型性能提升高达 20%。
summary.reading_guide: 重点关注 Taxonomy 部分对情境错觉的分类（Property, Relation, Context），以及 MSIBench 的构建逻辑。实验部分可快速浏览各模型在不同错觉类型下的表现差异，重点看 SFT 缓解策略的有效性及局限性。预计阅读时间 15 分钟。

summary_en.core_problem: Can Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) accurately understand and make reliable decisions when faced with 'situational illusions' (natural scenes where visual appearance deviates from the underlying physical state)?
summary_en.importance: Exposes a critical blind spot in MLLMs' perception of the real physical world. Unlike previous work focusing on artificially designed visual illusions (e.g., geometric illusions, adversarial examples), this paper addresses misjudgments of physical states caused by occlusion, perspective, or lighting in natural scenes. This is crucial for the reliable deployment of embodied AI and robotics, and represents a robustness issue that needs significant attention during VLM pre-training and alignment.
summary_en.technical_approach: 1) Develops a fine-grained taxonomy of situational illusions (Where-What-How), covering 4 scenarios, 12 misperceived targets, and 5 formation mechanisms. 2) Introduces MSIBench, a benchmark with 3,723 image-text pairs, to evaluate MLLMs' illusion discrimination, understanding, and reasoning capabilities. 3) Explores mitigation strategies, including prompting for closed-source models and Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) for open-source models, guiding models to attend to visual evidence for more accurate interpretation.
summary_en.experiments: Evaluated 27 model configurations, revealing that current MLLMs are highly vulnerable to situational illusions, with an overall average accuracy below 63%, dropping below 45% for action planning. Mitigation strategies (Prompting and SFT) improved model performance by up to 20% using limited data.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on the Taxonomy section for the classification of situational illusions (Property, Relation, Context) and the construction logic of MSIBench. Briefly review the experimental results to see the performance differences across models and illusion types, paying special attention to the effectiveness and limitations of the SFT mitigation strategy. Estimated reading time: 15 minutes.

recommendation.zh: 多模态预训练可 skim：重点看 taxonomy 和 6 类 failure mode，数据构造比排名更有用。
recommendation.en: Worth skimming for multimodal pretraining; focus on the taxonomy and six failure modes rather than the leaderboard numbers.

paper.title: Repo2Skill-Evo: Repository Skills Go Stale in Silence
paper.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate over evolving software repositories, where success depends on repository-specific procedural knowledge: which APIs to call, which scripts to run, and which conventions the current release expects. Agent skills externalize this knowledge into reusable units, and prior work shows that they can improve agent performance. What remains unclear is whether that improvement is durable. The same version specificity that makes a skill useful also make

summary.core_problem: 当 LLM agent 把“仓库特定的过程性知识”外化成可复用的 skill（例如该跑哪个脚本、该调用哪个 API、遵循什么约定）后，仓库版本迭代会让 skill 在没有显式信号的情况下悄然过期（silent staleness）。论文要解决的是：如何系统性评测并量化 agent 维护这些 versioned skills 的能力，以及失败主要卡在什么环节（定位受影响文件 vs 在文件内选择正确编辑）。
summary.importance:
对预训练研究是间接相关：它不是训练新基座或新目标函数，而是给“长期使用的 agent 知识资产”引入了时间维度与版本漂移问题，并提供了可复现的评测资产。它的价值在于两点：
- 评测层：把 skill 维护定义成严格 patch-grounded 的编辑任务，能更清晰地区分“真的跟随仓库变化修对了”与“写得像但没对齐证据”。
- 训练信号层：这种任务天然对应持续学习/continual adaptation 的数据构造方式（release patch + 旧 skill → 新 skill），未来如果有人用它做 mid-train 或工具使用策略学习，会比泛泛的代码编辑数据更可控。
但就当前论文贡献而言，它更像一个 agent/评测工作，而不是直接推动预训练 scaling 或 tokenizer/数据配比的工作。
summary.technical_approach:
Repo2Skill-Evo 由三块组成：
1) 固定的 V1 skill 集：基于 Repo2Skill 流水线，用 staged distillation + expert refinement 从仓库中提炼过程性知识，形成技能包（SKILL.md + 可选脚本/引用），并记录每条 claim 的 provenance（来源路径、符号等元数据），保证后续能追踪证据。
2) 维护任务定义：给定 V1→V2 的官方 release patch，维护 agent 需要删除或修改已被 patch 证实过期的 skill 行，同时尽量不改动仍然有效的行。这里的关键取舍是：不让模型“重写一遍技能文档”，而是做最小必要编辑，才能测出定位与证据追踪能力。
3) 评测：核心是严格 patch-grounded headline metric——奖励对 patch-verified obsolete lines 的正确删除/修订，惩罚对其他行的编辑；并辅以一个 rubric-based 的自然语言 Judge，从五个维度评估 V2 skill 集质量。
论文进一步把失败拆成两类瓶颈：skill 文件定位不全（coverage 不够导致漏改）与 edit selection 不准（改多了导致 precision 下降）。并用 oracle localization 实验说明：只解决“找对文件”还不够，文件内证据追踪与选择性编辑仍是难点。
summary.experiments:
关键设置与结果（来自全文引言部分给出的数字）：
- 数据规模：57 个仓库、105 个 release transitions；每个 transition 都包含一个固定的 V1 skill 集，并有人/流程标注出 patch-verified 的过期行。过期行数量中位数约 92 行。
- 参评模型/agent：评测了 6 个 frontier agents（具体名单需以正文实验表为准）。
- 主指标：这些 agent 在 avg@3 macro F1 上约 29.9%–69.7%，显示维护并不可靠。
- 诊断实验：在 20 个最难的 transitions 上做 oracle skill-file localization 能提升表现，但仍有显著残余错误，支持“定位之外还有 within-file evidence tracing / edit selection 问题”的结论。
另外，论文还做了一个 utility study：在随机抽取的 10 个仓库上，skills 对 baseline 最弱的任务带来最大绝对增益，暗示维护问题在“原本就不熟仓库”的场景更关键。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议（45–60 分钟）：
- 先读 Introduction 对 silent staleness 的定义与动机，理解为什么“外化知识”会让过期变得不可见。
- 重点看任务与指标定义：patch-grounded headline metric 的奖励/惩罚规则决定了它测的是“选择性维护”而不是“重写能力”。
- 看主结果表：关注不同 agent 的 precision/recall 取舍（论文提到更广泛编辑带来更高 recall 但更低 precision）。
- 看 oracle localization 与错误分析段落：它把问题拆成 localization 与 edit selection 两段，这对后续做数据合成或训练信号设计更有用。
如果你的关注点是 pretrain/posttrain 接口：把它当作一种可控的 continual adaptation 数据形态（patch 驱动的知识更新），思考是否能用来做 mid-train 或工具使用策略的持续训练。

summary_en.core_problem: When LLM agents externalize repository-specific procedural knowledge into reusable “skills”, repository releases can silently invalidate parts of those skills without any explicit signal. The paper studies how to benchmark and diagnose an agent’s ability to maintain versioned repository skills across releases—separating file localization failures from within-file evidence tracing and edit-selection failures.
summary_en.importance:
This is closer to an agent benchmark/maintenance study than a pretraining-method paper. Its relevance to foundation-model researchers is indirect but concrete:
- Evaluation asset: a patch-grounded maintenance protocol that rewards evidence-aligned edits and penalizes unnecessary rewrites, making it harder to “sound plausible” without being correct.
- Training-signal shape: (release patch + old skill → updated skill) is a clean continual-adaptation data form; it could later support mid-training or continual post-training with controllable supervision.
It does not, by itself, advance scaling laws, tokenization, or core pretraining objectives.
summary_en.technical_approach:
Repo2Skill-Evo is built as:
1) A fixed V1 skill set produced by Repo2Skill via staged distillation plus expert refinement. Each skill is packaged (e.g., SKILL.md, optional scripts/references) and augmented with provenance metadata (source paths/symbols) to enable traceability.
2) A maintenance task: given the official V1→V2 release patch, a maintenance agent must delete or revise patch-verified obsolete skill lines while preserving still-valid content. The design intentionally emphasizes minimal, selective edits rather than full regeneration.
3) Evaluation: a strict patch-grounded headline metric that rewards correct edits on verified obsolete lines and penalizes edits elsewhere, plus a rubric-based NL judge with five dimensions for overall quality.
The analysis frames two complementary bottlenecks: incomplete localization of affected skill files (coverage) and imperfect edit selection (precision/within-file evidence tracing). An oracle localization experiment tests how much of the gap is purely localization.
summary_en.experiments:
Reported setup and headline numbers:
- Scale: 57 repositories, 105 release transitions; each transition includes a fixed V1 skill set with patch-verified obsolete-line annotations. Median obsolete content is ~92 lines per transition.
- Models: six frontier agents (exact identities should be checked in the main experiment table).
- Performance: only ~29.9%–69.7% avg@3 macro F1, indicating maintenance is unreliable.
- Diagnostics: oracle skill-file localization on the 20 hardest transitions improves results but leaves substantial residual errors, supporting the claim that within-file evidence tracing and edit selection remain hard.
A utility study on 10 randomly sampled repos suggests skills help most where baseline agent performance is weakest, implying maintenance matters most in low-familiarity settings.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim plan (45–60 min):
- Read the Introduction for the precise definition of “silent staleness” and why externalized skills can decay invisibly.
- Focus on the task/metric section: the patch-grounded scoring rules are the core contribution.
- Check the main results table and look for the precision–recall trade-off pattern (broader edits → higher recall but lower precision).
- Read the oracle localization and error analysis: it cleanly decomposes failures into localization vs edit selection.
If you care about pretrain/post-train interfaces, treat this as a well-scoped continual-update supervision format and consider how it could be used for mid-training or continual post-training.

recommendation.zh: 读任务定义和错误分析即可；它提醒外部 memory 不是免费午餐，版本漂移会把技能变成隐性负资产。
recommendation.en: Read the task definition and error analysis; it is a useful warning that external memory can become a silent liability under version drift.

paper.title: Signal or Noise? A Benchmark Study of Agent Skills in Web Development
paper.abstract: Agent Skills are reusable procedural modules that are increasingly injected into coding-agent sessions to encode framework conventions, anti-patterns, and reusable tools. However, because each injected Skill expands the prompt of every query, an effective Skill benchmark must determine not only whether an agent can solve a task, but whether the Skill should have been injected at all. We introduce WebDev-Skills-Bench and use it for a controlled empirical study of 31 public WebDev Skills on 50 Web

summary.core_problem: 在代码 Agent 中注入可复用的 'Skill'（如框架约定、反模式、工具）会增加所有 prompt 的长度，这是否真的能提升 Web 开发任务的成功率，还是仅仅增加了 token 开销和干扰？
summary.importance: 揭示了 Agent Skill 注入的真实代价。指出当前许多 Skill 评测未分离'内容增益'与'长度干扰'，并证明盲目注入 Skill 往往弊大于利，对 Agent 框架设计和评测标准有重要警示作用。
summary.technical_approach: 构建了 WebDev-Skills-Bench，包含 50 个项目、1000 个任务和 31 个公开 WebDev Skills。核心设计是四种对照条件：C0（无 Skill）、C1（目标 Skill）、C2（长度匹配的无关 Skill，用于分离长度效应）、C3（留一法消融，分析规则、反模式、示例代码的作用）。采用工作区感知注入协议，仅将 SKILL.md 放入 prompt，辅助文件挂载到文件系统，确保长度控制的精确性。
summary.experiments: 在四种模型上，目标注入（C1）导致平均 Pass@2 下降 1.3 到 4.2 个百分点，token 成本增加 72% 到 394%，仅 17% 到 36% 的 (Skill, project) 对有收益。C2 对照表明：Sonnet 和 Qwen 易受长度干扰（无关 Skill 导致类似性能下降），而 GPT-5.1 和 DeepSeek 易受内容误导。C3 消融发现：反模式规则最有效，而示例代码对强模型往往起反作用。
summary.reading_guide: 重点关注 Benchmark Design 中的四种对照条件（C0-C3）设计，以及实验部分关于不同模型对'长度'和'内容'敏感度的差异分析。这对于设计更鲁棒的 Agent prompt 策略很有启发。

summary_en.core_problem: Does injecting reusable 'Skills' (e.g., framework conventions, anti-patterns) into coding agents actually improve success rates on Web development tasks, or does it merely increase token overhead and prompt distraction?
summary_en.importance: Exposes the hidden costs of Agent Skill injection. It highlights that many current Skill evaluations fail to disentangle 'content gain' from 'length distraction', demonstrating that blind injection often does more harm than good. This serves as a crucial warning for Agent framework design and evaluation standards.
summary_en.technical_approach: Introduces WebDev-Skills-Bench, comprising 50 projects, 1,000 tasks, and 31 public WebDev Skills. The core design features four matched conditions: C0 (no Skill), C1 (target Skill), C2 (length-matched irrelevant Skill to isolate length effects), and C3 (leave-one-out ablation to analyze rules, anti-patterns, and example code). It employs a workspace-aware injection protocol, placing only SKILL.md in the prompt while mounting auxiliary files, ensuring precise length control.
summary_en.experiments: Across four models, target injection (C1) resulted in a negative average ΔPass@2 (between -1.3 and -4.2 pp) and increased token costs by 72% to 394%, with only 17% to 36% of (Skill, project) pairs showing gains. The C2 control revealed that Sonnet and Qwen are length-distracted, whereas GPT-5.1 and DeepSeek are content-misled. C3 ablation showed that anti-pattern rules are the most reliable benefit, while example code often hurts stronger models.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on the design of the four matched conditions (C0-C3) in the Benchmark Design section, and the experimental analysis regarding the differing sensitivities of models to 'length' versus 'content'. This offers valuable insights for designing more robust Agent prompt strategies.

recommendation.zh: 一个反直觉的实证研究，证明了给 Agent 强塞 Skill 往往适得其反（掉点且费钱），对设计 Agent 框架的 context 管理有直接警示。
recommendation.en: A counter-intuitive empirical study proving that force-feeding skills to Agents often backfires (performance drop and higher cost), offering a direct warning for context management in Agent framework design.

paper.title: WildHandBench: A Benchmark for Handwritten Text Understanding that Challenges MLLMs and Humans
paper.abstract: While the top model on OmniDocBench now reaches 96.34% overall on printed-document parsing, the ability of current models to handle challenging handwritten documents remains largely uncharacterized. Existing benchmarks focus on isolated text or formulas, overlook handwritten tables and real-world degradation, and report aggregate accuracy without explaining why models fail. We present WildHandBench, a benchmark containing 500 handwritten documents across three structures (free text, tables, form

summary.core_problem: 如何系统评测并解释 MLLM 在真实手写文档理解中的失败模式：不仅要测“识别对不对”，还要区分错误来自视觉证据不足，还是模型过度依赖语言先验（类似 OCR 场景下的“幻觉式补全”）。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的直接贡献不在训练方法，而在“评测信号”：它把手写文档这一长期薄弱区从零散的手写行/字符识别，扩展到更贴近真实应用的三类结构（自由文本/表格/公式）与多语言、多退化场景，并给出可解释的错误归因指标 PDE。对做 VLM/文档理解预训练的人，价值在于：1）明确当前模型在手写场景的上限与短板不是单纯分辨率，而是结构恢复与不确定性建模；2）PDE 把“语言先验压过视觉证据”的问题量化，能反向指导预训练数据配比（手写、低质扫描、表格/公式）、训练目标（抑制无证据补全）、以及解码/校准策略（更保守的 abstain/uncertainty）。整体属于高质量 eval 资产，但对纯文本 LLM 预训练的外溢较弱。
summary.technical_approach:
1）数据与标注设计：WildHandBench 共 500 张手写文档图像，覆盖三种结构（自由文本 367、表格 81、公式 52 张且含 278 个公式区域），四种语言设置（简中为主，含英文、繁中、中英混写），九类真实场景（医疗、教育、历史档案等），并对每个样本按六个维度打难度标签（视觉退化、连笔程度、语言歧义、结构复杂度、领域知识、多语混写），便于分层分析。数据来源混合“线下真实手稿贡献”和“互联网公开材料”，并做内容相似度扫描去重 + 人工复核。
2）统一输出格式：自由文本用 Markdown、公式用 LaTeX、表格用 HTML <table>，把评测从字符级扩展到结构级。
3）PDE（Prior-Driven Error）指标：核心思想是把错误分成“由语言先验驱动的错误”与“由视觉证据不足导致的错误”。论文在引言中给出的直观定义是：当模型输出更像是流畅合理的语言补全，但与图像证据不一致时，计为 prior-driven。它试图回答传统 accuracy 无法回答的问题：模型错在哪里、为什么错。
4）对比基线：在统一协议下评测 18 个 SOTA MLLM/OCR-oriented VLM，并引入校准过的人类基线，强调“人类在不可辨识处更保守，而模型更倾向自信补全”。
summary.experiments:
关键结论集中在三组数字：
- 整体难度：最强模型总体仅 71.85%，明显低于打印文档基准的接近饱和表现；人类基线 77.09%，仍高于模型。
- 结构与指标差异：论文指出在某些“格式匹配”的文本转写指标上，顶级模型甚至能超过人类，但这并不意味着理解更可靠，往往伴随更强的“自信补全”。
- 错误归因（PDE）：模型错误中 63–91% 被判为 prior-driven，而人类约 49%。这说明当前 MLLM 在手写场景的主要风险不是“看不清就空着”，而是“看不清也要编一个看起来合理的答案”。
（注：你提供的全文片段在方法与实验细节处截断，更多分结构/分语言/分场景的细粒度表格与显著性检验若存在，需要回到论文实验章节核对。）
summary.reading_guide:
泛读优先级：
1）先看 Benchmark Design：三维组织方式（语言/结构/场景）与标注格式（Markdown/LaTeX/HTML）决定了它能测到“结构恢复”而不只是 OCR。
2）重点看 PDE 的定义与标注/判定流程：它是否依赖额外模型、是否有人类判定、如何处理“视觉不可辨识但语言合理”的边界情况；这是把它用于训练/对齐信号的关键。
3）看人类基线如何“校准”：给人类什么上下文、是否允许 abstain、评分协议是什么；否则人机差距容易被评测设置放大或缩小。
预计阅读时间：20–30 分钟可抓住设计与主要结论；若要把 PDE 用作训练信号或做复现，需精读指标定义、标注一致性与误差分析部分（可能 1–2 小时）。

summary_en.core_problem: How to evaluate and explain failures of MLLMs on real-world handwritten document understanding: beyond accuracy, the benchmark aims to attribute errors to either missing visual evidence or over-reliance on language priors (hallucination-like completions in OCR).
summary_en.importance: This is primarily an evaluation contribution rather than a pretraining recipe. Its value to foundation-model pretraining is the diagnostic signal it introduces: handwritten documents remain a distinct regime where structure recovery, uncertainty handling, and prior-vs-evidence conflicts dominate. The proposed PDE metric operationalizes “language prior overwhelms vision” and can inform (i) data mixture decisions (handwriting, degraded scans, tables/formulas), (ii) training objectives or alignment constraints that discourage unsupported completions, and (iii) decoding/calibration strategies that allow abstention or uncertainty. The spillover to pure text-only LLM pretraining is limited, but it is relevant for VLM/document pretraining and multimodal alignment.
summary_en.technical_approach:
1) Dataset design: 500 handwritten document images spanning three structures (free text, tables, formulas), four language settings (mostly Simplified Chinese plus English, Traditional Chinese, and mixed CN-EN), and nine real-world scenarios. It also provides per-sample difficulty annotations along six axes (e.g., degradation, cursiveness, structural complexity).
2) Structured ground truth: Markdown for free text, LaTeX for formulas, and HTML tables for tabular content—pushing evaluation from token/character correctness toward layout/structure fidelity.
3) PDE (Prior-Driven Error): an error attribution metric intended to quantify whether a model’s mistake is better explained by language priors than by the visual evidence, capturing confident but unsupported “plausible” transcriptions.
4) Evaluation protocol: 18 contemporary MLLMs / OCR-oriented VLMs are tested under a unified setup, alongside calibrated human baselines, enabling qualitative comparison of error types (humans being conservative vs models hallucinating).
summary_en.experiments:
Reported headline results:
- Best model overall accuracy: 71.85% on WildHandBench, indicating handwritten understanding is far from saturated.
- Human baseline: 77.09%, still ahead overall, though the paper notes cases where top models can surpass humans under certain format-matching transcription metrics.
- Error attribution via PDE: 63–91% of model errors are classified as prior-driven, versus ~49% for humans, highlighting systematic over-reliance on linguistic priors.
(The provided full-text excerpt is truncated before many detailed breakdown tables; for exact per-structure/per-language numbers and ablations, the experiment section should be checked directly.)
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim path:
1) Benchmark construction details (data sources, de-dup, annotation formats) to understand what is actually being measured (structure recovery vs plain OCR).
2) PDE definition and labeling/decision procedure—this determines whether PDE can be reused as a training or alignment signal.
3) Human baseline calibration protocol (instructions, context, abstention rules), since it heavily affects the interpretation of the human-model gap.
Time: ~20–30 minutes for the main ideas; 1–2 hours if you want to reuse PDE or reproduce the evaluation faithfully.

recommendation.zh: 揭示了当前 VLM 在手写识别中严重依赖语言先验（幻觉）而非视觉特征的缺陷，PDE 指标的设计对 VLM 评测有启发。
recommendation.en: Reveals that current VLMs heavily rely on language priors (hallucination) rather than visual features in handwriting recognition; the design of the PDE metric is inspiring for VLM evaluation.

paper.title: MobilePA-Bench: Benchmarking Mobile Planner Agents on Complex Real-World Tasks
paper.abstract: As on-device LLM agents evolve into personal copilots, the mobile operating system has become a key testbed for this paradigm, making rigorous capability evaluation essential. Yet existing benchmarks fall into two camps, each with a critical blind spot: GUI-centric benchmarks test surface-level screen manipulation while overlooking background tool use and long-horizon planning, whereas static function-calling benchmarks rely on offline API matching that is detached from real runtime constraints.

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解决的不是“手机 GUI 自动化”本身，而是如何评测一类更接近真实移动端助手的 central planner：它需要在有状态的手机环境里，把自然语言请求转成可执行的多步计划，并在结构化工具、记忆检索、复合技能、以及必要时的 GUI 子代理之间做正确编排。现有 benchmark 要么偏静态 function calling，只看 API 匹配，不看运行时反馈和状态变化；要么偏视觉 GUI 操作，把问题压成点击和截图理解，弱化了系统级工具调用、权限约束、异常恢复和长程任务分解。MobilePA-Bench 试图补上这块空白，评测对象是“移动端规划代理”的决策与编排能力，而不是单纯的界面操作能力。
summary.importance: 对基座预训练本身的直接影响有限，它更像 agent/eval 方向的基础设施论文；但它有两点间接启发。第一，它把移动端 agent 的能力拆成 Basic Tool Use、Sub-agent Collaboration、Memory Usage、Skill Usage 四个维度，这种拆法对后续做 tool-use 数据合成、planner SFT、以及面向 RL 的 reward 设计有参考价值。第二，它强调 stateful sandbox、动态数据库、权限阻塞、调用依赖和异常反馈，这些因素比静态 benchmark 更接近真实 deployment，也更适合暴露模型在长程规划和 runtime recovery 上的短板。若关心 pretrain-posttrain 接口，尤其是 agent 训练数据和交互式评测，这篇可以作为任务设计样例；若只看预训练方法，相关性不高。
summary.technical_approach:
方法上核心不是提出新模型，而是构建一套交互式 benchmark 与执行环境。论文把 mobile planner 定义为系统的高层决策核心：负责理解用户意图、检索长期记忆、调用结构化业务 API、装载复合技能，并在结构化工具不足时把局部任务委派给 GUI 子代理。围绕这个设定，作者设计了四类能力维度。Basic Tool Use 关注基础工具调用、多模态输入处理、严格执行顺序、权限边界和 OS 反馈；Sub-agent Collaboration 关注 planner 是否能把复杂任务拆解后交给下游专用代理，并完成有效上下文交接；Memory Usage 关注是否能从持久化本地上下文中取回用户偏好、身份信息、历史状态，用来消解含糊请求；Skill Usage 关注是否能调用预封装的多步复合技能，而不是每一步都从头规划，以减少长链误差累积。

执行层面，MobilePA-Bench 运行在一个可执行 sandbox 上，内部维护 live application databases，并返回结构化反馈。这个设计的关键取舍是：它刻意把 central planning 与低层视觉解析解耦。也就是说，benchmark 不把主要难点放在屏幕像素理解，而是把重点放在“什么时候该调 API、什么时候该查 memory、什么时候该调用 skill、什么时候该转给 GUI 子代理”。这使得评测更聚焦于 planner 的决策质量，而不是被视觉噪声淹没。与此同时，环境仍保留真实摩擦，包括 call dependency、permission block、dynamic state mutation 等，因此不是纯离线字符串匹配。

从 benchmark 资产看，作者构建了 1,705 个真实任务，覆盖 13 个功能域和 212 个工具。任务强调复杂真实工作流，例如多日旅行规划这类需要跨应用、跨工具、跨状态更新的请求。论文的设计意图很明确：不是测单步工具选择，而是测在动态环境中持续做对决策的能力。
summary.experiments:
实验部分的主结论是：即便是当前较强的 LLM，在这种交互式、状态化、工具中心的移动端任务上也还有明显缺口。论文给出的总体结果里，最佳模型 overall 只有 75.52%。这说明在作者定义的任务分布下，模型距离稳定可用的 mobile planner 还有一段距离。

从失败模式看，论文重点指出了四类常见问题：一是严格工具调用顺序下容易出错，说明模型虽然能“知道要做什么”，但在执行约束下不一定能“按正确顺序做”；二是遇到运行时系统异常时恢复能力弱，暴露出 planner 对环境反馈的闭环利用不足；三是涉及模糊用户请求时，memory retrieval 不稳定，说明模型不总能先补全缺失上下文再规划；四是多代理协作时上下文交接和任务分解容易失真。

从 benchmark 规模看，1,705 个任务、13 个 domain、212 个工具，已经足以支持较细粒度的能力切片分析。摘要和正文片段里没有给出更完整的分模型数字表，但从作者强调的结果看，benchmark 的区分度主要体现在复杂约束和交互反馈，而不是简单工具匹配。对阅读者来说，重点不是追逐某个模型名次，而是看错误是如何沿着 planning→tool use→state update→recovery 这条链条累积的。
summary.reading_guide:
这篇适合泛读，不必逐段细抠。建议先看 Introduction，把作者为什么不满意现有 function-calling benchmark 和 GUI benchmark 的理由看清楚；这决定了整套 benchmark 的设计边界。然后重点看 benchmark 设计部分，尤其是四个 capability dimension 的定义，以及 central planner、memory、skill、GUI sub-agent 之间的职责划分。这里能看出作者想测的到底是什么。

接着看任务与 sandbox 设计：关注 live databases、structured feedback、permission block、dynamic state mutation 这些机制，因为它们决定 benchmark 是否只是“包装过的静态题库”。实验部分建议重点看 overall result 和 failure analysis，而不是只看排行榜。真正有信息量的是：模型在哪些约束下失败，失败是因为规划、检索、调用顺序，还是异常恢复。

如果阅读时间有限，30–40 分钟足够建立判断。若想把它用于 agent 训练数据或 RL 环境设计，再回头细看任务 schema、反馈接口和能力拆分方式。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper is not about mobile GUI automation per se. It targets a harder evaluation problem: how to benchmark a central mobile planner that must convert natural-language requests into executable multi-step plans inside a stateful phone environment, while coordinating structured tools, memory retrieval, reusable skills, and GUI sub-agents when needed. Existing benchmarks usually miss one side of this problem. Static function-calling benchmarks ignore runtime feedback and state changes. GUI-heavy mobile benchmarks overemphasize screen manipulation and underweight system-level tool use, permission constraints, exception handling, and long-horizon planning. MobilePA-Bench is built to evaluate this broader planning-and-orchestration capability.
summary_en.importance: Its direct relevance to foundation-model pretraining is limited; this is primarily an agent evaluation infrastructure paper. Still, it has two useful implications. First, it decomposes mobile agent capability into four dimensions—Basic Tool Use, Sub-agent Collaboration, Memory Usage, and Skill Usage—which is a practical framing for planner SFT data design, tool-use supervision, and RL reward shaping. Second, it insists on a stateful sandbox with dynamic databases, permission barriers, call dependencies, and runtime exceptions. That makes it more informative than static benchmarks for studying long-horizon planning and recovery behavior. For readers focused on the pretrain–posttrain interface, especially interactive training environments for agents, it is worth skimming. For core pretraining methodology, the connection is indirect.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The contribution is a benchmark and execution environment rather than a new model. The paper defines a mobile planner as the high-level decision core of an on-device assistant: it interprets user intent, retrieves long-term memory, invokes structured business APIs, loads reusable composite skills, and delegates specialized subtasks to GUI sub-agents when direct tool use is insufficient. Around this setup, the benchmark is organized into four capability dimensions. Basic Tool Use covers utility calls, multimodal input handling, strict execution order, permission boundaries, and OS feedback. Sub-agent Collaboration measures whether the planner can decompose tasks and hand them off to downstream specialists with valid context transfer. Memory Usage tests whether the agent can retrieve persistent user context—preferences, credentials, prior state—to resolve underspecified requests before planning. Skill Usage evaluates whether the planner can invoke packaged multi-step skills instead of replanning every primitive action, reducing long-horizon error accumulation.

Operationally, MobilePA-Bench runs in an executable sandbox with live application databases and structured feedback. The key design choice is to decouple central planning from low-level visual parsing. In other words, the benchmark is intentionally not centered on pixel understanding; it is centered on deciding when to call an API, when to query memory, when to invoke a composite skill, and when to fall back to a GUI sub-agent. This keeps the evaluation focused on planner quality rather than visual noise, while still preserving realistic friction such as call dependencies, permission blocks, and dynamic state mutations.

The benchmark itself contains 1,705 real-world tasks across 13 domains and 212 tools. The task design aims at realistic workflows, such as multi-day travel planning, where success depends on cross-tool coordination and state-aware execution rather than single-step tool selection.
summary_en.experiments:
The main empirical message is that current strong LLMs still struggle in this interactive, stateful, tool-centric mobile setting. The best model reaches only 75.52% overall, which is a useful signal: the benchmark is not saturated, and realistic mobile planning remains far from solved under the paper’s task formulation.

The failure analysis is more informative than the headline score. The paper highlights four recurring weaknesses: errors under strict tool-call ordering, weak recovery from runtime system exceptions, unreliable memory retrieval for ambiguous user requests, and brittle coordination across multiple agents or execution modes. These are not superficial UI failures; they point to deficits in closed-loop planning under constraints.

In terms of scale, 1,705 tasks over 13 domains and 212 tools are large enough to support capability-level slicing. The excerpt does not expose the full per-model table, but the paper’s emphasis is clear: the benchmark differentiates models mainly through dynamic constraints and interaction feedback, not through static API matching. When reading the experiments, the useful question is not who ranks first, but where errors accumulate along the chain of planning, tool invocation, state update, and recovery.
summary_en.reading_guide:
This is a skim paper. Start with the introduction and make sure the critique of existing function-calling and GUI benchmarks is clear; that critique explains every major design decision. Then read the benchmark construction section, especially the definitions of the four capability dimensions and the role split between the central planner, memory, skills, and GUI sub-agents. That is where the paper’s evaluation target becomes precise.

Next, inspect the sandbox design: live databases, structured feedback, permission blocks, and dynamic state mutation. These details determine whether the benchmark is genuinely interactive or just a dressed-up static dataset. In the experiments, focus on the overall results and failure analysis rather than the leaderboard. The most useful information is which constraints break current models and whether the failures come from planning, retrieval, ordering, or exception handling.

If time is limited, 30–40 minutes is enough. If you want to reuse ideas for agent training environments or RL-style evaluation loops, revisit the task schema and feedback interface more carefully.

recommendation.zh: 构建了一个带真实沙盒和状态反馈的移动端 Agent 评测基准，比静态 API 匹配更接近真实场景，关注 Agent 评测的研究员可扫读其沙盒设计。
recommendation.en: Constructs a mobile agent benchmark with a real sandbox and state feedback, which is closer to real-world scenarios than static API matching; researchers focusing on agent evaluation should skim its sandbox design.

paper.title: OmniAssistBench: Assistant-style Interaction Benchmark for Omni-LLMs
paper.abstract: Recent omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) show great potential as real-time video assistants, which continuously perceive environments and guide users to achieve specific goals. Unlike traditional passive video understanding, interactive assistants should actively combine visual states, user goals, and prior knowledge to provide effective help. Evaluating this is rather challenging, as the model's unpredictable response dynamically changes the user's subsequent actions, which static of

summary.core_problem: 评测“实时视频助手型”Omni-LLM 的核心难点是交互路径发散：模型一句话会改变用户下一步动作，从而改变后续视频输入，静态离线 QA 数据集无法覆盖这种动态闭环。论文要解决的是：如何构造一个可复现、可评分、又尽量贴近真实助手场景的交互式视频评测基准。
summary.importance: 这是 eval 方向的工作，对预训练 recipe 的直接贡献有限，但对多模态基座训练的目标设定有反馈价值：它把“助手式能力”拆成可测的瓶颈（视觉提示跟随、长程记忆、延迟响应、跨轮目标保持），这些问题往往来自预训练/中期训练数据形态与上下文管理方式，而不只是后训练技巧。若你在做 omni-modal 预训练或长上下文训练，benchmark 暴露的失败模式可以反推数据与训练目标该怎么补。
summary.technical_approach:
OmniAssistBench 的关键设计是用“视频先验（priors）”把交互路径固定住，从而避免发散：
- 先从现成互联网视频中反向工程：筛选适合的源视频，推断用户目标与标准操作路径（procedural path priors），再把视频切成多轮 clip，模拟一步一步的助手对话。
- 评测时把这些 priors 显式提供给模型，要求模型沿唯一标准路径指导用户，减少评测对模型内置常识的依赖，也让后续视频片段不需要根据模型回答动态生成。
- 两层框架：Basic tier 测交互必需的基础感知/指令跟随（例如手势提示、社会关系等）；Advanced tier 用日常场景的 plot templates 测复杂目标导向任务。
- 额外拍摄 3 个长案例（平均 15 轮）覆盖多能力组合；用户指令以音频嵌入视频，输出为开放式文本；评分协议会惩罚冗余与幻觉。
summary.experiments:
作者报告了一个总体分数对比：Gemini-3-Pro 66.4/100；开源 Qwen3-Omni-Instruct 51.2/100。并总结了四类主要瓶颈：
1) 视觉提示跟随不足（如手势）；
2) 长期记忆差，上下文窗口在几分钟内被耗尽；
3) 延迟响应失败（应等待特定视觉情节出现，但模型提前输出无关描述）；
4) 跨轮上下文丢失（后续视觉输入干扰后忘记初始目标）。
由于未给出更多模型列表、分项得分表、方差/一致性分析等细节片段，无法进一步复核评分可靠性与统计显著性；需要在完整正文里看标注规范、打分 rubric、评审一致性（inter-annotator agreement）与基线设置。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议（30–45 分钟，偏做 benchmark 的读法）：
- Data Construction：重点看“priors”如何定义与呈现给模型；它决定了任务是否在测助手能力还是在测对脚本的复述。
- Evaluation protocol：看开放式评分如何落地、如何惩罚幻觉/冗余、以及评审一致性。
- Basic/Advanced 的任务清单与示例：把每类失败模式映射到可能的训练缺口（例如手势=视觉指令跟随数据；延迟响应=时序对齐与等待策略；长记忆=长上下文与摘要机制）。
- 3 个长案例：适合用来做模型 debug，观察上下文预算、跨轮目标保持与“等待”行为。

summary_en.core_problem: Evaluating omni-modal LLMs as real-time video assistants is hard because interaction paths diverge: the assistant’s response changes the user’s next action, which changes subsequent video inputs. Static offline QA benchmarks cannot capture this closed-loop dynamic. The paper addresses how to build a reproducible, scorable benchmark that still reflects assistant-style multi-turn video interactions.
summary_en.importance: Primarily an evaluation contribution, with indirect but useful feedback to pretraining: it operationalizes assistant-style bottlenecks (visual prompt following, long-term memory under context limits, delayed response, cross-turn goal retention). These failure modes often trace back to pretraining/mid-training data formats and objectives, not only post-training. If you build omni-modal or long-context pretraining pipelines, the benchmark’s taxonomy can guide what data and objectives are missing.
summary_en.technical_approach:
OmniAssistBench fixes interaction-path divergence by introducing explicit video-derived priors.
- Reverse-engineer Internet videos: select suitable source videos, infer user goals and a standard procedural path (priors), then segment videos into multi-turn clips to simulate step-by-step assistant interactions.
- During evaluation, provide the priors to the model and require guidance along a single route, reducing dependence on the model’s internal world knowledge and avoiding the need to dynamically generate new video branches.
- Two-tier framework: Basic tier for foundational interactive perception/instruction-following (e.g., gestures, social relations); Advanced tier for goal-oriented tasks using everyday plot templates.
- Additionally, film three long cases (~15 turns each) to test combined abilities; user instructions are embedded as audio; open-ended scoring penalizes redundancy and hallucinations.
summary_en.experiments: Reported headline results: Gemini-3-Pro scores 66.4/100; open-source Qwen3-Omni-Instruct scores 51.2/100. The evaluation highlights four major bottlenecks: (1) weak visual prompt following (e.g., gestures), (2) poor long-term memory with context quickly exhausted, (3) failure to delay responses (models answer too early with irrelevant captions), and (4) loss of cross-turn goal/context under new visual distractions. More detailed verification requires the full paper’s per-skill breakdown, scoring rubric, annotator agreement, and baseline coverage.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim plan (30–45 minutes, benchmark-oriented):
- Data construction: how priors are defined and presented; this determines whether the benchmark measures assistant reasoning or script regurgitation.
- Scoring protocol: how open-ended answers are graded, how hallucination/redundancy penalties work, and inter-rater reliability.
- Task taxonomy and examples: map each failure mode to likely training gaps (gesture-following data, temporal “wait” behavior, long-context training, cross-turn goal tracking).
- The three long cases: useful for debugging context budgeting, goal persistence, and delayed-response behavior.

recommendation.zh: 针对Omni-LLM交互能力的评测，通过逆向工程视频构建交互路径的思路比较巧妙，值得关注其具体的评测指标设计。
recommendation.en: A benchmark for Omni-LLM interactive capabilities. The idea of constructing interaction paths by reverse-engineering videos is clever; worth checking their specific evaluation metric design.

paper.title: MGAL: A Multilingual Granularity-Aware Long-Context Benchmark
paper.abstract: Evaluation of long-context Large Language Models (LLMs) has advanced rapidly. However, most existing benchmarks are limited to the document level and focus mainly on high-resource languages, leaving many fine-grained challenges insufficiently evaluated. To address this gap, we present MGAL, the first multilingual, granularity- and position-aware long-context benchmark. MGAL is constructed from United Nations (UN) reports spanning 8K to 128K tokens across the six official UN languages. It covers

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解决的不是“再做一个长上下文榜单”，而是把长上下文能力拆开测清楚。现有 benchmark 多半停留在文档级任务，语言覆盖偏高资源语种，也很少控制证据在长文中的位置，因此很难判断模型到底是不会跨粒度理解，还是只是被位置偏置、表面词重叠、评分方式等因素干扰。MGAL 试图把这几个变量显式分离：同一套长文材料上，同时考察词、句、段、文档四个粒度，并按 begin/middle/end 控制证据位置，再扩展到联合国六种官方语言。它要回答的是：长上下文模型在不同语言、不同粒度、不同证据位置下，失效模式到底长什么样。
summary.importance: 对基座研究的价值主要在评测设计，而不是提出新模型。它补上了两个长期缺口。第一，长上下文评测过去偏“粗粒度”，容易把很多局部检索、句法衔接、段落功能理解的问题淹没在文档级分数里；MGAL 把能力分解后，更适合诊断训练目标、位置编码、长序列注意力和数据配比带来的具体短板。第二，它把多语言和位置控制做到了同一框架里，这对分析长上下文 scaling 是否只在英语成立、以及低资源语言为何掉队，很有帮助。对做预训练的人来说，这类 benchmark 的意义不在 leaderboard，而在于它能把“模型为什么错”暴露得更具体：是 recency bias、option-order bias、局部语义拥挤，还是生成时的 input anchoring 不足。
summary.technical_approach:
MGAL 的核心做法是用联合国数字图书馆中的长篇报告构造一个位置对齐、跨语言可比的长上下文测试集。数据覆盖阿拉伯语、中文、英语、法语、俄语、西班牙语，输入长度从 8K 到 128K token。任务设计上分成 closed-ended 和 open-ended 两类，并覆盖四层语言粒度：词级、句级、段级、文档级。文中提到的任务包括 word-level QA、sentence-level cloze、paragraph filling、document summarization、translation 等，共 7 个任务；每种语言每个任务有 420 个 query-response 对。关键不只是任务种类，而是构造时同时控制了证据位置：在文档级和段落级都标注 begin/middle/end，使得同一模型在不同位置上的退化可以被直接比较。

数据来源选 UN 报告有两个原因。一个是天然多语平行和主题一致，便于做跨语言对照；另一个是文档结构较规范，适合定义词、句、段、文档四层 coherent unit。作者强调 same-position sentences 在六种语言中语义对齐，这让跨语言比较不只是“题型类似”，而是材料位置和语义都尽量一致。质量控制上，所有 query-response pair 都经过人工审查并删除有缺陷样本，明显是偏小而精的 benchmark 路线。

评分方面，closed-ended 任务主要用 Accuracy，开放生成任务用 ROUGE-L 等 reference-based 指标；对于 paragraph filling 这类仅靠 n-gram overlap 很难评准的任务，又引入了 LLM-as-a-judge。这个设计比较务实：如果只用自动指标，会低估语义正确但表述不同的答案；如果全靠 judge，又会把 benchmark 的可复现性变差。MGAL 采取的是两者并用。

从方法贡献看，它不是提出新的评测算法，而是把三个维度系统化了：multilingual、granularity-aware、position-aware。和 LongBench、LV-Eval、M4LE、ONERULER 这类已有工作相比，区别不在规模更大，而在控制变量更细，能支持更明确的误差归因。
summary.experiments:
实验部分的重点不是谁第一，而是错误模式。作者评测了 12 个 long-context LLM。摘要和正文给出的主要结论有四类。

第一，粒度越粗，性能越差。模型在词级任务上普遍表现较好，但从句子、段落到文档，能力明显下降。这说明很多模型的“长上下文能力”更接近局部匹配或局部检索，而不是稳定的跨段组织与全篇整合。

第二，多语言差异在低资源语言上被放大。大开源模型和闭源模型在高资源语言上的差距没有想象中大，但到了低资源语言，闭源模型优势更稳定，小型开源模型掉得更明显。这个现象对预训练很关键，因为它暗示长上下文能力并不是单独由架构决定，语料覆盖和跨语言表示质量仍然是主导因素。

第三，位置敏感性依然明显。sentence-cloze 中，空缺出现在文本前部时错误率最高，越靠后越好，和 recency-biased attention 的已有观察一致。作者还发现明显的 early-option bias：模型更容易选前面的选项，如 A/B，而不是逐项核对证据。这说明一部分错误不是“不会读长文”，而是推理过程被答题格式诱导。

第四，作者提出了两个更细的失效现象。其一是 local semantic crowding：相邻句子共享大量实体、年份、连接词时，模型容易根据表面重叠选错句子，忽略句子在段落中的功能角色，比如背景、解释、结果。其二是 fluency-consistency gap：生成结果往往流畅、风格也对，但和输入锚定不够，容易出现 factual drift 或无依据补写。这个观察对长上下文生成很重要，因为很多模型在 summarization/filling 上看起来“像对了”，但其实证据绑定很弱。

从数据规模上，benchmark 覆盖 6 种语言、7 个任务、4 个粒度、上下文长度 8K–128K，每语言每任务 420 个样本。虽然正文截断处没有完整表格数字，但这些设置已经足够支撑细粒度切片分析。若做复现实验，最值得关注的是不同模型在 begin/middle/end 和不同 granularity 上的相对斜率，而不是单一总分。
summary.reading_guide: 这篇适合泛读，不需要逐段精读。建议先看 Introduction 和任务定义表，确认它到底比 LongBench 一类工作多控制了哪些变量。然后重点看 benchmark construction：数据来源、跨语言位置对齐、人工审核流程，这决定了评测结论是否可信。实验部分优先看按 granularity 和 position 分层的主结果图，而不是总榜单；真正有信息量的是性能如何随词→句→段→文档退化，以及 begin/middle/end 的差异曲线。再看作者对 local semantic crowding 和 fluency-consistency gap 的案例分析，这两部分最接近“为什么模型会错”。如果时间有限，30–40 分钟足够抓住主要信息。若你在做长上下文预训练或位置编码，值得把相关图表和错误案例细看一遍，因为它们能直接转化成训练诊断假设。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper is not trying to add another long-context leaderboard. Its actual target is diagnosis. Existing benchmarks mostly evaluate document-level tasks, focus on high-resource languages, and rarely control where the supporting evidence appears in the context. That makes it hard to tell whether a model fails because it cannot reason across discourse units, because it is position-biased, or because the task setup hides the failure mode. MGAL isolates these factors explicitly: it evaluates word-, sentence-, paragraph-, and document-level understanding, stratifies evidence by begin/middle/end positions, and does so across the six official UN languages. The central question is: what exactly breaks in long-context LLMs when granularity, language, and evidence position are varied in a controlled way?
summary_en.importance: Its value is in benchmark design rather than model innovation. Two gaps are addressed. First, long-context evaluation has been too coarse. Document-level scores often hide failures in local retrieval, sentence function discrimination, paragraph coherence, and evidence anchoring. By decomposing performance by granularity, MGAL is more useful for diagnosing effects of pretraining data mix, positional schemes, long-sequence attention, and instruction tuning. Second, it puts multilinguality and position control into the same framework. That matters for understanding whether long-context scaling trends are mostly English artifacts and why lower-resource languages lag more sharply. For pretraining researchers, the benchmark matters less as a ranking tool and more as a failure-surface probe: recency bias, option-order bias, local semantic crowding, and weak grounding in generation become visible as separate phenomena.
summary_en.technical_approach:
MGAL is built from long-form reports in the UN Digital Library, using position-aligned multilingual documents so that cross-lingual comparisons are not merely task-level but also semantically and structurally aligned. It covers Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, and Spanish, with context lengths from 8K to 128K tokens. The benchmark spans four linguistic granularities—word, sentence, paragraph, and document—and includes both closed-ended and open-ended tasks. The paper mentions seven tasks in total, including word-level QA, sentence-level cloze, paragraph filling, document summarization, and translation, with 420 query-response pairs per task per language.

The key design choice is controlled stratification by evidence position. Examples are labeled by whether the relevant evidence appears at the beginning, middle, or end, indexed at both document and paragraph levels. This turns the benchmark into a diagnostic instrument rather than a generic task suite. The choice of UN reports is practical: they provide multilingual parallelism, topic consistency, and relatively regular discourse structure, which makes coherent unit definitions more reliable.

Quality control is manual and strict. The authors state that every query-response pair was audited and flawed samples were removed. This is a smaller-but-cleaner benchmark philosophy, which is appropriate for diagnostic evaluation.

Scoring is hybrid. Closed-ended tasks use precision-oriented reference metrics such as Accuracy, while open-ended tasks use ROUGE-L and, for tasks like paragraph filling where lexical overlap is insufficient, an LLM-as-a-judge setup. That trade-off is sensible: pure reference metrics under-credit semantically correct paraphrases, while pure judge-based evaluation reduces reproducibility. MGAL uses both.

Relative to LongBench, LV-Eval, M4LE, and ONERULER, the novelty is not simply broader coverage. The main difference is tighter control over variables that matter for error attribution: multilingual alignment, discourse granularity, and evidence position.
summary_en.experiments:
The experimental section is useful mainly for the error patterns it exposes. The benchmark is evaluated on 12 long-context LLMs. The main findings reported in the paper fall into four groups.

First, performance degrades as granularity becomes coarser. Models do well on word-level tasks, but performance drops at sentence, paragraph, and document levels. This suggests that many current long-context models are stronger at local matching or retrieval than at stable discourse-level integration.

Second, multilingual gaps widen in lower-resource languages. Large open-source and closed-source models are relatively comparable on higher-resource languages, but closed-source systems maintain a clearer lead on lower-resource ones, and smaller open models degrade more sharply. For pretraining, this points to data coverage and multilingual representation quality as major bottlenecks, not just architecture.

Third, position sensitivity remains strong. In sentence cloze, blanks appearing earlier in the text produce the highest error rates, with performance improving toward later positions, consistent with recency-biased attention. The authors also observe an early-option bias: models disproportionately choose earlier answer options such as A or B, indicating reliance on answer-order heuristics rather than evidence verification.

Fourth, the paper identifies two more specific failure modes. One is local semantic crowding: when neighboring sentences share entities, years, or discourse markers, models over-rely on surface overlap and pick the wrong sentence, failing to distinguish functional roles such as background, explanation, or outcome. The other is a fluency-consistency gap: generated outputs are often fluent and stylistically plausible but weakly anchored to the source, leading to factual drift and unsupported claims.

In terms of benchmark scale, MGAL covers 6 languages, 7 tasks, 4 granularities, and contexts from 8K to 128K, with 420 examples per task per language. Even without chasing a single aggregate score, this is enough to support meaningful slicing by granularity and position. The most informative numbers are likely the relative slopes across word→sentence→paragraph→document and begin→middle→end, not the overall ranking.
summary_en.reading_guide: This is a skim paper, not one that requires line-by-line reading. Start with the introduction and the task overview table to see exactly which variables MGAL controls beyond prior long-context benchmarks. Then read the benchmark construction section carefully: data source, multilingual position alignment, and manual auditing are what determine whether the later claims are trustworthy. In the experiments, focus on results broken down by granularity and position rather than the overall leaderboard. The most useful plots are the degradation curves across discourse units and the begin/middle/end slices. After that, read the qualitative analysis on local semantic crowding and the fluency-consistency gap; those sections contain the most actionable insights for model development. If time is limited, 30–40 minutes should be enough to extract the main value. If you work on long-context pretraining, positional methods, or multilingual data mixture, the error analyses are worth a closer look.

recommendation.zh: 长上下文预训练评测可扫数据构造和分层结果；只看总分会漏掉粒度和位置失败模式。
recommendation.en: Worth skimming for the dataset design and stratified results; aggregate long-context scores hide granularity and position failures.

paper.title: UpgradeBench: A Decision-Centric Benchmark for Upgrading Fine-Tuned LLM Specialists
paper.abstract: Organizations maintain task-specific adapters for open-weight language models, and each new base-model release forces a migration decision: retain existing specialists, port adapters, refresh from preserved behavior, or retrain. Prior transfer work evaluates isolated model pairs, without studying these choices across real model release sequences. We present UpgradeBench, a decision-driven longitudinal benchmark covering four consecutive Qwen releases, one continuation checkpoint, six tasks, and

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作讨论的是一个很现实但过去几乎没有被系统测量的问题：当组织已经在某个开源基座上训练出一批 task-specific specialist，新的 base model 发布后，到底该继续用旧 specialist、直接迁移 adapter、用旧 specialist 蒸馏新 base，还是重新训练？现有迁移论文通常只测某一对模型之间的 transfer，而没有沿着真实 release sequence 去衡量这个决策问题。UpgradeBench 要解决的是“base-model upgrade tax”的测量：不同升级策略在质量、训练成本和时间上的差距到底有多大，哪些任务值得迁移，哪些任务干脆冻结旧模型更划算。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究，它不是核心方法论文，但启发很直接。第一，它把 post-train 资产和 base pretrain checkpoint 的关系量化了，说明 specialist 的价值并不只取决于下游数据量，还强烈依赖新旧 base 之间的训练连续性。第二，它给出了一个很有用的经验判断：adapter 可移植性不是“同家族、同架构”就成立，而是受到底层权重轨迹距离约束。这对持续预训练、mid-training、annealing、checkpoint 发布策略都有现实意义。第三，它把任务分成更接近 data-bound 和 base-bound 两类，而不是常见的 discriminative/generative 二分，这个视角对理解预训练能力如何被后训练资产继承很有帮助。整体上，这篇更像是 pretrain↔posttrain 接口的测量工作，而不是单纯的 fine-tuning benchmark。
summary.technical_approach:
UpgradeBench 的设计核心是 longitudinal，而不是静态 pairwise transfer。作者沿着四代 Qwen release 加上一条 continuation release，构造了真实的升级路径；同时补充 OLMo checkpoints，因为 OLMo 的训练关系是公开且可验证的，可以把“是否来自同一训练轨迹”当成受控变量，而不是靠 release note 猜。

它把升级决策拆成四种策略：freeze、port、refresh、retrain。freeze 是继续部署旧 specialist；port 是把旧 adapter 或 task vector 直接迁到新 base；refresh 是用旧 specialist 作为 teacher，对新 base 做便宜的再专门化；retrain 则是从头按固定 recipe 重训 specialist。围绕这四种策略，作者定义并测量了几个关键量：retention、recovery cost、specialization half-life，以及 upgrade tax。这里最重要的是 retention：新策略相对“该 hop 上可达到的最佳 specialist”保留了多少收益。这样定义后，不同 hop、不同任务、不同模型规模可以放到同一坐标系里比较。

任务设置覆盖 6 个应用任务、3 类任务、2 个模型尺度，并把训练侧成本纳入 benchmark 输出，包括 GPU-minutes 和 energy。这个点做得比较扎实，因为很多迁移论文只报最终精度，不报恢复到同等质量需要多少代价，而实际部署决策恰恰取决于这个成本。

方法上它没有提出新的迁移算法，贡献在于实验设计和变量控制。尤其是对 port 的分析很关键：作者直接检验一个业界常见假设——只要新旧模型架构兼容，adapter 原样拷贝就是强基线。实验结论是否定的。决定能否直接拷贝的不是 shape compatibility，而是训练连续性，也就是两个 checkpoint 是否位于同一权重演化轨迹上，以及相距多远。

OLMo 部分进一步把这个结论做成了更接近机制层面的测量。沿同一 documented trajectory 往后走，adapter retention 会随着 continuation token 数增加而下降；文中给出的边界是，从 46B-token continuation 时仍有 0.88–0.99 retention，走到 2.9T-token continuation 时则掉到接近 no-adapter floor。后续 anneal 和 model-soup merge 并没有带来额外主要损伤。这个结果很有信息量，因为它把“能不能 port”从模糊经验变成了 distance budget 的问题。
summary.experiments:
实验规模不算大，但设计很完整：总共 98 次训练、193 个 evaluation cells，全部在一张 RTX 4090 上完成，并释放了 per-query prediction、bootstrap CI 和 energy log。这个设置说明作者更关心可复现的决策测量，而不是堆大算力。

几个关键结果值得记住。第一，specialist 不一定会很快过时。对于 intent classification，freeze 在 9 个 upgrade hops 上能保留 99%–101% 的 attainable gain；跨四代模型，retrained specialist 的参考分数只移动了 0.2 分，而 zero-shot 却提升了 21 分。这说明某些任务的专门化收益主要来自标签体系、输出格式或任务数据本身，base 进步并不会立刻吞掉这些收益。

第二，另一些任务则明显更依赖 base 能力。text-to-SQL 上，冻结旧 specialist 在单个 hop 上最多会损失 59% 的 attainable gain，而且它相对新 base 的优势会在三代内衰减到零。作者据此提出 data-bound 与 base-bound 的区分：前者 specialist moat 更稳，后者随着 base reasoning 能力增强会更快被追平。

第三，naive porting 可能非常危险。文中给了一个很强的反例：在两个架构完全相同但来自独立预训练运行的 checkpoint 之间，直接贴 adapter 会把 intent classification 从 92.8% 打到 42.9%，甚至低于不用 adapter 的 60.7%。但如果目标模型是同一权重继续预训练得到的 descendant，同样的操作可以保持接近 reference-level accuracy。这一组结果基本否定了“同家族同结构即可直接迁移”的经验法则。

第四，OLMo 验证复现了同样规律，并进一步定位了边界：同一训练轨迹上，随着 continuation 距离增大，port retention 从 0.88–0.99 逐步跌到 no-adapter floor；而 anneal、model soup merge 不是主要破坏源。这个结论对 checkpoint 发布和 continual pretraining 很有现实意义。

文中还给出了一个 half-life 估计：在 7–8B 规模，specialization half-life 大约落在 2–3 个 generation；在 1.5–1.8B 规模，至少观察到一次 crossing，即新 base 的便宜采用策略真正超过旧 specialist。这个量化虽然依赖任务集，但比过去泛泛讨论“要不要升级”要扎实得多。
summary.reading_guide: 这篇适合带着问题读。先看 Introduction 和 Figure 1，作者想推翻的三个直觉都写得很清楚：specialist 不一定很快过时、port 不一定安全、任务差异不能只按生成/判别来分。然后重点看 benchmark setup 和 metric definitions，尤其是 retention、recovery cost、specialization half-life 的定义；如果不先把这些量读明白，后面的结论会显得像经验观察。实验部分优先看四类策略在不同任务上的对比，以及 Qwen 与 OLMo 两条线如何共同支持“continuity 而非 architecture shape 决定 portability”。如果你做 continual pretrain、checkpoint 选择、adapter 生态或企业部署，这篇值得完整读一遍；如果只是想抓结论，读主文 40–60 分钟基本够。最值得深挖的是 §7.3 附近关于 independent pretraining run vs continued-pretraining descendant 的对照实验，它直接触及参数空间几何和任务向量可迁移性的边界。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies a practical but poorly measured question: once an organization has a fleet of task-specific specialists built on an open base model, what should it do when a new base release arrives? Keep serving the old specialist, directly port the adapter, cheaply refresh the new base using the old specialist as teacher, or retrain from scratch? Prior transfer papers usually evaluate isolated model pairs. UpgradeBench instead measures the full upgrade decision over real release sequences. The target quantity is the base-model upgrade tax: the quality-and-cost gap between the chosen migration strategy and the best attainable specialist on the new base.
summary_en.importance: This is not a core pretraining-method paper, but it is highly relevant to the pretrain–posttrain interface. First, it quantifies how strongly post-training assets depend on the underlying base checkpoint, not just on downstream data. Second, it shows that adapter portability is not guaranteed by family membership or architectural compatibility; it depends on continuity in weight space and on how far the target checkpoint has moved along the training trajectory. That has direct implications for continual pretraining, checkpoint release policy, annealing, and mid-training updates. Third, the paper proposes a more useful task distinction than the usual discriminative vs generative split: some tasks are data-bound, while others are base-bound. That framing is helpful for reasoning about when pretraining improvements will erase specialist advantages and when they will not.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The main design choice is longitudinal evaluation rather than static pairwise transfer. The benchmark follows four consecutive Qwen releases plus one continuation release, creating a realistic upgrade path. It also includes OLMo checkpoints, where training relationships are documented rather than inferred, allowing the authors to treat training continuity as a controlled variable.

The benchmark evaluates four upgrade strategies: freeze, port, refresh, and retrain. Freeze keeps serving the old specialist. Port copies the old adapter or task vector onto the new base. Refresh uses the old specialist as a teacher to cheaply re-specialize the new base. Retrain rebuilds the specialist from scratch under a fixed recipe. Around these strategies, the paper defines and measures retention, recovery cost, specialization half-life, and upgrade tax. Retention is especially important: it measures how much of the attainable gain on the target hop is preserved by a cheaper strategy relative to the best specialist achievable there. This makes comparisons across hops, tasks, and model scales much more meaningful.

The benchmark covers six application tasks from three classes, at two model scales, and treats training-side cost as a first-class output, including GPU-minutes and energy. That is a strong design choice because deployment decisions depend on cost-to-recover, not just final accuracy.

The paper does not introduce a new transfer algorithm. Its contribution is experimental structure and variable control. The most important analysis concerns porting. A common practitioner assumption is that if two checkpoints are shape-compatible, direct adapter copying is a strong baseline. The paper shows that this assumption is false. What licenses copying is not architectural shape but training continuity: whether the target checkpoint lies on the same weight trajectory, and how far away it is.

The OLMo experiments sharpen this into something close to a mechanistic statement. Along the same documented trajectory, adapter retention decays as continuation distance grows. The paper reports retention of 0.88–0.99 after a 46B-token continuation, but near no-adapter-floor performance after a 2.9T-token continuation. Subsequent annealing and model-soup merging add little extra damage. This turns portability from a vague family-level intuition into a distance-budget question.
summary_en.experiments:
The experimental scale is modest but well structured: 98 trainings and 193 evaluation cells, all run on a single RTX 4090, with per-query predictions, bootstrap confidence intervals, and energy logs released. The emphasis is clearly on reproducible decision measurement rather than brute-force benchmarking.

Several results stand out. First, specialists do not always become obsolete quickly. On intent classification, freezing retains 99%–101% of the attainable gain across nine upgrade hops. Over four generations, the retrained-specialist reference score moves by only 0.2 points, while zero-shot performance rises by 21 points. This suggests that some specialist value is tied mainly to task data, label taxonomies, or output conventions rather than to frontier base capability.

Second, other tasks are much more base-dependent. On text-to-SQL, the frozen specialist can forfeit up to 59% of attainable gain on a single hop, and its advantage over a newer base decays to zero within three generations. This motivates the paper’s data-bound vs base-bound distinction: some specialist moats are stable, others are rapidly eroded by improvements in the base model’s reasoning ability.

Third, naive porting can fail catastrophically. The paper gives a strong counterexample: between two architecturally identical checkpoints from independent pretraining runs, directly pasting the adapter drops intent classification from 92.8% to 42.9%, which is even worse than the 60.7% obtainable with no adapter at all. But when the target is a continued-pretraining descendant of the same weights, the same operation preserves near-reference accuracy. This directly challenges the common rule of thumb that same-family, same-shape transfer is safe.

Fourth, the OLMo validation reproduces the same pattern and localizes the boundary more precisely. Along the same training trajectory, port retention falls from 0.88–0.99 to the no-adapter floor as continuation distance increases; annealing and model-soup merge are not the main sources of damage. This is highly relevant for continual pretraining and checkpoint release strategy.

The paper also estimates a specialization half-life of roughly two to three generations at the 7–8B scale, and observes at least one actual crossing at 1.5–1.8B where cheap adoption of the new base overtakes the old specialist. The exact values are task-dependent, but this is much more concrete than the usual qualitative discussion around whether upgrades are worth it.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Read this one with a concrete deployment or training question in mind. Start with the introduction and Figure 1, where the paper lays out the three intuitions it challenges: specialists do not always age quickly, porting is not always safe, and task differences are not well captured by a generative/discriminative split. Then read the benchmark setup and metric definitions carefully, especially retention, recovery cost, and specialization half-life. Without those definitions, the later conclusions can look like anecdotal observations.

In the experiments, prioritize the strategy comparisons across tasks and the evidence from both Qwen and OLMo supporting the claim that continuity, not architectural shape, governs portability. If you work on continual pretraining, checkpoint selection, adapter ecosystems, or practical model deployment, this is worth a full read. If you only need the main conclusions, 40–60 minutes on the main paper should be enough. The section around the independent-pretraining-run vs continued-pretraining-descendant comparison is the most important one to study closely, because it directly probes the limits of parameter-space transferability.

recommendation.zh: 适合看作 posttrain 资产折旧评测；读 release 序列实验即可，别把新 base 更强等同于 specialist 必然升级。
recommendation.en: Read it as an evaluation of post-training asset depreciation; the release-sequence results matter more than any single transfer score.

institutions: Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business

paper.title: Evaluation-as-Search: Adaptive Discovery of Grounding Failures in Meeting Assistants
paper.abstract: LLM-powered meeting assistants are deployed at scale, yet systematic evaluation of their grounding fidelity remains limited to static benchmarks that miss failure modes tied to specific discourse structures or reasoning demands. We propose Evaluation-as-Search (EaS), a feedback-driven methodology that frames quality evaluation as an adaptive search over the space of natural questions a meeting participant might ask. Rather than sampling uniformly, EaS learns from evaluator feedback across iterat

summary.core_problem: 静态 benchmark 很难发现会议助手在特定话语结构和认知需求下的 grounding failure，论文试图把评测过程本身做成自适应搜索。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是评测方法与 benchmark 构建。它不是基座训练论文，但对如何更高效地挖掘 LLM 失败模式有方法论价值，尤其适合做高成本人工评测的团队参考。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 Evaluation-as-Search，把问题生成视为在自然问题空间上的主动搜索：根据评审反馈，用 UCB 评分的 coverage map 迭代聚焦更可能出错的认知需求区域，并配合 blind multi-dimensional quality evaluation。基于该流程构建 MeetingProbe。
summary.experiments: MeetingProbe 含 20 份会议转录、3 种会议类型、3 个 LLM 助手、3000+ 标注 QA。消融显示自适应搜索比随机 probing 多发现 2.5 倍失败案例，failure finding rate 从 2.9% 提升到 7.1%。摘要未给出底层模型规模。
summary.authors_note: Microsoft。Ross Cutler 长期做语音、会议智能与多模态系统。

summary_en.core_problem: Static benchmarks miss grounding failures in meeting assistants that depend on discourse structure and cognitive demand; this paper turns evaluation itself into an adaptive search process.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is an evaluation methodology plus benchmark construction. It is not a pretraining paper, but it is useful for teams that need more sample-efficient failure discovery under expensive human evaluation.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper proposes Evaluation-as-Search, treating question generation as active search over the space of natural user questions. Guided by evaluator feedback, a UCB-scored coverage map focuses probing on cognitive-demand regions likely to expose failures, combined with blind multi-dimensional quality assessment. This process yields the MeetingProbe benchmark.
summary_en.experiments: MeetingProbe contains 3,000+ annotated QA pairs over 20 transcripts, three meeting genres, and three LLM assistants. Ablations show adaptive search finds 2.5x more failures than random probing, improving failure discovery rate from 2.9% to 7.1%. No model scale is given in the abstract.
summary_en.authors_note: Microsoft. Ross Cutler is known for work on speech, meeting intelligence, and multimodal systems.

recommendation.zh: 不是 pretrain 论文，但评测设计很干净；只看方法和消融就够，尤其是 adaptive probing 比随机抽样高 2.5 倍这一点可直接迁到内部 red-teaming。
recommendation.en: Not a pretraining paper, but the eval design is clean; read the method and ablation only, especially the 2.5x gain over random probing for internal red-teaming.

paper.title: Personalized Privacy Control in LLMs via Attention Head Intervention
paper.abstract: The rise of agentic AI enables LLMs to access diverse user data, raising critical privacy concerns. Prior work on contextual privacy studies whether LLMs regulate information disclosure according to context-dependent norms. However, acceptable disclosure boundaries may vary across users even within the same context. To address this limitation, we introduce \textit{personalized privacy}, which incorporates user-specific disclosure preferences into privacy control. We further present P3Bench~(\tex

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解决的是：LLM 在同一语境下需要根据不同用户的个体隐私偏好决定是否披露信息，但现有 contextual privacy 设定无法表达这种个体化边界。
summary.importance: 价值主要有两层：一是把 privacy control 从“上下文相关”推进到“用户个体化偏好相关”，二是给出 P3Bench 这类可复用评测资产。对基座预训练本身不是直接推进，但对 agent 场景下模型行为约束、偏好条件化控制和推理时干预有参考意义，贡献类型更接近 benchmark + inference-time control。
summary.technical_approach: 作者先定义 personalized privacy 任务，将原有 contextual privacy policy 扩展为带用户特定披露规则的设定；随后构建 P3Bench，用于衡量模型是否遵守个体化隐私策略。方法上提出 Repair，一种推理时 attention head intervention：定位与隐私泄露相关的注意力头，并在生成时进行干预，以降低违反个体化策略的概率。整体属于不改权重或少改权重的 inference-time control，而不是预训练或后训练范式创新。
summary.experiments: 摘要中报告，prompt-based policy 对个体化隐私控制不可靠，Qwen2.5-7B 和 Gemma3-4B 的平均 policy ignorance ratio 分别达到 51.25% 和 74.28%。实验重点看起来是：基于 P3Bench 比较纯提示策略与 Repair 干预策略在隐私遵从率上的差异。未见大规模训练或预训练设置，更多是中小模型上的行为评测与推理时修正。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自首尔大学、IPAI 和 Max Planck Institute for Software Systems。团队背景偏 NLP 与可信/安全方向，不属于典型大模型基座预训练主线。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies how LLMs can regulate disclosure based not only on context but also on user-specific privacy preferences within the same context.
summary_en.importance: Its main value is to extend privacy control from contextual norms to personalized disclosure policies, and to provide P3Bench as a reusable evaluation asset. This is not a direct pretraining contribution, but it is relevant to agent-time behavior control, preference-conditioned generation, and inference-time intervention.
summary_en.technical_approach: The authors formalize personalized privacy by augmenting contextual privacy policies with user-specific disclosure rules, then build P3Bench to evaluate policy compliance. They also propose Repair, an inference-time attention-head intervention method that identifies and modifies privacy-relevant heads during decoding to reduce policy violations. This is an inference-time control method rather than a pretraining or post-training paradigm change.
summary_en.experiments: From the abstract, prompt-only policies fail badly on personalized privacy: Qwen2.5-7B and Gemma3-4B show average policy ignorance ratios of 51.25% and 74.28%, respectively. The experimental focus appears to be benchmark-based behavior evaluation and comparison between prompting and head intervention, not large-scale training.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors are from Seoul National University, IPAI, and the Max Planck Institute for Software Systems. The team appears more aligned with NLP and trustworthy AI than core foundation-model pretraining.

recommendation.zh: 和 pretrain 主线距离较远，但 P3Bench 可当 agent 隐私行为评测备查；方法本身偏推理时打补丁，不必细读正文。
recommendation.en: Far from core pretraining, but P3Bench is worth bookmarking for agent privacy evaluation; the method is mostly an inference-time patch, so a full read is unnecessary.

institutions: Max Planck Institute for Software Systems
Affiliation:Max Planck Institute for Software Systems

paper.title: StateSight: Benchmarking Latent Spatial-State Reconstruction in Vision-Language Models
paper.abstract: Vision-language models are increasingly used for multimodal question answering, yet their ability to reconstruct latent spatial structure from a single image remains difficult to isolate. Broad benchmarks often combine perception, optical character recognition, domain knowledge, linguistic priors, and reasoning in the same evaluation. We introduce StateSight, a procedurally generated benchmark for cube-net opposite-face reasoning, occluded cube-tower counting, and 4-neighbor connected-component

summary.core_problem: 如何隔离并准确评估视觉语言模型（VLMs）从单张图像中重建潜在空间结构的能力，而不受感知、OCR、领域知识等因素的干扰？
summary.importance: 提出了StateSight基准测试，专门用于评估VLM的潜在空间状态重建能力。通过程序化生成的数据集和精确匹配的评分机制，提供了一个干净的测试环境，揭示了当前顶级模型（如GPT-5.5和Claude Sonnet 5）在纯空间推理任务上与人类基线之间的显著差距。
summary.technical_approach: 构建了StateSight基准测试，包含三个任务：立方体网络对立面推理、遮挡立方体塔计数和4邻接连通分量计数。每个任务包含300个程序化生成的单图提示，具有确定性的oracle标签和精确匹配评分。这种设计排除了语言先验和领域知识的干扰，专注于纯粹的空间推理。
summary.experiments: 测试了OpenAI GPT-5.5 (gpt-5.5) 和 Claude Sonnet 5。GPT-5.5在三个任务上的准确率分别为59.3%、33.3%和28.3%；Claude Sonnet 5分别为53.3%、18.7%和7.3%。而30名人类参与者的基线准确率分别为80.8%、68.8%和64.3%，显著高于模型。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology。

summary_en.core_problem: How to isolate and accurately evaluate the ability of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to reconstruct latent spatial structures from a single image, without interference from perception, OCR, domain knowledge, etc.?
summary_en.importance: Introduces StateSight, a benchmark specifically designed to evaluate latent spatial state reconstruction in VLMs. Through procedurally generated datasets and exact-match scoring, it provides a clean testing environment and reveals a significant gap between current top models (e.g., GPT-5.5, Claude Sonnet 5) and human baselines on pure spatial reasoning tasks.
summary_en.technical_approach: Constructs the StateSight benchmark comprising three tasks: cube-net opposite-face reasoning, occluded cube-tower counting, and 4-neighbor connected-component counting. Each task contains 300 procedurally generated single-image prompts with deterministic oracle labels and exact-match scoring. This design eliminates interference from linguistic priors and domain knowledge, focusing purely on spatial reasoning.
summary_en.experiments: Evaluated OpenAI GPT-5.5 (gpt-5.5) and Claude Sonnet 5. GPT-5.5 achieved 59.3%, 33.3%, and 28.3% accuracy across the three tasks; Claude Sonnet 5 achieved 53.3%, 18.7%, and 7.3%. A 30-participant human baseline significantly outperformed both models with accuracies of 80.8%, 68.8%, and 64.3%.
summary_en.authors_note: Author is affiliated with Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology.

recommendation.zh: 一个针对VLM空间推理能力的合成评测集，揭示了当前模型在纯空间结构重建上的短板，可作为VLM能力分析的参考。
recommendation.en: A synthetic benchmark targeting VLM spatial reasoning capabilities, revealing shortcomings of current models in pure spatial structure reconstruction; useful as a reference for VLM capability analysis.

paper.title: FormalTCS: Benchmarking End-to-End Frontier Formal Theoretical Computer Science Research of Large Language Models
paper.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown growing potential for automated theoretical computer science (TCS) research, yet existing benchmarks remain far from realistic research settings. We introduce \ourbenchmark, an expert-validated benchmark for evaluating LLMs on frontier, end-to-end TCS research. \ourbenchmark contains $175$ instances drawn from papers accepted to STOC, FOCS, SODA, and COLT in 2025-2026, preserving paper-specific definitions, assumptions, and proof dependencies, with expert-

summary.core_problem: 把“LLM 做理论计算机科学研究”从零散能力测评（只测 autoformalization 或只测证明）推进到更接近真实研究流程的端到端评测：从论文语境里的自然语言核心主张出发，补齐 paper-specific 定义/假设/引理依赖，最终产出可在 Lean + Mathlib 版本下通过的形式化陈述与证明，并能定位流水线中最硬的瓶颈环节。
summary.importance: 对基座预训练的直接贡献不在训练配方，而在“评测信号与数据资产”：它把前沿研究内容（2025–2026 顶会论文）和端到端分解式诊断结合起来，给出一个更难被训练集污染、也更能暴露模型短板的评测面。对预训练研究的启发点主要有两类：第一，当前模型在“数学建模/形式化建模”（把自然语言主张变成合适的形式化定义与定理陈述）上明显弱于“在给定形式化目标下做证明搜索”，这会影响后续是否值得在 pretrain 阶段引入更强的结构化/形式化语料与目标；第二，端到端分解评测能把能力缺口具体化为可训练的子任务（定义生成、陈述对齐、依赖管理），比单一成功率更利于设计数据配比与中期训练（mid-train）策略。
summary.technical_approach: 数据与任务设计是核心。FormalTCS 由 175 个实例组成，每个实例来自一篇 2025–2026 年 STOC/FOCS/SODA/COLT 论文，保留论文特有的定义、假设与证明依赖结构；并由专家给出经验证的 Lean 4.32.2 + 对应 Mathlib 版本的形式化与证明。基准将“从自然语言到形式化证明”的过程拆成五个阶段逐段评测，从而能区分：是 autoformalization（定义/定理陈述构造）失败，还是证明阶段失败，还是依赖管理/分解策略失败。作者还在基准之上搭了一个端到端研究框架：让模型先提出主张，再尝试形式化并证明；结果显示模型更容易证明“自己提出的、自己表述的”主张，但这些主张经人工检查往往缺乏新意，指向所谓 research taste 的不足。与以往 TCS/数学基准相比，差异点在于：内容更新（前沿论文而非教材/Mathlib 现成定理）、语境更真实（paper-specific 设定与多层依赖）、评测更可诊断（分阶段而非单点能力）。
summary.experiments: 基准规模 175。形式化证明复杂度统计：平均 22.0 条 statements、29.6 个 proof nodes（用于表征形式化与证明的结构复杂度）。模型评测结论是端到端完成率仍低，且最尖锐瓶颈在 autoformalization：最佳模型在“将自然语言核心主张翻译为合适的形式化定义与定理陈述”上只有约 10%–11.5% 的水平（文中同时出现 10% 与 11.5% 的表述，需以主表/设定为准）。端到端研究框架实验显示：当主张由模型自拟时，模型往往能给出可通过的 Lean 证明，但人工检查认为多数主张新颖性有限，说明“提出值得证明的东西”比“把给定东西证明出来”更难。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读优先抓三块：1）任务分解与数据格式（看 FormalTCS 的五阶段定义、Table 2 的实例字段设计），理解它如何把端到端失败定位到具体环节；2）主结果表（Table 1）与分阶段结果：重点看 autoformalization 与后续证明阶段的差距，判断是否是“建模/表述”而非“推理/搜索”在卡住；3）数据构建与污染控制的描述：它决定了这个基准对 pretrain 研究是否能提供更干净的外部信号。预计阅读时间 30–45 分钟；若要用于训练/数据工作，再精读标注流程与质量控制细节。

summary_en.core_problem: Move evaluation of LLMs for theoretical CS from isolated skills (autoformalization-only or proof-only) to a realistic end-to-end pipeline: starting from a paper-context natural-language core claim, reconstruct paper-specific definitions/assumptions/lemma dependencies, and produce Lean statements and proofs that check under a fixed Lean/Mathlib version—while diagnosing which stage actually fails.
summary_en.importance: The main contribution is an evaluation asset rather than a training recipe. For pretraining researchers, the value is in (1) a harder, more contamination-resistant benchmark built from 2025–2026 top-conference papers, and (2) stage-wise signals that separate “mathematical/formal modeling” (turning NL into the right formal definitions and theorem statements) from “proving once formalized.” This distinction matters for deciding whether to invest in formal/structured corpora, intermediate training, or objective design targeting definition/statement construction and dependency management.
summary_en.technical_approach: FormalTCS contains 175 instances, each sourced from a distinct STOC/FOCS/SODA/COLT 2025–2026 paper. Each instance preserves paper-specific context (definitions, assumptions, proof dependencies) and includes expert-validated Lean 4.32.2 + Mathlib formalizations and proofs. The benchmark decomposes the end-to-end research workflow into five stages and evaluates models stage by stage, enabling bottleneck attribution (e.g., statement/definition synthesis vs proof search). On top of the benchmark, the authors build an end-to-end framework where the model proposes a claim and then formalizes/proves it; models tend to succeed more on self-proposed/self-phrased claims, but human inspection suggests limited novelty—highlighting a gap in “research taste” rather than pure proving ability. Compared to prior TCS/math benchmarks, the key differences are frontier content, realistic paper-conditioned setups, and diagnostic multi-stage evaluation.
summary_en.experiments: Dataset size is 175. The expert Lean proofs average 22.0 statements and 29.6 proof nodes, indicating nontrivial formalization/proof structure. Across evaluated frontier models, end-to-end success remains low; the sharpest bottleneck is autoformalization (mapping NL claims to appropriate formal definitions and theorem statements), where the best model reaches only about ~10%–11.5% depending on the reported slice/metric (the paper mentions both figures; the main result table should be treated as authoritative). In the end-to-end framework, models can often produce valid Lean proofs for claims they themselves generate, but those claims are frequently judged as low-novelty by humans.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim with focus on: (1) the five-stage pipeline definition and the instance schema (Table 2) to understand what is actually evaluated and how failures are localized; (2) the main results table(s) and per-stage breakdown to see how large the autoformalization gap is relative to proof generation; (3) the data construction and contamination-mitigation protocol, since that determines how trustworthy the benchmark is as an external signal for pretraining decisions. 30–45 minutes for a solid pass; deeper reading if you plan to use it for training data or mid-train targeting.

recommendation.zh: 这不是 pretrain 核心，但结论很实：别再把 formal reasoning 失败都归因于 proof search，先看 autoformalization；读结果表和任务拆分就够了。
recommendation.en: Not core pretraining, but the takeaway is solid: stop blaming formal-reasoning failures on proof search alone—autoformalization is the real bottleneck; the task decomposition and main result table are enough.

paper.title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
paper.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly require selective removal of harmful or sensitive knowledge, called unlearning, yet existing methods and benchmarks fail to evaluate this capability completely. Current approaches rely on disjoint forget and retain sets composed of independent facts, and measure success using simple and direct factual recall. This framing fails to capture a key requirement of unlearning, namely the ability to eliminate harmful behaviors while preserving benign and benefi

summary.core_problem: 评估 LLM 是否能在遗忘有害用途的同时，保留同一概念在良性场景中的正确使用能力。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是 unlearning benchmark。它指出现有 forget/retain set 与直接事实回忆评估过于粗糙，难以覆盖 dual-use concepts 这类现实安全需求。对预训练研究员的价值在于：模型删除、数据治理和安全后训练不能只用独立事实集合来测。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 context-sensitive unlearning 视角，并构造 ConceptGuard benchmark。核心单元是 dual-use concepts：同一概念既可能用于有害行为，也可能用于良性任务。评测目标是检查模型是否只移除危险应用，而不是把整个概念连同安全用法一起抹掉。
summary.experiments: 摘要未给出 benchmark 规模、覆盖概念数、评估模型或具体方法表现。可确认的评估维度包括 harmful behavior removal、benign knowledge retention，以及直接事实回忆之外的上下文敏感测试。
summary.authors_note: Pune Institute of Computer Technology；University of California, Irvine。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper evaluates whether an LLM can forget harmful uses of a concept while preserving correct benign uses of the same concept.
summary_en.importance: This is an unlearning benchmark contribution. It argues that existing forget/retain splits and direct factual recall metrics are too coarse for dual-use concepts. For pretraining researchers, the relevance is data governance and safety: deletion cannot be validated only with independent factual probes.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper introduces a context-sensitive view of unlearning and builds the ConceptGuard benchmark. The key unit is a dual-use concept that can appear in both harmful and benign contexts. The benchmark tests whether unlearning removes unsafe applications without erasing the concept wholesale.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract does not provide benchmark size, number of concepts, evaluated models, or quantitative results. The intended evaluation covers harmful behavior removal, benign knowledge retention, and context-sensitive probes beyond direct factual recall.
summary_en.authors_note: Pune Institute of Computer Technology; University of California, Irvine.

recommendation.zh: 读 benchmark schema 就够；它提醒 unlearning eval 不能再用独立事实集糊弄，但结果需看数据覆盖面。
recommendation.en: Read the benchmark schema; it usefully rejects disjoint-fact unlearning evals, but the value depends on concept coverage.

paper.title: MemTrapBench: Benchmarking Cognitive Traps in LLM Memory Use
paper.abstract: Memory has become a key component of large language models, enabling them to retain information and learn from long-term interactions. However, existing memory benchmarks mainly evaluate whether information is correctly extracted, stored, and retrieved, while largely overlooking how retrieved memories reshape model reasoning and affect performance on the current task. We identify memory-induced cognitive traps: even faithfully recorded and semantically relevant memories can distort model reasoni

summary.core_problem: 现有的 LLM 记忆评估基准忽略了检索到的记忆如何扭曲模型推理并降低当前任务性能（即“认知陷阱”），如何系统地评估这一问题？
summary.importance: 首次系统性地定义并评估了 LLM 记忆机制中的“认知陷阱”（推理固化和信念扭曲），揭示了现有记忆增强方法的重大缺陷。
summary.technical_approach: 构建了 MemTrapBench 基准，涵盖推理固化（Reasoning Fixation）和信念扭曲（Belief Distortion）两种认知陷阱。在两个模型家族和五种代表性记忆框架上进行评估。
summary.experiments: 实验表明，所有评估的记忆策略在 MemTrapBench 上的表现均低于无记忆设置，最强的方法性能下降也超过 10%。
summary.authors_note: 浙江大学、NUS、腾讯等机构合作，Ningyu Zhang 团队工作。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing LLM memory benchmarks overlook how retrieved memories distort model reasoning and degrade current task performance ('cognitive traps'). How to systematically evaluate this?
summary_en.importance: Systematically defines and evaluates 'cognitive traps' (Reasoning Fixation and Belief Distortion) in LLM memory mechanisms for the first time, revealing significant flaws in existing memory-augmented methods.
summary_en.technical_approach: Constructs MemTrapBench, covering two cognitive traps: Reasoning Fixation and Belief Distortion. Evaluates across two model families and five representative memory frameworks.
summary_en.experiments: Experiments show all evaluated memory strategies underperform the no-memory setting on MemTrapBench, with even the strongest methods suffering >10% performance drops.
summary_en.authors_note: Collaboration between Zhejiang University, NUS, Tencent, etc. Work from Ningyu Zhang's team.

recommendation.zh: 揭示了 RAG/Memory 机制的负面效应（记忆反而干扰当前推理），对长上下文和 RAG 相关的后训练/评测有警示作用，值得关注其 failure case 分析。
recommendation.en: Reveals the negative effects of RAG/Memory mechanisms (memories interfering with current reasoning), serving as a warning for long-context and RAG-related post-training/eval. Worth noting its failure case analysis.

paper.title: DeltaML-Bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Real-World Research Repositories
paper.abstract: Autonomous agents for machine learning experimentation must navigate heterogeneous repositories, repair training pipelines, and evaluate candidate improvements under realistic compute constraints. Existing benchmarks only partially capture these conditions. We introduce DeltaML-Bench, a benchmark comprising 48 tasks sourced from research papers that require agents to improve published baselines within imperfect, open-source repositories. We evaluate GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4 with a standard Modu
